examples.title: A case table shares one test body

limitations: The rule compares substantial sibling tests within one suite and skips inline snapshots and materially different comments. Short no-substitution strings and const-asserted literals share the existing input normalization; assertion values, property names, multiline strings and long strings retain their contracts.
Matching normalized body shapes do not prove runtime equivalence or independent setup; parameterization is a manual review, not an automatic deletion.
rules.rationale: Copy-pasted test bodies hide the cases that differ and allow equivalent assertions to drift independently.
rules.remediation: Consider a case table with one named test or subtest per case; preserve setup lifetime, test modifiers, and each case's assertions rather than deleting coverage.
rules.summary: Disallow substantial sibling tests with the same body shape; express their differing inputs as a parameterized case table.

examples.title: Imports precede module declarations

limitations: The rule skips tests and generated files, treats re-exports as neutral, and does not order body declarations. Only misplaced import type declarations in comment-free files are automatically moved; runtime imports and directive activation remain manual.
rules.rationale: Interleaved imports obscure module dependencies, while a displaced `use server` string is not an active directive.
rules.remediation: Move `use server` to the first statement when present, then place imports before declarations and executable statements.
rules.summary: Require imports before body statements and require `use server` to be the first statement.

/**
 * This file is the seam between the draft and backend models.
 * Everything above it uses the local application representation.
 * Everything below it uses a separately mirrored wire representation.
 * Field names use the API shape while the draft uses another shape.
 * This module translates every field between those representations.
 * The backend models changed several times during early development.
 * Each historical change required another edit in this adapter file.
 * The write half previously assembled several resources in one payload.
 * It now saves those resources separately through their own routes.
 * Clear contract types and generated clients should express this boundary.
 */
import type { Draft } from './draft';

examples.title: Adapter paragraph narrates application behavior
Concrete wire compatibility constraint remains local

limitations: Only an unattached file-header JSDoc block with at least ten non-empty lines and 65 words that narrates file layout or change history is inspected.
Generated files, tests, scripts, stories, licenses, typed API documentation, and comments attached to declarations are excluded.

Safe fixes blank only interior plus-only decoration when removing those non-prose lines clears the existing volume finding. All prose bytes, comment markers and line endings remain; directives, licenses, examples, literal-output/prompt/credential contexts, Markdown structure and ambiguous comments remain for review.
rules.rationale: Narrative implementation paragraphs compete with the code and can drift independently from behavior.
rules.remediation: Delete narration and clarify names, types, or structure; retain only durable constraints and external contracts.
rules.summary: Flag long standalone implementation commentary that should be expressed by code.

examples.title: Do not prove Terraform behavior with a regex

limitations: The rule follows stable lexical bindings and static source paths, including named node:path/path join and resolve imports with a complete trailing static path. Reassigned bindings, dynamic trailing paths, namespace or unknown path wrappers, iterator pipelines, and interprocedural flows remain unreported.

Known fixture, golden, snapshot, and generated source paths remain unreported after dot-segment normalization, as do contained static paths beneath stable native temporary directories and literal mutation nonidentity guards comparing the same read.
When raw representation is genuinely the contract, use an exact line suppression explaining that contract.
rules.rationale: Substring and regex checks can pass on comments, formatting, or unreachable Terraform configuration while clients fail silently.
rules.remediation: Reuse adequate existing validation; otherwise assert a distinct rendered-plan, provider-state, or runtime contract. Preserve deliberate representation contracts with an exact justified suppression.
rules.summary: Disallow raw IaC source text as a test oracle; inspect a rendered plan, provider state, or runtime behavior.

examples.title: Keep helpers behind the runtime boundary

files.source: interface Store { load(): void } class DiskStore implements Store { load() { this.read(); } read() {} }

examples.title: Do not grow an undeclared public surface

limitations: Automatic conversion is limited to unused private module/block classes without heritage, decorators, computed members, static execution, or eval; referenced classes remain manual.
Only concrete classes with an explicit `implements` clause are checked; constructors, static members, protected extension hooks, and overrides are excluded.
Inherited interface members are resolved by TypeScript. Computed names are excluded because their contract identity is not stable syntax.
The rule abstains for the whole class when TypeScript cannot resolve any implemented contract, avoiding false positives for missing or unavailable package declarations.
Referenced classes remain report-only because a public member can have consumers in another source file; the developer must choose whether to extend the interface or privatize it.
TypeScript-private members are left to prefer-ecmascript-private-members so one concern produces one diagnostic.
rules.rationale: An implementing class should expose exactly its declared interface while keeping implementation helpers runtime-private.
rules.remediation: Add the method to the interface when it is public API, or make it `#private` and remove external or inherited access.
rules.summary: Require methods outside an implemented interface contract to use ECMAScript private names.

examples.title: Do not repeat the complete child annotation

files.source: import { z } from "zod"; const KeySchema: z.ZodEnum<{ a: "a"; b: "b" }> = z.enum(["a", "b"]); export const RecordSchema: z.ZodRecord<typeof KeySchema, z.ZodString> = z.record(KeySchema, z.string());

examples.title: Reference the named child contract

limitations: Only direct module-level const z.record calls with two arguments, a ZodRecord annotation, and an earlier local const child with a complete explicit Zod type are inspected.
The entire generic child annotation must match token for token; input/output, defaults, transforms, readonly modifiers and brands are never compared by output shape alone.

Bare leaf types, broad ZodType constraints, type queries, imported or unqualified type references, annotation cycles, comments on the repeated argument, mutable bindings and generated files are excluded.

Import aliases and namespace imports resolve through scope bindings. Independent public contract pins can use one shared named type alias or an exact reasoned suppression; runtime validation and outer annotations are preserved.
rules.rationale: Repeating a child schema's generic contract creates a second maintained declaration even though the record already uses that child at runtime.
rules.remediation: Replace only the matching record type argument with `typeof ChildSchema`, or share one explicit named schema type alias between child and record to retain an independently named public contract. Keep the outer annotation required by isolatedDeclarations and every runtime schema operation.
rules.summary: Reference a named Zod record child's complete schema type instead of repeating its explicit annotation.

files.source: test.each(['valid', 'invalid'])('decodes %s', (input) => { try { decode(input); } catch (error) { throw error; } expect(result()).toBe('ok'); });

examples.title: Each table case propagates its failure

limitations: Only bare returns owned by an inline supported test callback and followed lexically by a framework assertion are reported, including each/for tables and runIf/skipIf builders. Custom builders and indirect callback references are excluded. A runner skip suppresses the finding only when it is an unconditional earlier statement in the return's block. Vitest imports and unshadowed runner globals support TestContext.skip on the first ordinary-test parameter or second for-table parameter, including a directly destructured skip alias; each-table data arguments, reassigned bindings, overwritten skip methods and dynamic skip conditions are excluded.
rules.rationale: An unasserted catch return can swallow a failure and skip later assertions; the complete test result also depends on other assertions and hooks.
rules.remediation: Rethrow the error, assert on it, or use the runner's explicit skip mechanism when the capability is optional.
rules.summary: Disallow a bare return from a test catch block when it skips a later assertion.

examples.title: Use the generated client's application-facing property names

limitations: Only adapter/adapters files and receivers explicitly annotated with a scope-resolved type imported from an API/client/SDK/contract/generated module are checked. Unrelated imports, local type shadows, reassigned receivers and inferred receiver types are excluded.
Only object properties that directly translate the same identifier between snake_case and lowerCamelCase are reported.
Quoted/computed protocol keys, generated/vendor code, tests, fixtures, and indirect conversions are intentionally excluded.
rules.rationale: Duplicating wire-name translation can drift from an API client contract. When the SDK owns application-facing names, centralizing conversion avoids maintaining another mirror by hand.
rules.remediation: Move wire-name ownership and case conversion into the generated SDK/model layer; keep application adapters on the generated typed surface.
rules.summary: Review direct snake_case/camelCase mirror mappings on explicitly API-typed adapter values.

files.source: function label(enabled: boolean) { if (enabled) { return "Enabled"; } else { return "Disabled"; } }

examples.title: Boolean data may select a pure value

files.source: const book = (premium: boolean) => premium ? premiumBook() : regularBook();

examples.title: Name the selected operation explicitly

limitations: Requires type information. Checks an owned single-statement if/else, returned conditional or conditional expression statement, and expression-bodied arrow conditionals. Only a direct broad-boolean parameter or its negation is considered; optional, nullable, literal-only, generic, destructured and indirect predicate conditions are excluded.

Preserves setters, pure mappings, selected pure data passed to one stable lexical operation or assigned to one simple target, independently authored callable and inherited member contracts, inline callbacks, and statically proven named callback references. Independent helpers remain checked in JSX files; callback identity is established from references rather than handler names.

The block-body detector preserves the existing literal on[A-Z] object-property exemption; the concise-arrow extension does not infer a callback contract from that name. Multi-statement bodies, short-circuit guards, local parameter aliases and arbitrary control flow are not inferred. Noncomputed property reads count as data without proving getter effects; computed reads remain outside that exemption, including literal keys. Side-effect detection does not prove whether a called function is pure, and a warning requires manual design review. Generated files are excluded; tests remain checked.

Automatic fixes only reuse two already authored private zero-argument ordinary operations returning primitive string literals. A complete comment-free four-declaration module must contain those operations, one private const broad-boolean arrow selecting their direct calls, and one exported zero-argument ordinary function with an explicit string-array return that calls the selector exclusively with literal true and false. Calls are routed to the existing named operations and the exclusively used selector declaration is removed. All other APIs, callbacks, dynamic arguments, contracts and operation bodies remain manual.
rules.rationale: A positional boolean hides which operation a caller requests. Splitting independent actions can make that intent explicit, while boolean data, pure mappings and externally required callback or method contracts remain valid.
rules.remediation: Consider separate named operations or an explicit domain mode. Review the public API and its callers manually; preserve required callback, setter and inherited contracts instead of wrapping them solely to silence the warning.
rules.summary: Prefer intention-revealing operations over a boolean parameter selecting between actions.

examples.title: Preserve the explicit contract

limitations: Requires TypeScript type information and an implemented function with an explicit return annotation. Checks unknown, object, and unknown-valued index-only dictionaries, including aliases and Promise results.

Unparsed unknown/any values, generics, empty object literals, and declaration-only signatures are excluded. Parameter contracts are not inferred from names. Intentional opaque return boundaries require an explained local suppression. Automatic fixes remove the annotation only from an unused private function declaration in a module or block; referenced and public contracts remain manual.
rules.rationale: An unknown, object, or unknown-valued dictionary return hides fields that the implementation already knows.
rules.remediation: Return the existing domain type or retain the inferred return contract. Keep unknown at unparsed input boundaries.
rules.summary: Report explicit broad return annotations that erase a known return value.

examples.title: An effect starts a data request

limitations: The rule recognizes common fetch clients syntactically and exempts analytics endpoints and non-GET `fetch` calls.
rules.rationale: Effect-driven reads begin after rendering and can create request waterfalls, duplicate fetches, and loading-state layout shifts.
rules.remediation: Fetch in a React Server Component or Server Action, or use a client cache such as SWR or React Query.
rules.summary: Disallow direct data fetching inside `useEffect` or `useLayoutEffect`.

examples.title: A comment repeats the statement below

limitations: The rule skips generated files and conservatively preserves prose, issue references, licenses, examples, and tool directives. Automatic fixes remove only whole-line punctuation-only banners while preserving line endings; narrated prose, unfinished work and contextual labels remain manual.
rules.rationale: Decorative, narrated, or dead-code comments obscure the constraints and rationale that comments should preserve.
rules.remediation: Delete dead code and narration; express boundaries with named code and retain only comments that explain constraints or intent.
rules.summary: Flag commented-out code, section-banner comments, and leading file-header comment preambles.

examples.title: Use the direct contract

files.source:
declare const includePage: boolean;
const query = { limit: 20, ...(includePage ? { page: 1 } : {}) };

examples.title: Preserve the explicit contract

limitations: Reports ternary expressions with an empty object branch directly spread into an object literal. Does not report array or argument spreads, logical spreads, or two nonempty alternatives.

This is an explicit readability policy. Comment-free conditionals with exactly one nonempty object-literal branch are automatically rewritten as logical spreads, preserving omission, evaluation order and property ownership. Other expression branches require manual review.
rules.rationale: An empty-object conditional spread hides whether a property is omitted, which differs from assigning undefined.
rules.remediation: Construct the object explicitly and add the conditional fields only when the original condition holds, preserving evaluation order and ownership.
rules.summary: Build conditional properties explicitly instead of spreading an empty-object branch.

examples.title: Match each literal input with its result
Do not swap domain variants behind overloads

limitations: Automatic fixes align only an unused private complete same-file overload group with its existing literal implementation results. Binding aliases, exports, merges, eval, declaration files, comments, nonliteral result syntax and observed callers preserve manual ownership; runtime checks and returned values never change.

Requires type information and a top-level non-generic, synchronous function with two to 32 unique, single-required-parameter overloads. Each public input must be a directly authored string, finite number, boolean or null literal. Broad, duplicate, aliased, optional, rest and multi-parameter inputs are excluded.

The implementation must have one required identifier parameter and only return a strict literal equality/inequality conditional. Both branches must be primitive literals or flat objects containing only primitive literal property assignments. Calls, computed keys, getters, spreads, duplicate keys and __proto__ are excluded.

Reports only a concrete returned literal incompatible with its primitive contract or an explicit returned property incompatible with the corresponding primitive property contract. Missing properties, arbitrary structural incompatibility, brands, enums, opaque types, effects and general control flow are outside this proof.

Compiler-invalid implementation input/output envelopes, generated files, ambient declarations, methods and callbacks are excluded. Null input overloads require strictNullChecks: under loose null checking an earlier overload can mask their advertised result. No automatic rewrite changes a public overload or its runtime behavior.
rules.rationale: TypeScript checks an overload implementation against an overall envelope, without proving each input/result relationship. A function can compile while returning the opposite domain variant for every advertised literal input.
rules.remediation: Return the variant promised for each input. Prefer a checked case map or separate variant-specific operations when that makes the relationship explicit; retain overloads required by public APIs.
rules.summary: Preserve the input/result relationship promised by literal overloads.

examples.title: Array membership alone does not prove text elements

examples.title: Establish the element domain at the boundary

examples.title: An empty target has no successful member

files.source: function nonPrimitive(value: unknown): value is object { return typeof value === "object"; }

examples.title: A typeof-object check also accepts null

files.source: function ready(value: unknown): value is "ready" { return typeof value === "string"; }

examples.title: A string check admits other strings

limitations: Automatic fixes replace the unsound predicate with boolean only for an unused private function declaration without overloads, exports, eval, comments in the predicate, or declaration-file ownership. Runtime checks are preserved; observed callable contracts remain manual.

Requires type information, an explicit predicate over a directly named parameter and a single returned positive typeof equality for the same scope-resolved parameter. Both strict and loose equality and reversed operands are supported.

Recognizes broad primitive targets, finite primitive literal/nullish unions and never, with unknown or fully classified primitive/nullish inputs. Closed input domains are checked against the actual target, including finite numeric enum members. Mixed broad-and-literal, branded, unique-symbol, structural, generic, asserted, declaration-only and multi-statement validators are excluded rather than guessed.

For the intrinsic object target, typeof-object also admits null only when the declared input admits null and strictNullChecks is enabled. This narrow check does not infer structural property validation or classify other object/function relationships. Overloaded implementations, contextually typed callbacks and methods with class heritage or contextual object contracts retain their separate callable domain.

Compiler-invalid predicate target/input relations and typeof comparisons impossible for the input remain with existing compiler and unnecessary-condition controls. This rule does not validate arbitrary predicates or runtime refinements. Generated files are excluded; tests remain checked.

A sole native Array.isArray call on unknown cannot establish a plain primitive-element array target. Standard-library call signatures and an unshadowed Array binding are required. Element validators, any/unknown elements, tuples, enums, branded or opaque elements and independent callable contracts abstain. Visible Array or host-global aliases, mutation, escapes, extracted methods, any value constructor or unresolved computed-property access and unrelated Array namespace uses disable this proof: structural receiver types cannot establish runtime constructor identity. Native Reflect value uses and Object prototype/descriptor reflection or namespace aliases also withdraw authority. Indirect opaque runtime replacements are not inferred.
rules.rationale: TypeScript trusts an explicit type predicate without verifying its implementation. A contradictory check can admit the wrong primitive, overclaim a closed literal or empty domain, accept null as a non-null object, or remove valid alternatives from the false branch.
rules.remediation: Match the predicate to every value the check accepts and rejects. Check literal membership for a closed domain and exclude null when promising a non-null object. Use a boolean return for an intentional value filter; preserve required public and callback contracts.
rules.summary: Keep explicit type predicates consistent with their primitive or native array membership check.

files.source: import cors from 'cors'; cors({ origin: 'https://app.example.com', credentials: true });

examples.title: Use a trusted origin for credentialed callers

files.source: import cors from 'cors'; cors({ origin: '*', credentials: true });

examples.title: Review a wildcard that blocks access to credentialed responses

limitations: Options require a stable official cors default import or hono/cors named or namespace import, one literal object argument, literal origin '*', and credentials true. No-substitution templates and erased TypeScript literal wrappers preserve these values. Custom bindings, callbacks, arrays, conditional origins and dynamic options are excluded.

Literal header maps use effective case-sensitive JavaScript property writes followed by native Headers combination of differently-cased header names. Unknown values/spreads/computed keys, accessors and non-null prototypes lose proof; literals used only inside object spreads are not reported independently.

Manual set/setHeader/delete/removeHeader calls (including static computed method names) use direct identifier receivers and literal arguments in straight-line program or function bodies. Control-flow bodies, member receivers, aliases and unknown operations are excluded. Append requires a proven empty native Headers constructor or a preceding known write/removal.

The rule reviews a local configuration contract, not actual request credentials or a data disclosure. Runtime patches, custom header method implementations, interprocedural mutation and later consumers are not resolved. No autofix.
rules.rationale: Browsers do not expose credentialed cross-origin responses when Access-Control-Allow-Origin is '*'. Credentialless requests can still use a wildcard even when Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is emitted, so review the intended caller contract.
rules.remediation: Use a trusted explicit origin for credentialed callers, or omit the credentials opt-in for a credentialless wildcard endpoint.
rules.summary: Review wildcard CORS origins combined with an explicit credentials opt-in.

files.source: localStorage.setItem("sidebar-collapsed", "true");

examples.title: Store a non-credential preference in localStorage
Do not store an access token in localStorage

limitations: Only static keys and cookie names whose words name an access credential (token, secret, password, jwt, credential, api key) are checked.
Storage wrappers, computed keys and values stored under neutral names are not followed.
rules.rationale: localStorage, sessionStorage and cookies written through document.cookie are readable by any script on the origin, so one injected script can copy the credential and replay it elsewhere.
rules.remediation: Keep the credential on the server and send it as an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookie set by a server response, or hold a short-lived token in memory only.
rules.summary: Do not write credential-named values to browser storage or script-readable cookies.

files.source: export default { images: { dangerouslyAllowSVG: false } };

examples.title: Keep active SVG delivery disabled

files.source: export default { images: { dangerouslyAllowSVG: true } };

examples.title: Do not enable active SVG delivery

limitations: Automatic boolean changes are withheld when the module contains explicit TypeScript or JSDoc contracts; those contracts can constrain an aliased property to literal true. Plain objects and as const inference remain fixable.

Automatic fixes disable the unsafe SVG opt-in; already hardened configurations are preserved. Only literal effective properties of a directly exported object, unescaped const alias, or isolated module.exports object are analyzed. Wrappers, factories, spreads, dynamic computed keys, dynamic policies and mutations are not inferred.
rules.rationale: SVG files can contain scripts and other active content; enabling dangerouslyAllowSVG makes the image optimizer serve that content from the application origin.
rules.remediation: Keep dangerouslyAllowSVG disabled. If SVG optimization is required, retain attachment disposition and set the image Content-Security-Policy to `script-src 'none'; sandbox;`.
rules.summary: Next.js image configuration enables SVG rendering without the required response hardening

examples.title: Do not restate every enum member

files.source: enum Status { Pending = 'pending', Finished = 'finished', Failed = 'failed' }

examples.title: Let clear member names stand alone

limitations: Automatic fixes remove only an exact multiword member-name comment on its own line and retain all physical line endings; threshold-based or novel prose remains manual.
Only enum and class bodies meeting the configured comment-count and restatement-ratio thresholds are reported.

maxNovelWords.description: Most content words a comment may add beyond its member's own source and still count as a restatement.

minCommentedMembers.description: Fewest commented members that can count as a wall.

minCommentedRatio.description: Least share of the members that must be commented; below it the comments are group labels.

minRestatedRatio.description: Least share of the member comments that must be restatements.

rules.rationale: A dense block of repetitive member comments obscures the few comments that add information and drifts with renamed members.
rules.remediation: Delete comments that restate member names and retain comments that explain constraints, lifecycle, or behavior.
rules.summary: Flag an enum body or class body whose member comments mostly re-spell the members' own names.

files.source: class Client { readonly request = (input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => fetch(input, init); }

examples.title: Store a receiver-safe forwarding wrapper

files.source: class Client { readonly request = fetch; }

examples.title: Do not store raw ambient fetch as an object method

limitations: The rule follows stable local variables and defaulted parameters from an unshadowed ambient fetch or globalThis/self/window fetch into direct class, object, or member storage.

Bare local aliases, callback arguments, returns, direct calls, compatible global or undefined bind/call/apply receivers, tests, scripts, generated files, and locally defined fetch implementations are excluded.
Interprocedural aliases, mutable aliases, collection storage, and host identity remain manual review boundaries.

Automatic edits only bind a direct canonical ambient fetch to unshadowed undefined in a sole exported zero-argument ordinary function containing a private one-property object and its sole returned literal data-URL request. The callable and object never escape. Web IDL operations use the function realm's global object for an undefined receiver. Imports, comments, wrappers, other statements, options, shadows and identity observations remain manual; this repairs receiver behavior rather than preserving a host IllegalInvocation failure.
rules.rationale: Calling a raw ambient fetch through a class or object property supplies that object as `this`; receiver-sensitive hosts can reject that invocation only after deployment.
rules.remediation: Store a forwarding wrapper such as `(input, init) => fetch(input, init)`, or bind the callable to a compatible global or undefined receiver before storing it.
rules.summary: Keep the ambient global fetch receiver-safe when storing or explicitly rebinding it.

files.source: import { useRouter } from "next/navigation"; const router = useRouter(); const refresh = () => router.refresh(); window.addEventListener("focus", refresh); document.addEventListener("visibilitychange", refresh);

examples.title: Do not duplicate a route refresh

files.source: import { useRouter } from "next/navigation"; const router = useRouter(); const refresh = () => router.refresh(); window.addEventListener("focus", refresh);

examples.title: Listen to one lifecycle signal

limitations: Only active direct window focus and document visibilitychange statements in the same block whose shared identifier callback directly calls refresh on a next/navigation useRouter binding are inspected; matching direct removals are honored, and generated and test files are excluded.
rules.rationale: A browser tab activation can emit both lifecycle signals and invoke the same route-wide refresh twice.
rules.remediation: Choose one lifecycle signal or route both signals through an explicitly debounced refresh policy.
rules.summary: Do not register one Next.js route-refresh callback for both focus and visibilitychange.

examples.title: Distinct inputs have independent rows

examples.title: Vitest for tables preserve distinct boundaries

rules.rationale: Exception details can contain database, provider, filesystem or credential information that belongs in server-side diagnostics rather than a client response.

limitations: The created JSX value must initialize a private actual const binding. Only unused values or same-function-scope fixed reads of already proven consumed scalar props are supported. Enclosing invocations must have no runtime argument or arguments-object dependency, async/generator suspension, or unproved captured values. Unused simple arguments and captured scalar data reuse the existing provenance proof; destructured/default/rest arguments remain unsupported. Exported, returned, aliased, captured, aggregated or forwarded elements, whole-props access, opaque calls, type observations and writes abstain. A caller can mutate production React props after creation even when development React freezes them; initial source provenance alone is insufficient. This restriction intentionally excludes ordinary exported and rendered elements until their consumers can be proved.

The rule abstains when the receiving or calling project runtime dependency context contains a known ordinary Object-prototype effect or exposure, native eval/Function capabilities, any explicit call, constructor or tagged-template invocation, for-of or for-in iteration, an ambient or uninitialized value declaration or a declaration-file value read, an unresolved lexical value (including a shorthand or a type-only name used as a value), an erased const-enum value without a runtime binding proof, an opaque globalThis member, an implicit this/super/module-metadata capability, an extracted reflective method, or a member-write target not proven to be a fresh unrelated object/array literal. Callable and class metadata writes, including through erased const aliases, abstain: runtime metadata can observe omitted fields even when it is absent from the native JSX contract. Native shorthand value symbols preserve global capability identity instead of trusting a newly created property symbol. Property keys, control-flow labels, intrinsic JSX names and erased type positions do not evaluate lexical values; their missing symbols or Any types do not alone veto a finding. Native ESM imports/re-exports and literal dynamic imports are followed in both dependency and known-importer directions, including other dependencies of those importers and resolved bare path aliases; whole-clause import type/export type forms are skipped. Import-equals and other loader forms are unsupported. Per-specifier type imports/exports retain their runtime edges when native verbatimModuleSyntax emit keeps an empty import/export. Unresolved runtime imports and declaration-only or external-library runtime imports abstain. Literal dynamic imports retain their module-resolution proof. External code outside the analyzed project context and standard library implementations remain opaque; standard ordinary Object built-ins are assumed. Connected runtime dependency contexts beyond 128 files or const-alias proofs beyond 64 steps abstain. Safe reflective code may therefore be excluded. This finite known-effect exclusion does not prove universal prototype pristineness.

Requires parser-owned TypeScript information, a strict module implementation, a complete Object base, a self-closing identifier tag with one plain object-literal spread and no other attributes, and one nongeneric implemented synchronous arrow receiver with a resolved finite props surface. Sibling attributes or children could override the proven source values. Unknown, opaque, union, overloaded, generic, intrinsic and class receivers are excluded.

Mapped types, index signatures, namespace/value-derived contracts, unresolved inherited or computed receiver keys, nonliteral computed source keys, nested spreads, accessors and explicit __proto__ keys are excluded. Source type properties alone do not prove enumerable own runtime keys. key, ref, React's __self/__source development metadata and TypeScript's hyphenated JSX attribute names are preserved.

Native member lookup includes inherited, optional, readonly and implicit Object capabilities. The rule reports runtime keys outside the contract; it does not infer unused component fields, demand smaller public APIs, or erase producer type information.

Runtime alias references require active native checking of each reached local implementation, with no located syntax or semantic errors. Checking disabled by noCheck or native-shaped TypeScript suppression directives is unavailable evidence. JavaScript, declaration/default/external-library files, foreign SourceFile objects and project-reference programs are unsupported for this alias proof. Importer indexing does not request full semantic checks; reached files reuse the parser-owned Program's diagnostic caches. Unlocated/global diagnostics are not treated as a clean project or as proof of runtime binding presence. Namespace value reads, including merged and const-enum-only namespace carriers, abstain because a ValueModule symbol can survive erased runtime output without a native error. Pure type namespaces and nonambient namespace declaration names remain non-value positions; explicit ambient namespace declarations retain their existing exclusion. A non-import-alias value declared in another source also abstains: inclusion in the type Program does not establish that a script/global implementation executes or that an ambient binding is supplied as a data property. Native standard global identities retain their existing assumptions.

Requires a single returned view made from intrinsic JSX, literals and scalar parameter reads/operators. JSX objects may be rendered as children or returned branches, but cannot be operands of scalar coercions or intrinsic attribute values. Free runtime values, helper calls, callbacks, object-valued consumed fields, custom tags, rest/spread, reflection and dynamic access prevent a finding; indirect element.props aliases cannot be inferred safe. Every inspected or destructured root field must be an own source-literal key; an omitted field could invoke an inherited getter. Bound/read source values require concrete scalar types without undefined, Any or unknown and runtime primitive provenance: literals, operators/templates with proven primitive operands, proven conditional tests and branches, or local immutable const initializers after removing assertions. Direct own fields of a same-file const object literal are supported only when every object reference is a fixed field value in a direct object initializer, inline JSX spread, JSX expression or local binding, with no direct eval. Mutation, accessors, method receivers, dynamic keys, reflection, whole-object aliases and exports abstain. Opaque calls, getters, parameters, mutable bindings and imported source values abstain even when annotated as scalars. Unproven source paths beyond 64 expressions abstain as an analysis resource limit. Only successful value proofs are memoized. An alias or assertion cannot turn an object into a primitive; undefined can activate runtime defaults. Opaque HOC and declaration-file signatures remain unsupported.

The actual tag must resolve through immutable identifier aliases to a const arrow initializer. Constructible ordinary functions, mutable, member, proxy, call-produced and asserted receiver values are excluded even when their callable type resembles a known implementation; inherited runtime metadata can change ordinary function dispatch. Exactly one actual parameter and no explicit this parameter are supported.

Reached files containing actual JSX additionally require their compiler-owned implicit runtime import and the native module symbol's declaration owners. Known non-declaration runtime implementations are unsupported even when their bodies have no ordinary Object effects: a custom factory can reinterpret forwarded fields. External declaration files and owned top-level ambient module declarations in declaration files retain the explicit standard-React library assumption; those declarations do not prove the actual runtime JavaScript identity. Missing or ambiguous internal import metadata, missing native symbols, foreign owners and local nonambient declaration-module sources abstain. Non-JSX dependencies do not acquire a runtime edge merely because the compiler records an unused synthetic JSX import. Runtime rebinding outside the compiler-visible module context remains opaque, not validated by this proof.

Requires target ES2015 or newer, explicit native ES-module output and the standard React automatic JSX runtime (react-jsx or react-jsxdev). Downlevel arrows become constructible functions; CommonJS exports remain mutable. Preserve/classic JSX, custom factories, namespaces, import sources and per-file JSX directives are unsupported. Imported library implementations and cross-project source redirects are opaque; relative imports within this program remain supported.
rules.rationale: A spread can forward unrelated data even when structural typing accepts the larger object. Changing its annotation does not remove runtime fields.
rules.remediation: Forward the declared fields explicitly or review the receiving contract. A projection changes object identity and allocations; this rule never constructs one automatically.
rules.summary: Report statically known fields spread outside a resolved component props contract.

examples.title: Seven nested decisions exceed the error limit

limitations: Sarj metric, not exact Sonar compatibility: functions and callbacks are independent; calls, recursion, types, parameter defaults, decorators, and class initializers are not scored.
Conditions, loops, catch clauses, switch statements, and conditional expressions add one plus nesting. Else-if and else add one; their bodies add nesting. Each run of like boolean operators adds one.
Nullish coalescing and optional chaining are free. Labeled break/continue add one. Try, finally, return, unlabeled jumps, and await add no points themselves.
Generated code is excluded; authored tests, React components, and all function lengths are checked. The threshold is a shared policy constant, not a correctness boundary.
rules.rationale: Nested control flow increases the context a reader must retain while following a function.
rules.remediation: Scores up to 20 pass; 21 or more are errors. Examples are fictional; domain types are omitted. Refactor one function at a time, starting with its largest contributors. First simplify control flow and reduce nesting within the function. Extract a helper only when it clarifies a cohesive responsibility or enables meaningful reuse; do not split code solely to lower the score. Use lookup tables only for equivalent pure dispatch. Preserve APIs, side effects, evaluation order, and exception behavior. Run relevant tests before and after; remeasure the original and extracted functions. Do not hide branches in dense expressions or add indirection just to lower a score.
rules.summary: Report an error for function bodies with cognitive complexity above 20.

rules.rationale: A broad `try` block obscures which operation failed and encourages one catch clause to recover from unrelated errors.
rules.remediation: Keep only the operations that share one recovery policy inside the `try` block and move other work outside it.

Automatic fixes use Reflect.has only for a sole exported ordinary function with an explicit boolean return annotation and a literal-string property check on its single direct collection parameter, with no comments, other statements, source callouts or shadowed Reflect. rules.rationale: The `in` operator checks properties on the collection object and its prototype, while `.has()` checks stored entries. The similar spelling can silently test the wrong namespace.

limitations: Requires type information and an explicitly annotated local const initialized with a plain own-data object literal. Only non-exported, stable bindings without escapes or nested captures qualify. Deletes and descriptors that can lock writability or configurability invalidate storage provenance. The closed non-union contract must declare the initialized data property; parameters, opaque constructors/factories, accessor, method, indexed, callable and unresolved generic targets are excluded.

Inspects native Object.assign with one plain object-literal source, native Reflect.set with a static string key and no separate receiver, and native Object/Reflect.defineProperty with a plain value descriptor. Dynamic keys, spreads, accessors, API aliases, extra properties and multiple assign sources are excluded.

Any, unknown, never, unresolved generic or overloaded property/value types are excluded because this check cannot prove their incompatibility. Type arguments and nested data fields are inspected with a 32-type recursion bound. Readonly fields are checked only for incompatible values; compatible writes are outside this rule. Under exact optional properties, authored write types are recovered only for direct non-transient declarations without mapped or generic substitution; other explicit-undefined writes can be missed.

Scope-resolved globals and standard-library signatures establish API identity. File-local namespace escapes, aliases, direct replacements or reflective mutation of Object/Reflect invalidate that namespace. Visible Object.prototype mutation or escape invalidates both APIs because descriptors inherit its fields. Indirect monkey-patching and external proxy behavior are not inferred. Generated files are excluded; tests remain checked.
rules.rationale: Object.assign, Reflect.set and property descriptors accept values that a normal typed property assignment rejects. They can invalidate a domain object's contract while subsequent reads retain its original type.
rules.remediation: Use an assignment that satisfies the declared property type, or construct and validate a complete replacement. Preserve any deliberate construction or external compatibility contract; do not cast away the incompatibility.
rules.summary: Keep native object mutation APIs from writing incompatible values into declared property types.

Targets must be broad primitives, finite unbranded primitive/nullish literal unions, or never. Any, unknown, void, object, enum, branded, intersection, generic and opaque targets are preserved. The import binding must be used only by direct custom calls or type-only references. Other namespace uses, aliases, exports, mutation and escapes conservatively disable the proof for that binding. Generated files are excluded; tests remain checked. No autofix is offered.
rules.rationale: Without a validator, z.custom<T>() returns its input unchanged while promising T. A parsed primitive outside that value domain fabricates a contract the caller may trust.
rules.remediation: Provide actual validation, use the appropriate primitive schema, or retain an honest unknown result until validation. Preserve composed validators and independently owned domain contracts.
rules.summary: Do not parse an incompatible primitive literal through an unvalidated Zod custom schema.

limitations: The rule uses stable local catch bindings and unshadowed built-in constructors, not runtime type information. Native DOMException constructor coverage is validated in Node; browser serialization is not evaluated. Custom replacers and explicit toJSON hooks are left to their serializer contract; a catch value is not guaranteed to be an Error. Member values, including cause, do not inherit the base Error's provenance; even an Error-valued member requires explicit value/dataflow proof outside this rule. Known literal __proto__ initializer chains preserve native hook inheritance and own toJSON precedence; computed __proto__ keys remain data. Unknown prototype expressions, hook values/spreads and deferred hook writes conservatively lose default serializer proof. Explicit writes invalidate constructor provenance except a later, separate top-level statement; deferred functions, loops, and unknown property keys conservatively lose constructor proof. Statically owned global/property writes and native Reflect.set/Reflect.defineProperty/Object.defineProperty/Object.defineProperties calls are tracked. Mutator aliases, replaced Reflect/Object methods, external calls, and runtime-only property names are not resolved; uncertain ordering conservatively loses proof.
rules.rationale: Native Error details are non-enumerable, so generic JSON serialization discards diagnostic information.
rules.remediation: Serialize explicit error fields or use an error-aware serializer.
rules.summary: Avoid generic JSON serialization that can omit native Error details.

examples.title: Use an explicit structural comparator

files.source: const same = JSON.stringify({ id: '1', state: 'ready' }) === JSON.stringify({ state: 'ready', id: '1' });

examples.title: Do not compare object serialization

limitations: Only direct binary comparisons between two unshadowed global JSON.stringify calls, including stable const destructured aliases of that global, are checked.
Primitive-only arrays are excluded when TypeScript can prove their element types.
Mutable, defaulted, reassigned, transitive and unknown aliases, stored serialization results, custom JSON objects, tests, generated files, and equality hidden inside helper calls are excluded.

Automatic fixes only reuse an already called private ordinary comparator in a complete comment-free two-declaration module. Its two inline record parameter types must contain the same ordered unique string fields, including an already-authored own non-callable string toJSON field; its sole return compares every corresponding field with strict equality and conjunction. The sole export is an ordinary zero-argument function explicitly returning boolean[], whose sole returned array contains the existing comparator call and one direct strict JSON comparison of fresh literal records with those exact ordered fields and primitive string values. Imports, ambient declarations, callbacks, computed/spread/getter properties, prototype-related keys, type parameters and all other expressions remain manual.

The own primitive toJSON data field is required in every literal and is never introduced by the fix: it prevents an inherited Object.prototype.toJSON hook from changing serialization. The direct unshadowed JSON.stringify intrinsic must retain its standard behavior; no new helper, field, import or domain name is chosen.
rules.rationale: JSON text equality depends on property insertion order and serialization behavior, so semantically equal objects can compare unequal and distinct values can collapse together.
rules.remediation: Compare an explicit domain projection structurally, or use a reviewed canonical serializer when JSON semantics are required.
rules.summary: Do not use JSON serialization as structural object equality.

limitations: Requires TypeScript type information. Only annotated local const bindings with identifier initializers are inspected; literals, calls, parameters, exported bindings, and type assertions are excluded.
Only unknown, object, and index-only dictionaries with unknown values are rejected. Typed dynamic registries, finite-key records, empty accumulators, and unknown external input are preserved.

Intentional type erasure at a real abstraction boundary needs a local suppression explaining that boundary. Automatic fixes remove the annotation only from an unused private binding in a module or block; referenced bindings retain their declared contract for manual review.
rules.rationale: Erasing a typed value's fields forces downstream code to rediscover the same contract through casts, reflection, or representation checks.
rules.remediation: Keep the inferred type, select the required domain fields, or use satisfies to check compatibility without erasing evidence.
rules.summary: Preserve a known value's contract instead of widening a local binding to unknown, object, or an unknown-valued dictionary.

limitations: Automatic fixes replace the unsound predicate with boolean only for an unused private function declaration without overloads, exports, eval, comments in the predicate, or declaration-file ownership. Runtime checks are preserved; observed callable contracts remain manual.

Requires type information and a non-generic, non-async function with one directly annotated parameter, an explicit broad string/number/bigint/boolean predicate and a single return. Literal, branded, structural, multi-primitive union, assertion, method and overloaded contracts are excluded; contextually typed callbacks are preserved.

Recognizes double-negation truthiness, a boolean parameter return or one same-kind literal comparison, optionally after a matching typeof equality. Without a typeof check, the input must already belong to the target primitive, except for double negation. String length comparisons use only concrete witnesses up to 256 characters. Arithmetic, dynamic bounds and complex boolean conditions are not inferred.

A broad string predicate returning local Schema.safeParse(parameter).success is also checked for a locally unchanged official z.uuid() or z.string().uuid() schema. The checker must resolve the namespace to installed node_modules/zod declaration files; local path aliases and opaque module resolution abstain. The const schema permits local parse/type/direct-export reads; every safeParse call must have exactly one direct argument, without options or spreads. Local aliases, method writes and opaque consumers abstain. Direct export alone is not mutation, but external consumer monkey-patching is not proved absent. Other value uses of its imported Zod namespace cause abstention. Transforms, brands, custom schemas, imported schemas and dynamic parse calls are excluded. Visible RegExp capabilities, regex literals or dynamic evaluation invalidate this initial native-pattern proof; external runtime monkeypatches are not inferred. This new schema profile has no automatic fix.

A concrete member of the promised broad primitive must demonstrably return false. Numeric witnesses must also be assignable as literals to the declared input: broad number assignability alone does not prove membership in a numeric enum. Compiler-invalid target/input relations, any/never/generic inputs and opaque implementations abstain. This rule does not discourage total boundary guards or infer branded refinements. Generated files are excluded; tests remain checked.
rules.rationale: Type predicates narrow both branches, and TypeScript trusts their implementation. A positive-number or non-empty-string predicate can return false for a value belonging to its promised type, causing callers to treat that value as a different type.
rules.remediation: Use a boolean return for an intentional value filter, or recognize every member of the promised type. Preserve required callback and public contracts; a refined domain may need a distinct validated type. Recheck false-branch callers when changing a predicate.
rules.summary: Do not give a partial primitive filter an explicit type predicate that excludes valid values in the false branch.

limitations: Requires type information proving the built-in Array or ReadonlyArray reduce/reduceRight method, an inline callback, and a fresh empty array or object-literal seed.

A copy is evidence for review, not proof of growth or measured latency. Automatic edits only remove an exact identity reducer over a fresh nonempty literal-string array in a sole exported zero-argument function with an explicit string[] return. The direct literal return remains fresh on every call. Snapshots, aliases, callbacks, nonliteral values, reverse reduction, imports, comments and other control flow remain manual.
rules.rationale: Copying a growing accumulator at every step can make collection quadratic instead of linear in its output size.
rules.remediation: Use map or flatMap where their semantics match, or append into a fresh locally owned accumulator. Preserve retained snapshots and shared state.
rules.summary: Review copies of the accumulated collection inside a built-in reduce callback.

examples.title: A public union retains its observable alternatives

limitations: Automatic fixes additionally require every existing identifier caller to be natively assignable to the original contract, without Any, unknown, error or unresolved types on the relevant surface. Comments inside the annotation and TypeScript suppression directives keep the finding manual. Removed named types/imports must retain an independent top-level exported type-alias or direct type-export read. Other removable annotations/assertions, the covering annotation and own-definition/self references cannot keep one another live; otherwise simultaneous fixes can introduce unused-type errors. The exact authored covering type and terminator token sequence are retained; edits that would merge distinct CR and LF terminators remain manual; no producer, call or function body is rewritten.

Only an inline binary parameter union in a strict module's top-level private scalar consumer is supported. Exactly one parameter, an explicit broad primitive return annotation, a single pure returned scalar expression and direct identifier-argument callers are required. Type queries or type-only exports of the callable, public APIs, callbacks, contextual signatures, overloads, generics, decorators, async functions, direct eval and fresh-object callers prevent findings.

Both alternatives must have complete ordinary finite structural surfaces consisting only of explicitly readonly broad string, number, boolean or bigint properties. Aliases, imports, re-exports and ordinary inheritance are resolved by the parser-owned TypeScript checker. Any, unknown, missing imports, open/generic/mapped/indexed types, classes, brands, literal discriminants, methods, properties with scalar type aliases, callbacks and recursive or nested object fields are unsupported.

Reports only proper native assignability: covered is assignable to covering and the reverse is false. Every covering member, including optional members, must exist in the covered type's enumerated declared surface. Otherwise an existing identifier may carry an incompatible extra field and be rejected after simplification; implicit Object members containing Any also cannot witness coverage. The covering type must declare every read field and a read required field; an all-optional reduced contract can reject existing callers. Identical alternatives and primitive/top/bottom redundancy remain upstream-owned; mutually assignable but nonidentical structures are excluded.

General union simplification can change Extract, conditional types, in-narrowing, fresh-literal checking and public presentation. Those contexts are excluded even when ordinary assignment succeeds. Flat destructuring counts every bound field as read; whole-object escape, mutation, helpers, closures, reflection, serialization, dynamic reads, implicit Object capabilities and JSX prevent findings. Imported Python protocol assignability is not approximated by this rule.
rules.rationale: A private consumer can advertise a redundant object alternative even though native assignability proves that the other alternative accepts every covered value. Dog | Animal keeps Animal; requiring Dog would unnecessarily restrict callers.
rules.remediation: Review retaining the covering alternative, or revise the alternatives if distinct cases were intended. Preserve producer types and runtime objects. The safe fix edits only a proven private parameter annotation; public APIs, producer types and runtime objects remain unchanged.
rules.summary: Keep the covering object contract in a private scalar consumer union.

String, scalar, tuple, set, record, aliased, composed, and dynamically constructed schemas are excluded.
The reversed `.default(...).optional()` order is preserved because its outer optional can return undefined instead of the default.
Defaults must be literal arrays or synchronous functions returning one literal array; dynamic or undefined fallbacks are excluded because Zod 3 reparses the fallback.

Automatic fixes require a whole module containing only one explicit zod/v3 namespace import and one unused unannotated private const with exact z.array(z.string()).optional().default([]). Other findings remain manual: exported introspection and supported Zod 4 constructor hooks observe the removed wrapper.
Calls containing comments are excluded so the fix never deletes authored context.
Test and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: An outer default already accepts undefined array input, so the inner optional wrapper adds no state or fallback behavior.
rules.remediation: Keep the array default and remove the immediately preceding `.optional()` call.
rules.summary: Remove `.optional()` immediately inside a Zod array default.

limitations: Only standalone line comments of two to eight words with at least two content tokens directly above a supported single-line statement are inspected; one-word headings and sentence-ending punctuation are excluded.

Evidence comes from that statement's identifier tokens, not strings, template text, comments, or neighboring statements. Stopwords and inflection folding are heuristic, not proof of semantic equivalence.

Directives, protected references, conditions, restrictions, ordering, repetition, direction, questions, prose paragraphs, sibling-group labels, novel content, and generated files are excluded. Automatic deletion is limited to whole-line comments whose removal preserves adjacent tool directives.
The conservative sibling-group exemption includes enclosing sibling groups and declaration/type-query pairs; it can miss genuine restatements inside those groups.
rules.rationale: A comment that only repeats code adds no context and can become stale independently.
rules.remediation: Remove a genuine restatement; retain conditions, constraints, rationale, and information absent from the statement.
rules.summary: Flag short standalone comments that repeat the adjacent statement's identifiers.

limitations: Test files, teardown calls, explanatory comments, non-function handlers, and handlers that consume or report the error are excluded. Empty statements are ignored when proving a whole handler is silent.

Recognized imported Zod construction chains and their stable local aliases are excluded, including URL schemas and primitive bigint, boolean, number and string coercion. Other untyped catch-like APIs are not proven to be Promises.

examples.title: Adding a different matcher preserves the built-in proof

limitations: Only supported `expect` matcher calls in recognized test files are inspected, including imported aliases, static string messages on imported Vitest/Playwright expect calls, and a single `.not` on zero-argument matchers. Local or type-only bindings, regular expressions, async modifiers and unsupported coercions are excluded; failing constant assertions are not tautologies.

The literal proof resolves scalar const bindings and aliases through lexical scope; mutable bindings, objects, arrays, destructuring, runtime initializers and forward references are excluded from that proof.

Positive toBe assertions on the same initialized, unreassigned local identifier const binding also have fixed identity, including runtime results. Different bindings, imported live values, property/getter accesses and deep-equality reflexivity remain excluded from this identity proof.

Expected-side runtime dependence, including a complete inline snapshot computed from its actual value, remains manual review; independent static interpolation and intentional partial masking are valid.

Direct framework expect.extend registrations exclude replaced built-in matchers; opaque registrations exclude all supported matchers, and nonempty custom equality testers exclude deep equality. Direct synchronous expect callbacks observed by a throwing matcher retain their assertion contracts. Cross-file or indirect matcher customization is not inferred.
rules.rationale: An assertion fixed by literal setup or one immutable binding's identity cannot distinguish a wrong result from the intended behavior.
rules.remediation: Assert on a value produced by the behavior under test against an independently specified expectation, or remove only the redundant assertion while preserving coverage.
rules.summary: Disallow supported assertions fixed by literal setup or immutable self identity.

examples.title: Let clear member names and types stand alone

limitations: Automatic fixes remove only an exact multiword member-name comment on its own line and retain all physical line endings; threshold-based or novel prose remains manual.

Only interface and type-literal bodies meeting the configured comment-count and restatement-ratio thresholds are reported. Negation, requirements, conditional relations, and fixed-value contracts are not counted as restatements. The novel-word threshold is a review heuristic, not proof that a comment contains no useful contract.

maxNovelWords.description: Most content words a comment may add beyond its member's own source and still count as a restatement.

minCommentedMembers.description: Fewest commented members that can count as a wall.

minCommentedRatio.description: Least share of the members that must be commented; below it the comments are group labels.

minRestatedRatio.description: Least share of the member comments that must be restatements.

rules.rationale: Repetitive member comments add scanning cost while hiding the comments that describe facts absent from the type.
rules.remediation: Delete comments that restate member names or types and keep comments that add constraints or behavior.

Automatic fixes remove only an erased mock assertion from an unused private unannotated const initialized by an identifier, optionally through unknown assertions. Every erased named type/generic/namespace binding must retain an independent exported type use; potentially erased annotations and self references cannot witness each other. rules.rationale: A type assertion can claim an unmocked value is a mock and bypass checking between the original callable and the mock API.

limitations: Only generated-free test files and direct double assertions containing a fn or spyOn call from a resolved Vitest/Jest import or an unshadowed vi/jest global are checked. Automatic fixes remove only erased double assertions on an unused private unannotated const initialized by a plain object containing primitive literals, nested plain objects and zero-argument canonical mock fn calls. Every erased named/generic/namespace binding must retain an independent exported type use outside self references and other erasable annotations. They retain the original runtime expression; exports, reads, contextual functions, generic mock factories, spreads, accessors, comments, scripts, declaration files and eval remain manual.
rules.rationale: Casting a partial object through unknown hides missing or stale collaborator members, so production interface changes can compile while the test double silently drifts.
rules.remediation: Define the smallest injected port and implement a typed recording fake, or make the fixture satisfy the real contract without passing through unknown.
rules.summary: Disallow mock-backed test doubles that bypass collaborator contracts through double assertions.

examples.title: Explain the concrete runtime contract
Reject a suppression with no auditable reason

limitations: Only ESLint disable comments and TypeScript expect-error directives are checked.
The rule uses a small anchored vocabulary and does not score prose quality generally.

Descriptions outside that exact vocabulary are excluded; an unflagged reason is not proof of a justified suppression. Missing descriptions remain owned by the upstream description requirement. Explicit path exclusions own generated-source boundaries; a source marker does not waive suppression accountability.
rules.rationale: Generic phrases satisfy require-description mechanically while leaving reviewers unable to audit the risk or remove stale debt.
rules.remediation: Name the exact type/runtime mismatch, external contract, or safety invariant that makes this suppression acceptable.
rules.summary: Require suppression descriptions to name the concrete mismatch or invariant instead of a generic non-reason.

examples.title: Use explicit async control flow

examples.title: Do not directly return a Promise callback chain from async code

limitations: The default async-return scope checks one directly returned `.then` call with an inline callback. The all-promise-calls scope checks direct calls to built-in Promise/PromiseLike.then, including optional and literal-computed calls, without automatic rewrites.

The receiver must be proven Promise-like by TypeScript; an earlier chain can still produce that receiver. The default async-return scope excludes rejection handlers and named callbacks. This is not the upstream return-await policy and no scheduling equivalence is promised.
The default async-return scope excludes direct loader callbacks passed to resolved `React.lazy` and `next/dynamic` imports because returning the module Promise is their framework contract.

All-promise-calls requires type information and excludes unproven/custom thenables, dynamic property names, property reads, destructuring, and extracted method aliases. Catch and finally remain available. Framework callback exclusions apply only to the default async-return scope.
rules.rationale: Promise callback chains mix explicit async control flow with nested callbacks, making sequencing and failure handling harder to read.
rules.remediation: Consider awaiting the Promise and returning the transformed value with ordinary async statements. Preserve catch boundaries, callback behavior, and observable scheduling when rewriting manually.
rules.summary: Prefer explicit `await` for proven Promise `.then` calls; the default scope checks direct async returns.

examples.title: Do not compare authentication tokens with equality

limitations: This uses secret-name heuristics and bounded stable local aliases of credential headers from an unshadowed native Request or imported NextRequest. Literal header names include no-substitution templates and erased TypeScript wrappers; unknown receivers and mutated aliases are excluded. This is not proof of runtime sensitivity. Ambiguous token names require an authentication or cryptographic qualifier; test files and public sentinel comparisons are excluded.
rules.rationale: Ordinary equality offers no constant-time guarantee for comparing secrets.

Producer analysis requires a finite literal tag, every declared tag syntactically witnessed, exhaustive simple return paths without literal constant conditions, plain object returns, and consistent optional-field presence for each tag. It resolves only unmerged local aliases/interfaces without inheritance or generics, and the built-in Promise around async returns. This is syntax-only evidence of field presence; explicit undefined, void and null payloads are skipped, while expression value types are not inferred. Dynamic returns, spreads, computed keys, accessors, loops and try statements are deliberately skipped.

A switch producer is supported only for a non-overloaded function declaration when its sole body statement switches on an unchanged direct string or number parameter, has unique same-kind literal labels and a default, and every nonempty case body is a sole object return or throw, optionally inside sole blocks. Empty labels may share the next terminating body; nested conditions, conditional returns, statement prefixes, breaks, other fallthrough, captured/closed inputs and switches under preceding control flow abstain. Broad parameter domains establish input witnesses for each label and the default; this does not infer branch-specific runtime effects or expression value types. Path visits, depth and returned objects are bounded conservatively.

Returned variants prove this producer's key relationships, not all legal consumers of a shared type. Automatic fixes are limited to an unused private nongeneric synchronous function with a direct inline contract and one literal-object conditional return; they preserve original member types and all runtime code. Shared/observed contracts and generated/declaration/test files remain excluded.
rules.rationale: A flat object with optional branch data loses the relationship between a tag and its payload. Callers cannot narrow to the required fields, and the type permits incomplete or contradictory combinations.
rules.remediation: If the variants are mutually exclusive, represent each with a literal tag and its required payload. Preserve shared fields on every member, including payload value types and nullability. For a producer returning a subset of a broader wire contract, give the producer a precise domain return type after validation.
rules.summary: Prefer discriminated unions for result contracts and locally proven tag-specific return payloads.

examples.title: Every required dependency is read

limitations: Automatic fixes additionally require every existing identifier caller to be natively assignable to the original contract, without Any, unknown, error or unresolved types on the relevant surface. Comments inside the annotation and TypeScript suppression directives keep the finding manual. Only unread required property signatures are removed; every read or optional member, modifier and terminator token is preserved. Edits that would merge distinct CR and LF terminators remain manual.

Requires parser-owned TypeScript information and a strict external module. Only top-level private function declarations and raw const arrows with exactly one explicit parameter and an independent broad primitive return annotation are supported. Every callable reference must be a direct call with one identifier argument; exports including type-only exports, typeof queries, callbacks, storage, constructors, contextual signatures, overloads, generics, decorators, async functions and direct eval prevent findings.

Only anonymous inline contracts made of broad string, number, boolean or bigint property types are supported. Fields may be plain or readonly; the consumer body must still prove read-only usage. Retained field modifiers and optional members are preserved. Named domain contracts, brands, literal discriminants, classes, methods, callbacks, indexes, mapped types and imported parameter contracts are excluded. At least one read required field and one unread required field must be established; all-optional reduced contracts can reject existing callers through weak-type checks.

The single return expression may use only fixed scalar field reads, flat destructuring, literals, operators, templates and scalar calls to same-file implemented top-level functions or raw const arrows with an explicit return annotation. These calls require one native resolved declaration, no generic or predicate signature, scalar arguments/result and complete active native checking of the local implementation file. Their helper bodies need not be pure because only scalar values cross the call and only an erased parameter annotation changes. Imported, aliased, ambient, overloaded, optional, spread and member calls remain unsupported. Bound destructured fields count as reads even when their local aliases are unused. Whole-object escape, identity, mutation, closures, reflection, serialization, dynamic keys, implicit Object capabilities and JSX are unsupported. Unknown semantic information causes abstention. Findings outside the fix proof remain manual; this is not a requirement to minimize every object or discard useful producer fields.
rules.rationale: A private scalar consumer can unnecessarily require data it never reads. Removing unused required fields accepts more structural values while preserving the original runtime object and producer information.
rules.remediation: Review a smaller existing contract, Pick or interface containing the read fields and preserving readonly and optional modifiers. Change the consumer annotation; a new runtime projection has different identity and allocation costs. The safe fix removes only proven unused required property signatures from the private inline annotation; producer objects, calls and function bodies remain unchanged.
rules.summary: Prefer the proven read-only subset for a private consumer parameter.

Test fixtures, generated clients and recognized local-file reads are excluded. This is bounded local analysis, not a general control-flow or mutation proof.
rules.rationale: External JSON is untrusted at runtime even when its expected TypeScript shape is known statically.

examples.title: Make finite dispatch explicit

limitations: Only direct if/else-if chains with at least three strict-equality tests are reported.

The discriminant must be a resolved lexical variable or parameter; unresolved globals, calls, getters, and indexed reads are excluded. Automatic conversion requires terminating compared branches and an explicit final else or type-proven open discriminant, preserving branch scopes and excluding comments, break statements, and function declarations.
Case values must be primitive literals. Member references and named constants are excluded because evaluating them can observe getters or mutate the selector. Generated sources are excluded.
The rule deliberately ignores compound predicates, loose equality, ranges, and chains that compare different discriminants.
rules.rationale: A switch makes finite dispatch cases visually uniform and easier to extend without duplicating the discriminant.
rules.remediation: Replace three or more strict-equality branches over the same discriminant with a switch; keep if statements for ranges, guards, and heterogeneous predicates.
rules.summary: Prefer switch over long if/else-if chains that compare one value for strict equality.

limitations: Requires TypeScript type information. Inspects scope-resolved global Reflect.get with a literal key (including no-substitution templates and erased TypeScript wrappers) on a closed object type, and Reflect.apply with a known call signature and a literal argument array.

Dynamic keys, open dictionaries, unknown/any/generic targets, explicit Reflect.get receivers, aliases, and nonliteral argument arrays are excluded. Deliberate proxy or metaprogramming calls need a local suppression. Automatic fixes cover comment-free nonoptional Reflect.get calls with a known existing property on an object. Immediate calls/tags, missing keys and Reflect.apply remain manual to preserve receiver and argument contracts.
rules.rationale: Reflect.get and Reflect.apply can accept property or argument mistakes that normal typed access catches.
rules.remediation: Use direct typed property access or call the typed function, preserving receivers and evaluation semantics.
rules.summary: Prefer typed access when Reflect.get or Reflect.apply discards a known contract.

examples.title: Consider grouping related data properties

Indexed runs with an immediately adjacent literal exact-length assertion are excluded; non-adjacent length checks and intentional prefix contracts remain manual review. No automatic rewrite: grouping can change observable getter or proxy reads.
rules.rationale: One whole-object assertion presents related expectations together and produces a complete structural diff.
rules.remediation: Consider one `toMatchObject` assertion for ordinary data objects. Preserve missing-property checks, identity, and getter or proxy behavior when deciding whether to combine assertions.

examples.title: Do not duplicate the schema shape
