examples.title: Infer the schema type

limitations: Automatic fixes use the original imported Zod namespace and existing schema only for an unused private unmerged interface or object alias with a positively identical shape and no declaration-file ownership or comments. Referenced/public contracts and coarse optional matching remain manual.
Only module-level const schemas and module-level type declarations are paired; local declarations are excluded rather than matched by spelling across scopes.
By default every field must positively agree; collection, nested-object and referenced-schema equivalence is not inferred from outer syntax alone.

This is a bounded syntactic comparison, not general type equivalence. Review schema input versus output, interface augmentation, and separately evolving domain contracts before replacing a declaration.
rules.rationale: A derived type stays synchronized when the runtime schema changes.
rules.remediation: Replace the hand-written twin with `z.infer<typeof Schema>`.
rules.summary: Derive a type from its Zod schema with `z.infer` instead of hand-writing a twin declaration beside it.

import { z } from "zod"; import type { ParsedRow } from "./contracts.js"; const RowSchema = z.object({ id: z.string() }); function load(): ParsedRow { return RowSchema.parse({}); }

examples.title: Do not hand-write the parsed return shape

files.source: import { z } from "zod"; const RowSchema = z.object({ id: z.string() }); type Row = z.output<typeof RowSchema>; function load(): Row { return RowSchema.parse({}); }

examples.title: Derive the validated return contract

limitations: Requires TypeScript type information and a returned output from a module-level local Zod object schema's `.parse()` or `.safeParse()` result.

Same-module name-correlated twins that `prefer-zod-infer` can prove are left to that established rule; this companion owns richer or renamed same-module and cross-module contracts proven by parse-return data flow.
Only a single plain non-generic object interface or object type alias with exact property keys and bidirectional assignability is reported.

Direct returns, nullish conditional branches, and one immutable local parse-result binding are followed; second aliases, assignments, helper calls, imported schemas, and other indirect data flow are intentionally excluded.
Contracts returned from more than one distinct local schema are excluded because no single schema has unambiguous ownership.
Readonly, augmented, indexed, callable, generated, constrained, any, unknown, and never contracts are excluded rather than guessed.

Nested contracts must preserve property keys, optionality and readonly behavior through aliases, containers and unambiguous unions. Distinct nested classes, accessor or method declarations, opaque members, ambiguous unions, or graphs beyond 128 compared pairs or 16 union alternatives are excluded.

Explicit callable bindings, independently annotated contextual callbacks or object members, and class members fulfilling an annotated heritage contract retain ownership of their named output contract. Inference from the function body alone does not establish ownership; independent helpers remain eligible.

Automatic fixes replace only the bare return annotation of an unused private nongeneric synchronous function returning one direct local-schema parse result. The removed named contract must retain an independent top-level exported type-alias or direct type-export read; references in other removable annotations/assertions or its own definition cannot keep it live. Sole-use contracts, multiple consumers, public/callback/async/nullish/aliased returns, comments, shadowing and missing original Zod import provenance preserve manual ownership; schemas and domain declarations are never moved or exported.
rules.rationale: A hand-written contract can drift from the runtime-validated value. Schema ownership determines whether deriving the type preserves the domain architecture.
rules.remediation: When the schema owns the contract, derive it with `z.output<typeof Schema>`. Preserve independently owned domain and public API contracts, and validate schema compatibility with those contracts.
rules.summary: Consider deriving validated return contracts from the Zod schema when the schema owns the contract.

examples.title: Do not repeat literal cases

limitations: Only consecutive top-level assertions with direct calls and static inputs and expected values are checked. Test-local callees and fixtures are excluded; imported or outer functions can still be stateful, so manual independence review is required. Not every runner supports test.each.
rules.rationale: Copy-pasted cases obscure the input table, and a thrown assertion can stop later cases from being reported.
rules.remediation: If the calls are independent, use the runner's named parameterized cases or subtests. Preserve ordered state-transition scenarios as one test.
rules.summary: Review three or more consecutive static-input call assertions as potential named cases.

examples.title: Make the default exhaustive

declare const kind: 'a' | 'b';
switch (kind) { case 'a': break; case 'b': break; default: }

examples.title: Do not leave an exhaustive default empty

limitations: Requires type information and singleton case values covering the current union. The helper must accept never to provide a compile-time check; its spelling alone is not a proof of that contract. Review the desired runtime behavior for unexpected external values.

Automatic fixes reuse only an existing private ordinary assertNever function with one never parameter, explicit void return and an exactly empty body. The complete comment-free module must otherwise contain only one exported ordinary function with an explicit primitive return type, one string-literal-union parameter, a complete switch with primitive literal returns and a final empty or break default, followed by a primitive fallback return. The existing helper is called in that default, preserving unexpected-value continuation while adding the never compile guard. Throwing helpers, other statements or exports, imports, defaults, aliases and dynamic behavior remain manual.
rules.rationale: An empty default silently accepts new union members instead of making the compiler identify the missing case.
rules.remediation: Call `assertNever` with the discriminant in the exhaustive switch default.
rules.summary: Require an empty switch default to call `assertNever` so discriminated unions remain exhaustive at compile time.

Composed JSX passed as props, render/asChild adapters, dynamic labels, children, unknown components, and prop spreads are left to runtime accessibility testing. Referenced IDs, CSS visibility, and meaningful wording are not verified. Generated files, tests, fixtures, and stories are excluded. No automatic labels are invented.
A hidden prop with unshadowed undefined or exact void 0 does not hide the element or its children. Shadowed undefined and dynamic hidden values remain unproven.

limitations: Quoted string keys and bracket access are treated as explicit external-wire boundaries.

Computed, numeric, symbol, private, generated, and PascalCase property names are excluded. External-library ownership is not inferred: preserve its spelling using quoted keys and bracket access, or an exact local suppression.

Automatic renaming is limited to an unused private interface or object type alias without heritage, exports, collisions, polymorphic this, computed/indexed keys, merged declarations, or eval. Runtime objects, referenced types and protocol boundaries remain manual.
rules.rationale: Unquoted snake_case property syntax makes external wire naming indistinguishable from application-domain naming and lets inconsistent contracts spread through typed code.

examples.title: A structurally compatible fake fails the constructor's runtime guard

limitations: Requires direct construction of both owned consumer and collaborator classes, with a first-statement consumer constructor guard rejecting the exact parameter with if (!(parameter instanceof Contract)) throw. Parentheses preserve exact constructor and guard symbol identity; casts remain excluded.

The contract must resolve to an abstract class without decorators, static blocks, unresolved ancestors, or custom computed static members in its resolved hierarchy. Escaped class constructors are checked across every owned module in the typed program.

Structural interfaces, non-rejecting branches, reassignment before the guard, casts, unresolved heritage, dynamic factories, implementation static blocks, explicit implementation constructors or initializers, involved modules referencing prototype-mutator members or assigning prototypes, escaped class constructors, and third-party classes are excluded.

Automatic edits only add the existing abstract base to a closed explicit module with exactly three private classes and one direct construction. The base has only one abstract void method and no constructor, fields, heritage, decorators or static work; the implementation has the matching empty method. The consumer retains the exact readonly parameter and TypeError nominal rejection guard. No guard is weakened. Other runtime inheritance or initialization remains manual; this intentionally repairs the diagnosed startup TypeError.
rules.rationale: A structurally assignable fake can still fail a constructor's nominal runtime guard. Pure structural interfaces do not require an implements clause.
rules.remediation: Use an implementation inheriting the existing abstract class, or remove the nominal guard if the boundary is intentionally structural.
rules.summary: Require nominal inheritance when an injected abstract class is rejected by an instanceof guard.

examples.title: The service declares its operation

files.source: class OrchestratorService { constructor(private readonly worker: Worker) {} run(): void { this.worker.run(); } }

examples.title: A single service operation still needs its contract

limitations: Automatic fixes only add the exact existing closed type alias named by an already-authored direct factory return annotation. A complete comment-free four-declaration module must contain one exported closed object type alias containing one zero-argument void method, one local matching worker interface, one ordinary nonabstract nongeneric class with an empty constructor retaining a private readonly worker parameter and one matching public forwarding method, and one exported ordinary required-worker-parameter factory returning that exact new class as the port. Unique lexical bindings, no heritage/decorators/defaults/imports/merges/other members or authority, and exact existing types/calls are required. Mergeable public interfaces are refused because downstream declaration augmentation can introduce a private-field compatibility error. No contract, method, field, import or name is invented; emitted JavaScript remains identical. Other shapes remain manual.
The rule checks service, store, and provider class declarations whose constructor stores a typed behavioral collaborator and whose public method reaches that collaborator.
Existing local interfaces, type aliases, and inherited contracts can cover the operations; the compiler owns signature compatibility.
Imported or dynamic base classes with unavailable declarations and decorated classes or operations are unresolved and do not produce a finding.

Constructor retention requires an untouched parameter property or one direct, unconditional assignment. Written or replaced operation members do not prove their declared bodies execute; external aliases, mutators, and callbacks are not resolved.
Generated files and JavaScript without implements syntax are excluded.
rules.rationale: A one-operation service can orchestrate a collaborator without declaring the contract that callers consume and implementations and fakes satisfy.
rules.remediation: Explicitly implement a focused interface or extend an abstract class covering the service operations. Export the contract only when its consumers need it.
rules.summary: Require explicit contracts for classes that invoke retained collaborators.

Unshadowed native fetch members and bounded stable const aliases or destructuring are recognized. Reassigned, defaulted and unknown aliases and arbitrary forwarding functions are excluded.
Accessors and unproved prototypes are excluded because native option conversion can attach or replace a signal before it is read.

allowIn.description: Glob patterns for wrapper modules exempt from the rule. Matched against the ABSOLUTE file path, so anchor with a `**/` prefix (e.g. `**/http-client.ts`).

rules.rationale: An unbounded request can occupy work indefinitely when an upstream stalls.
rules.remediation: Pass an abort signal, such as `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)`, in the fetch init.
rules.summary: Require an explicit abort signal on locally analyzable global fetch calls.

examples.title: Export behavior through a focused contract

limitations: Automatic fixes only add the exact existing closed type alias named by an already-authored direct factory return annotation. A complete comment-free four-declaration module must contain one exported closed object type alias containing one zero-argument void method, one local matching worker interface, one ordinary nonabstract nongeneric class with an empty constructor retaining a private readonly worker parameter and one matching public forwarding method, and one exported ordinary required-worker-parameter factory returning that exact new class as the port. Unique lexical bindings, no heritage/decorators/defaults/imports/merges/other members or authority, and exact existing types/calls are required. Mergeable public interfaces are refused because downstream declaration augmentation can introduce a private-field compatibility error. No contract, method, field, import or name is invented; emitted JavaScript remains identical. Other shapes remain manual.
JavaScript files are excluded because implements is TypeScript syntax; imported framework base contracts still require manual policy review.
An exported injected service may also receive require-port-for-service: the two diagnostics intentionally enforce distinct service-boundary and general exported-contract policy scopes.

The rule checks module-level class declarations and direct class-expression values exported directly, through local export specifiers, or through a default identifier; re-exports and expressions wrapped in other calls require review.
An extends clause satisfies the contract only when its target is a locally declared abstract class; imported base-class contracts require an explicit implements clause.
Static factories and data-only classes without public instance methods are outside the contract requirement.
rules.rationale: An explicit contract names the intended public capability separately from implementation details. TypeScript already supports structural compatibility; this is an architecture policy, not a prerequisite for substitution.
rules.remediation: Declare a focused interface and add an implements clause, or inherit from an intentional base contract.
rules.summary: Require exported concrete classes with public behavior to declare a contract.

Automatic renaming is limited to private module const bindings with no collisions, exports, dynamic eval, or inferred function names. Public names and unsafe reference shapes remain manual.
rules.rationale: A reusable Zod schema is a runtime type contract. PascalCase mirrors that role; SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE should remain reserved for scalar values and lookup tables.

A complete comment-free four-declaration module must contain one exported closed object type alias containing one zero-argument void method, one local matching worker interface, one ordinary nonabstract nongeneric class with an empty constructor retaining a private readonly worker parameter and one matching public forwarding method, and one exported ordinary required-worker-parameter factory returning that exact new class as the port. Unique lexical bindings, no heritage/decorators/defaults/imports/merges/other members or authority, and exact existing types/calls are required. Mergeable public interfaces are refused because downstream declaration augmentation can introduce a private-field compatibility error. No contract, method, field, import or name is invented; emitted JavaScript remains identical. Other shapes remain manual.

Retained injection requires an untouched parameter property or a single direct, unconditional constructor assignment. Conditional, repeated, replaced, updated, or deleted stores are unresolved rather than proof of retained injection.

examples.title: Own queries in an injected repository

limitations: The rule recognizes conventional database receiver names, Cloudflare DB bindings, direct pool.query calls, explicit query-builder terminals, and Prisma-style model delegates; unusually named or heavily aliased clients require architectural review.
Query construction without a recognized execution terminal is intentionally not reported.
Stable local Map, WeakMap, and URLSearchParams instances are excluded. Other conventional receiver names are heuristics, not proof of a database API.
Constructor injection inherited from a base class or transformed through a wrapper is not inferred by this syntax-only rule.
rules.rationale: An injected repository class is the preferred ownership boundary for database access under this architectural policy; free functions can also express explicit dependencies.

Tests, stories, fixtures and generated files are excluded. No automatic title or decorative marker is invented.
A hidden prop with unshadowed undefined or exact void 0 does not hide the element. Shadowed undefined and dynamic hidden values remain unproven.

Named imports of node:path/path join and resolve are followed when their complete trailing static path proves a source suffix. Assertion roots are scope-resolved for supported test runners and Node assert imports; local or unknown helpers with assertion-like names are not inferred.

Contained static paths, including stable nested join/resolve descendants, beneath a native mkdtemp/mkdtempSync result are generated artifacts. Absolute or drive-anchored resolve segments and traversal above the proven directory remain unproven. Literal replace/replaceAll nonidentity guards comparing the same raw read remain unreported; fixed-string comparisons remain candidates.

rules.rationale: Substring and regex checks can pass on comments or unreachable configuration and fail after behavior-preserving formatting changes.
rules.remediation: Reuse adequate existing validation; otherwise assert a distinct parsed or runtime contract. Preserve deliberate representation contracts with an exact justified suppression.

limitations: Cross-environment comparisons require at least two discovered, readable HCL or JSON tfvars environments.
Only scalar variables declared exactly as bool, number, or string are compared; dynamic, collection, interpolated HCL, heredoc, and incomplete roots are conservatively skipped.
Unreadable declarations, JSON configuration declarations, and override files suppress findings because the effective variable contracts cannot be proven.
Malformed or duplicate-key JSON inputs suppress findings for that file and comparisons across the root.
Numeric-to-string comparisons abstain for non-finite values or exponents expanding beyond 10,000 decimal places; unsupported HCL string escapes are also skipped.
Named tfvars files are inferred as environments; repeated values are advisory because invocation order and intentional fail-closed contracts cannot be proven from filenames.
Generated fixtures, testdata, backend configuration, backups, templates, and other specimen inputs are excluded.
Sensitive and non-primitive values are never printed in diagnostics.
rules.rationale: Undeclared assignments are stale configuration, while repeated scalar values can hide whether a setting is truly environment-specific or belongs in shared configuration.

limitations: Comparisons against a catalog traversal with an exact static deployment selector, such as local.catalog.prod.project, are advisory warnings when both operands have the same qualified identity leaf. Catalog keys can describe business concepts rather than deployments. Dynamic keys, computed operands, alias definitions and external catalog contents are not resolved. Existing literal-comparison findings remain errors and take precedence within the same attribute.
A comparison inside validation, precondition, postcondition, check, or assert asserts which inputs are legal and is exempt. Terraform test files are rejected separately by SARJ206.
Comparison against the empty string is an unset-input test, not an environment branch, and is ignored.

An interpolated value such as "cache-${var.environment}" names a resource and is not a branch. Quoted templates used as comparison operands or literal-list contains needles are inspected only when their interpolations are references or pure normalizers. Escaped markers, branches inside templates, directives, brace-containing interpolation bodies, arbitrary function results, and heredoc bodies remain opaque.
Pure case/whitespace normalization with lower, upper, or trimspace is unwrapped; arbitrary function results remain opaque.

Ambiguous identity names (`project`, `account`, `tenant`, `branch`, `stack`, and `slug`) require an environment-labelled comparison literal or literal-list member such as `platform-prod`; comparisons to ordinary business values and map indexing by those names are intentionally ignored.
Only .tf and terragrunt.hcl are read; Packer, Nomad, and other HCL dialects are outside this rule.
Environment-keyed map indexing and lookup are data selection rather than branching and are allowed.
A diagnostic is reported at the attribute's line. In a multi-line value the comparison itself may sit further down, so `# sarj-noqa: SARJ204` belongs on the attribute line.
rules.rationale: Hard-coded environment branches scatter deployment policy through expressions and obscure the actual capability or value that callers intend to vary.
rules.remediation: Pass the selected typed value or one named capability from the root configuration. Retain an explicit validation, precondition, or check when environment identity is itself the safety invariant.
rules.summary: Warn when Terraform chooses behavior from deployment-identity comparisons; prefer explicit typed capabilities or values.

Resource/data overrides replace computed provider attributes, not configured or noncomputed default attributes. Without provider-schema proof, these overrides are excluded, even for genuine computed-value reassertions. Mock providers, generated defaults, transformed assertions, JSON test syntax, provider-scoped overrides, and dynamic expressions are also excluded.

limitations: Safe fixes select an existing literal leaf only from a closed Boolean-literal conditional tree with homogeneous Boolean, bounded decimal-number or plain quoted-string leaves on one standalone attribute line in top-level locals. All branches are validated; comments, escapes, templates, nulls, references, calls, mixed types and ambiguous source ranges remain manual.
Only direct conditional branches are inspected; independent choices inside calls, collections and templates remain out of scope.
Assertions, generated files, fixtures, testdata and non-.tf inputs are excluded.
An existing deployment-identity diagnostic takes precedence at the same attribute.
This is a review advisory; no automatic extraction or deletion is safe for every expression.
rules.rationale: Chained conditional branches obscure the value being selected and scatter deployment policy.
rules.remediation: Extract a branch into a named local or pass a typed input from the caller. Preserve lazy evaluation, null guards and resource dependencies when extracting an expression.

Empty literal values are not reported.
rules.rationale: A plain `value` copies the secret into Terraform state, the plan output and the service revision, where anyone who can read them sees it, and rotating it needs a redeploy.
rules.remediation: Store the secret in Secret Manager and reference it with `value_source { secret_key_ref { ... } }` or `value_from { secret_key_ref { ... } }`.

Scalar role values also follow same-file unique static local aliases and bounded literal join expressions; grouping and HCL string escapes preserve the value. Cycles, duplicate declarations, templates and unknown inputs remain opaque.
Local collections must be literal strings consumed as a set; duplicate declarations, local aliases, dynamic values, maps and comprehensions are excluded.
Unknown expressions, inherited organization/folder access and other roles are not guessed.

String validation enforces a narrower domain format

limitations: Safe fixes remove only complete standalone validation blocks containing exactly the proven redundant condition and a literal error message, without comments or additional content.
Only exact, syntax-parsed tautologies over the validation block's own variable are reported.
Provider constraints, compound expressions containing a real domain predicate, dynamic types, heterogeneous tuples, and validations of another variable are intentionally not inferred.
Generated files, fixtures, testdata, and non-.tf inputs are excluded.
rules.rationale: Terraform applies declared type and nullability constraints before custom validation. Rechecking readability, conversion to the declared type, non-nullability, or an exhaustive non-nullable boolean domain cannot reject another valid input and obscures actual domain requirements.
rules.remediation: Delete the redundant validation block. Keep validation for narrower domain requirements such as ranges, formats, enums, otherwise permitted nulls, and relationships between fields.

examples.title: Comment merely narrates an assignment
Generated HCL is owned by its generator
Comment labels a group of sibling attributes
Maintained block comment repeats its attribute
Comment records a provider constraint
Comment repeats one declaration label

limitations: Safe fixes remove only the diagnosed complete standalone comment group, preserve line boundaries and require identical executable HCL tokens.
Only short comments immediately above native HCL declarations at the same indentation are compared.
Comment groups, sibling headings, heredocs, directives, generated files, fixtures, references, units, modality, and causal explanations are preserved.
rules.rationale: A declaration-label comment adds no durable information and can drift; comments that explain constraints, grouping, or operational rationale remain useful.
rules.remediation: Delete the restatement or replace it with the constraint the configuration cannot express. Improve an author-controlled label when the declaration itself is unclear.
rules.summary: Flag a short comment attached to an HCL declaration when it only repeats that declaration's kind, label, or attribute name.

examples.title: A literal true assertion adds no constraint
Retain the resource without an inert assertion
Do not model deployment policy as a fake resource
Keep a lifecycle condition protecting a provisioning operation

limitations: Safe fixes remove only standalone literal-true conditions with literal messages and no comments or extra content, preserving the resource address and all other lifecycle behavior. Real assertions require ownership review.
Only lifecycle precondition and postcondition blocks directly inside terraform_data resources are checked.
Resources with a direct file, local-exec, or remote-exec provisioner are excluded; their conditions may protect provisioning operations.
Ordinary terraform_data replacement triggers, variable validation, check blocks, and lifecycle conditions on provider resources remain allowed.
Only .tf files are read; Terraform test files and other HCL dialects are outside this rule.
rules.rationale: A terraform_data resource created only to reject a plan turns configuration policy into stateful graph noise. The assertion drifts with today's configuration while obscuring the input, resource, test, or deployment boundary that owns the invariant.
rules.remediation: Delete the terraform_data guard. Put an input invariant on its variable, a provider invariant on the owning resource, and environment or rollout policy in tests and deployment review.
rules.summary: Disallow lifecycle conditions attached to terraform_data guard resources.

Cloud SQL child database uses its deletable default

limitations: Only curated resource-specific guard spellings with stable provider semantics are recognized.
Provider versions can change defaults; unresolved expressions are advisory because protection cannot be proven within one file.
A lifecycle prevent_destroy guard is accepted as Terraform plan-time protection but does not survive removal of the resource block.
rules.rationale: Stateful services can lose durable production data when an accidental Terraform change or destroy is allowed to delete the backing resource.
rules.remediation: Use the exact provider guard supported by that resource. Where none exists, consider lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }, which no longer protects the resource after its block is removed.
rules.summary: Require a curated stateful Terraform resource to declare a proven provider-native deletion guard or literal lifecycle destroy guard.

limitations: Only the curated resource types and documented Google provider guards are recognized.

Dynamic guards, ABANDON retention policies, and unresolved destructive options retain WARNING; missing or literal-disabled protection enforces the explicit protect-or-explain policy.
Terraform lifecycle.prevent_destroy is plan-time protection and does not survive removal of the resource block.
rules.rationale: Buckets, secrets, and registries may hold durable state; unguarded deletion needs review when no authoritative recovery source exists.
rules.remediation: Prefer a supported provider guard. Otherwise consider lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }, which stops planned deletion only while the resource block remains, or suppress SARJ203 with a disposable rationale.
rules.summary: Require a curated durable-data container to declare a literal provider-side deletion guard or Terraform lifecycle destroy guard.

Unknown methods/callables, decorated functions, async generators, conditional bindings, transferred stacks, wildcard imports, and generated files are excluded.
Resource aliases and interprocedural mutation are not inferred. No autofix is offered because executing previously dropped cleanup can raise new exceptions.

Coroutine-function assignment aliases must remain unmutated and unescaped; attribute inspection, containers, returned functions and unknown helper arguments abstain. Direct calls and proven stack registrations remain supported.
Visible namespace APIs, frame/module introspection, code mutation and bound attribute setters invalidate the file's provenance proof.
rules.rationale: The synchronous callback API discards the returned coroutine without awaiting it, so the cleanup body never runs.
rules.remediation: Use AsyncExitStack and register the coroutine function with push_async_callback.
rules.summary: Do not register a proven async cleanup function with ExitStack.callback.

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

async def close():
    executor = ThreadPoolExecutor()
    executor.shutdown(wait=True)

examples.title: Waiting shutdown runs on the event-loop thread

limitations: Requires a stable direct assignment from an import-proven concurrent.futures ThreadPoolExecutor or ProcessPoolExecutor constructor and a direct shutdown call in an executing async function body.

Only omitted wait or literal wait=True is reported. Literal wait=False, dynamic arguments, nested synchronous callbacks, custom factories, borrowed receivers, context-managed bindings and explicit receiver/API mutation are excluded.

Stable enclosing-function and module bindings are recognized. Ordinary argument passing does not erase the constructor identity; external monkey-patching inside opaque consumers and runtime replacement of stdlib modules are not inferred.

Unknown bound-method consumers, receiver aliases/storage, conditional imports, namespace escapes, reflection, wildcard imports and generated files conservatively abstain. No automatic shutdown-policy change is offered.
rules.rationale: Executor.shutdown waits for workers by default; invoking it directly in an async function can block the event loop and delay unrelated service work or cancellation.
rules.remediation: Await asyncio.to_thread(executor.shutdown, wait=True), or use the application's explicit nonblocking shutdown policy after arranging worker ownership and completion.
rules.summary: Run waiting executor shutdown outside the async event-loop thread.

examples.title: Default is outside the declared field bounds

limitations: The rule checks direct public fields on classes that directly inherit Pydantic `BaseModel`.
It reports only statically provable literal conflicts with nullability, `Literal` domains, and numeric or string-length bounds from assignment or `Annotated` Field metadata.
Fields with before, plain, or wrap validation that can transform a default are excluded.
Imported annotation aliases are followed only to a unique local Python module within the same checkout.
Test and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: Pydantic does not validate defaults unless default validation is enabled. An invalid literal can therefore enter a model while contradicting its annotation or field bounds.
rules.remediation: Choose a default allowed by the annotation and every literal `Field` bound, or widen the contract when the value is intentional.
rules.summary: Require literal Pydantic model-field defaults to satisfy their resolved contract.

examples.title: Public API returns an unnamed record

limitations: Visible FastAPI routes are owned by SARJ094. Private functions and classes, closures, tests, generated files, documentation examples, recognized framework hooks, and dictionary conversion methods are excluded.

Record evidence is flow-sensitive but local: literals, proven built-in dict keyword construction, static string-key writes, and unique unconditional local type aliases are recognized. Dynamic keys, opaque escapes, ambiguous control flow, generic aliases, and cross-module aliases make the rule abstain.
An explicit unique local mapping type alias preserves a named open/pinned mapping contract. Type aliases do not add required-key validation; stricter Any-value typing remains owned by SARJ447.
rules.rationale: A named record makes field types and required keys explicit to callers and static tooling.
rules.remediation: Define and return a `TypedDict`, Pydantic model, or frozen dataclass for a closed record shape. When the API intentionally exposes an extensible concrete dictionary, use one explicit named mapping type alias to preserve its dictionary contract and runtime API.
rules.summary: Public Python API returns an unnamed fixed-shape record.

examples.title: Validate each floating candidate
Do not validate only the reduced value

limitations: Requires an unshadowed multiargument built-in min/max, stable local aliases/float conversion, and a subsequent direct not math.isfinite/numpy.isfinite rejection guard. Only a single raising guard or its OR with direct comparisons is supported.

Floating candidates are direct float-typed parameters, float literals/casts, known NumPy floating constructors, or scalar min results from closed local NumPy array/asarray constructors with explicit floating dtype and optional sum. The initial array payload must be a direct unannotated or float-typed parameter; literal, locally assembled and integer-typed payloads abstain. NumPy scalar constructors require an already proved NaN-capable scalar argument. Unknown methods named min and external model arrays are not inferred.

Requires a finite-capable first operand and a distinct later NaN-capable origin. Integer-only inputs, repeated aliases of the same floating origin, a known NaN first operand, custom key/comparators, mutation/escape and unknown numeric types abstain.

Any preceding finiteness check in the same function causes abstention rather than attempting arbitrary validator/control-flow equivalence. Dynamic namespaces, import mutations/escapes, test and generated files are excluded. The warning concerns an ineffective finiteness subcheck; it does not prove every other acceptance condition is satisfiable. Control-transferring enclosing finalizers abstain. There is no automatic rewrite or rule against deliberate NaN-ignoring APIs.
rules.rationale: Python's min/max compares operands in order. A later NaN can be ignored, leaving a finite result that passes a finiteness check even though an original candidate was invalid.
rules.remediation: Check every floating candidate before reducing it, or use a deliberately NaN-propagating reduction and validate its result.
rules.summary: Validate floating candidates before a built-in min/max can hide a NaN.

limitations: Only assertions on an attribute named `status_code` in collected Python tests are checked.
Exact status contracts, finite success sets, arbitrary `.status` attributes, and locally suppressed chaos tests are excluded.
Only Python `assert` statements in default test_* collection shapes are analyzed.

rules.rationale: Authentication, routing, validation, and domain failures can all replace the intended response while a negative-only status assertion remains green.

examples.title: PostgreSQL computes a time-series reporting rollup

limitations: Statically recoverable SQL in non-test, non-generated Python modules with native PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite imports is analyzed, regardless of filename. The historical SARJ020 identifier is retained.

Every parsed SELECT DISTINCT (including DISTINCT ON), deduplicating UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, GROUP BY, and built-in SQL aggregate is reported, including CTEs, nested writes, windowed aggregates, identity-bounded queries, and LIMIT queries. ALL set operations remain valid. This deliberately replaces the former reporting-size thresholds.

A single imported backend owns module SQL. Resolvable first-party query contracts and re-exports retain their native analytical-provider evidence. Mixed backend modules require a direct query sink on a source-proven native connection or annotated parameter; unresolved receivers and separately bound queries abstain.

Known ClickHouse, BigQuery, DuckDB, Snowflake, Trino, Athena, and Databricks drivers are analytical owners. Comments, scalar SQL values, identifiers, Python docstrings, and IS DISTINCT FROM do not trigger the policy.
SQLite multi-argument MIN/MAX and MySQL ANY_VALUE retain their scalar semantics; PostgreSQL ANY_VALUE remains an aggregate.

PostgreSQL pg_catalog aggregates and lowercase quoted built-ins retain native identity. Unknown schemas and distinct quoted uppercase PostgreSQL function names abstain. Executing EXPLAIN ANALYZE is analyzed; plan-only EXPLAIN and unsupported PostgreSQL EXPLAIN options abstain.
Dynamic SQL grammar, ORM expression trees, unknown wrappers, user-defined aggregates, and malformed SQL are not inferred. No automatic datastore migration is safe.
rules.rationale: Project architecture reserves deduplication, grouping, and aggregate queries for ClickHouse or another analytical database, so reporting work does not compete with transactional reads. This is a datastore policy; SQL syntax alone cannot establish a query's execution cost.
rules.remediation: Move reporting and aggregation to ClickHouse or another analytical database with an explicit freshness contract. Use an indexed EXISTS or direct row lookup for operational existence checks. Preserve atomicity for transactional invariants; use an exact, explained SARJ020 exception when a reviewed invariant must remain in the transactional database.
rules.summary: Keep DISTINCT, GROUP BY, and SQL aggregates in analytical databases.

examples.title: A TypedDict preserves the record schema

limitations: Automatic fixes replace only direct Any values in covariant Mapping parameters of closed private nested synchronous helpers whose parameter is entirely unused. Defaults, consumers, reflection/frame access, comments, shadowed object, mutable/aliased/string annotations and newly unused Any imports remain manual.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.
Only proven built-in or standard-library string-keyed mappings whose value recursively contains `typing.Any` are reported; `object` is intentionally not treated as `Any`.

Unique unconditional module-level PEP 695 and explicit TypeAlias chains are resolved with cycle guards. Plain module assignments are checked only when they directly define an Any-valued mapping used in a module-level annotation; imported, conditional, rebound, and ambiguous aliases are excluded.
Generated and vendored sources are excluded; exact local suppressions remain auditable.
Annotated metadata, Literal values and unresolved generic parameter positions are excluded; only type arguments are inspected.
Proven override method signatures and direct BaseModel.model_dump return contracts are excluded; local annotations, casts and TypeAdapter targets remain checked.
Ambiguous type-import origins, attribute mutations, escaped canonical type namespaces and dynamic namespace access cause conservative file abstention.
rules.rationale: An `Any`-valued mapping disables checking transitively and conceals whether the value is a fixed record, an arbitrary JSON tree, or a genuinely opaque Python object.
rules.remediation: Use `TypedDict` (and `Unpack[TypedDict]` for closed keyword arguments) for fixed records, a Pydantic model for untrusted runtime input, `pydantic.JsonValue` for arbitrary JSON, or `object` plus explicit narrowing for a genuinely opaque Python value. Preserve unchanged external API signatures with an exact explained suppression; do not automatically widen published returns.
rules.summary: String-keyed mapping types must not erase their values with `Any`.

examples.title: Do not hide client allocation in a service constructor
Inject a client owned by the async composition scope

limitations: This is an explicit architecture policy for import-proven HTTPX AsyncClient calls executed by synchronous nongenerator class __init__ methods, including import aliases and stable constructor assignment aliases bounded to 32 links, eager comprehensions and nested definition defaults/decorators.

One-hop same-file undecorated synchronous factories with stable lexical bindings are followed only when their sole statement after an optional docstring returns a proven constructor call. Zero-argument lambda factories are supported when invoked; deferred function/lambda/generator bodies are not constructor execution.

Unknown or imported factory implementations, overridable methods, wrapper chains, dynamic namespace access, wildcard imports, ambiguous/rebound aliases and visible namespace mutation are not inferred. A generator's first iterable is eager; other generator expressions remain deferred even when a caller might consume them immediately.
Constructor parameter defaults execute at class definition, not on each constructor call, and are outside this rule. No automatic ownership transfer, sharing decision or lifecycle rewrite is safe.
Annotations and lazy type-alias/type-parameter expressions are excluded: their source location does not prove constructor-time execution. Framework-driven evaluation of annotations is not inferred.

Escaped HTTPX module objects cause conservative abstention, including module-object assignment aliases. Constructor aliases must remain confined to calls, annotations, attribute access or stable single-name aliases; unknown argument, return or storage escapes and visible mutation invalidate the import proof.

Nested class bodies are followed only without bases or metaclass keywords, because custom class namespace preparation can replace imported names. Method bodies still use their normal lexical bindings. Generator factories and lambdas create deferred generators rather than clients and are excluded.

HTTPX recommends scoped client reuse and explicit asynchronous closure; its API does not universally prohibit constructor ownership. This stricter constructor boundary is the requested policy. See https://www.python-httpx.org/async/ . Ruff ASYNC212 instead owns blocking HTTPX use in async functions.
rules.rationale: Constructor-owned clients repeat transport setup for each service instance and hide the boundary that owns pooling and asynchronous cleanup.
rules.remediation: Create and close an appropriately scoped AsyncClient at the async composition boundary, and inject it into consumers. Keep tenant credentials, cookies, event loops and independent ownership boundaries separate; do not replace them with a global client.
rules.summary: Inject an HTTPX AsyncClient instead of constructing one in __init__.

examples.title: Each call creates a fresh coroutine

limitations: Only a proven functools import used as the innermost decorator on a coroutine function is reported.
Async generators, transformed functions, ambiguous or rebound imports, and generated files are excluded.
Wildcard imports and names rebound by relative imports or imports outside the module body are excluded conservatively.
lru_cache with disabled, dynamic, or unpacked maxsize arguments is excluded; an omitted size or literal positive integer or None is required.
Indirect wrapping calls and runtime monkeypatches are not resolved. Test code is checked because coroutine reuse fails there too.
No automatic rewrite is offered because cache lifetime, cancellation, and concurrency require an explicit design decision.
rules.rationale: `functools.cache`, `lru_cache`, and `cached_property` store the coroutine object returned by an async function rather than its awaited value. A subsequent cache hit can raise `RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine`.
rules.remediation: Remove the standard library cache or use an async-aware cache that stores completed results.
rules.summary: Standard library cache decorates a coroutine function and retains single-use coroutine objects.

examples.title: Bare Arrange, Act, and Assert labels

limitations: Safe fixes remove only reported standalone phase labels, preserving executable tokens and meaningful rationale.
Standalone comments across recognized test and test-support files are checked, including fixtures, helpers, and module sections.
Trailing comments and comments inside bracketed expressions are excluded.
Comments containing words beyond the bounded phase-label grammar are preserved.
rules.rationale: Phase labels narrate test structure without explaining behavior and often indicate that a test needs clearer names or smaller units.
rules.remediation: Delete the label; if the phases remain hard to follow, extract a named helper or split the test.
rules.summary: Test files must not use bare phase comments such as Arrange, Act, Assert, Given, When, or Then.

examples.title: A copied outer mapping can be updated locally
Removing a raw entry changes caller data
Before-validation changes the original mapping
Return normalized data without changing the original

limitations: Only import-resolved Pydantic model_validator and field_validator decorators with literal mode='before' are analyzed.

Owned model ancestry must be undecorated and retain its effective validation contract. Even a spelled typing.final class decorator is excluded when its provider cannot be proven; class replacement or mutation can detach the validator.
Explicit descriptors and Pydantic's automatic classmethod conversion require an untouched builtin namespace; builtin imports or __builtins__ access conservatively abstain.
Standalone model files with unknown module identity and non-Pydantic/non-typing imports are excluded because self-imported model aliases cannot be resolved safely.

Class member values must be inert literals or closed canonical Field/ConfigDict constructions with literal options or known builtin default factories. Descriptor aliases, special methods, unknown decorators and wrap validators are excluded.
The raw value parameter, stable aliases, direct item writes, and type-proven builtin container mutators are checked. isinstance narrowing and resolved typing.cast preserve provenance.
After validators, ordinary methods, arbitrary same-named methods, unknown container mutators, captured closure aliases, and ambiguous control-flow bindings are excluded.
Generated/vendor sources are excluded; maintained tests are checked. No autofix is offered because copying, validation, identity, and evaluation order can differ.
rules.rationale: Treat raw before-validator inputs as borrowed data. They can be caller-owned or reused by another validation branch; mutation can leak normalization into aliases and leave data changed after validation fails. Return replacements even when a particular caller supplies fresh data.
rules.remediation: Return a normalized replacement mapping or collection. Copy the changed path before updating nested values; a fresh outer copy permits outer writes but retains shared descendants.
rules.summary: Preserve raw inputs in Pydantic before validators.

limitations: Checks actual Python comment tokens for bare or empty sarj-noqa, unscoped pyright: ignore, basic/standard Pyright modes, report* downgrades below error, analyzeUnannotatedFunctions/disableBytesTypePromotions/strictParameterNoneValue=false and scoped Ruff/Flake8 file or Ruff range disables. SARJ054 retains precedence for Ruff banned-api file directives.
Ruff owns blanket noqa and type: ignore through PGH004 and PGH003. Exact local exceptions remain available; this rule does not judge whether their explanations justify the exception.

Directive examples inside strings and unrelated Pyright feature flags are excluded. Source-generated markers cannot waive accountability; use explicit whole-path exclusions for generated/vendor code. Consumer type-checker configuration remains outside this source rule.

The full Standards gate protects this rule and the existing suppression-accountability checks from inline waivers, rule exclusions and diagnostic baselines. Explicitly selected partial checks remain scoped.
rules.rationale: A blanket suppression hides unrelated errors on its line. A file-level diagnostic downgrade also authorizes future defects outside the reviewed exception. Suppression checks cannot waive themselves.
rules.remediation: Fix the diagnostic or use an exact, line-local rule code with a concrete boundary reason.
rules.summary: Use named, line-local suppressions instead of blanket, file or range disables.

examples.title: Preserve named typed keywords with a named unused binding

limitations: Safe fixes remove only an unused keyword capture with no annotation or proven builtin object on a private unescaped nested synchronous nongenerator helper when every direct call already satisfies the remaining declared signature. They preserve every caller argument and bare-star keyword-only contract. Module/public/callback contracts, other annotations, extra keywords, expanded calls, captures, decorators, type parameters and namespace/frame access remain review-only. Known frame and metadata capabilities, their import aliases and metadata field access prevent fixes.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.
This strict interface policy is not proof of incorrect behavior or a universal ban on the object type; genuinely open boundaries use a reasoned exact-code exception.
Reports missing, Any- or object-valued keyword captures whether discarded, read or forwarded.

Precise or unresolved decorated signature-declaration families and functions with unresolved decorator effects are excluded; known classmethod/staticmethod/abstractmethod/final/override declarations remain eligible.
Homogeneous keyword types constrain values but allow arbitrary names; ParamSpec preserves only its target's existing contract.

Generated/vendor source and stubs are excluded. Unresolved imports, wildcard imports, conflicting imports, actual global or definition-time writes and shadowed annotation provenance are conservative. Identical imports and read-only global declarations remain eligible.

Cross-file aliases, external stubs, generated signatures and runtime reflection are not resolved; transparent annotation metadata and ambiguous decorated declaration families can cause conservative false negatives.
Open or used captures still require an explicit intended contract. Dynamic payload/formatting APIs can intentionally need an exact-code exception.
Runtime special methods and canonical override declarations retain WARNING because framework and inherited signatures can require an open keyword contract; ordinary declared interfaces use ERROR.
rules.rationale: Replacing a fixed typed interface with broad **kwargs can erase required keyword names and per-key value types, making test doubles accept calls the real implementation rejects. object remains a safe typed top type, and deliberately open data interfaces can be valid; this strict interface policy requires a precise contract or a documented open-boundary exception.
rules.remediation: Keep explicit typed parameters at fixed interfaces. Preserve required keyword names with named unused local bindings. Use ParamSpec for forwarding, Unpack[TypedDict] for named schemas, or a precise homogeneous value type. Document genuinely open interfaces with an exact-code reasoned suppression.
rules.summary: Prefer precise keyword interfaces over missing, Any- or object-valued captures.

limitations: Only files named conftest.py are inspected.
A test module is recognized from an explicit module-path component or test-package import name beginning with `test_` or ending with `_test`.
Literal pytest_plugins declarations are checked; dynamically assembled plugin paths are excluded.
rules.rationale: pytest imports conftest for every test module in its scope; importing a specific test from conftest turns that test into global collection infrastructure and creates cycles and order dependence.

examples.title: Recognize the primitive promised to callers
TypeGuard can intentionally recognize no inputs
A constant result does not prove a primitive type
An integer test does not prove a string

limitations: Checks undecorated, non-generic module functions with one parameter and a single returned direct builtin isinstance call, its unary not, or a bool constant, optionally after a docstring.
Guard symbols must resolve to typing or typing_extensions TypeGuard or TypeIs. Targets and checked classes are builtin int, bool, str or bytes; bool is treated as an int subtype.

Inputs must be object or fully classified plain unions of those primitive types and None. Direct positive impossible isinstance tests and compiler-invalid TypeIs target/input relationships are excluded.
Input unions are traversed iteratively with a bounded node budget; overly complex annotations are excluded.
Literal and refined targets, aliases, custom classes, float numeric promotion, tuple isinstance tests, helper predicates, nested functions and complex bodies are not inferred.

TypeGuard may intentionally recognize a subset of its target, so TypeGuard[int] with an isinstance bool test remains legal. Visible namespace mutation and ambiguous or shadowed symbols abstain conservatively.

Constant false remains legal for TypeGuard. Constant true is reported only with a proven incompatible primitive or None input; false TypeIs needs a proven inhabited target. Negated isinstance uses the same finite witness domains.
Repeated top-level function definition names abstain because overloads can constrain the public input more narrowly than the implementation input.
Generated files are excluded; maintained tests remain checked. No autofix guesses a domain or changes false-branch behavior.
rules.rationale: A guard annotation does not validate its implementation. Returning an incompatible primitive predicate check makes callers trust the wrong primitive; TypeIs also incorrectly excludes rejected target values in the false branch.
rules.remediation: Align the declared target and runtime test. For an intentional partial predicate, TypeGuard may narrow only the true branch; TypeIs must recognize every target value admitted by its input. Review callers before changing the narrowing contract.
rules.summary: Primitive type guards must agree with the builtin predicate they return.

examples.title: Override repeats its base method documentation
Override documents its implementation-specific behavior

limitations: Only methods inherited through a local base name, parameterized local base, or simple local class alias declared earlier in the same lexical body are compared; imported and dynamic bases are excluded.
Transitive local ancestors are followed in declared base order without guessing across lexical scopes.
Overloads, generated files, undocumented bases, and methods whose docstring is their entire body are excluded.
rules.rationale: Inherited documentation is available through `inspect.getdoc` and `help`, while a duplicate can drift. Direct `Child.method.__doc__` consumers remain a reason to retain and suppress the copy.
rules.remediation: Delete the copied docstring only when the base contract is complete and no runtime or generated-documentation consumer requires direct `__doc__`. Keep override-specific behavior in the override docstring.
rules.summary: An override repeats the documentation of the single local base method it actually overrides.

examples.title: A POST route repeats the verb in its path

limitations: Only literal route paths on a FastAPI or APIRouter receiver created in the same file are checked.
The final path segment is read; its first word (split on '-', '_' or '.') must be create, add or new.
A final path parameter is accepted, and tests and generated files are excluded.
Deliberate RPC-style integration endpoints exist; keep them with an exact suppression and its reason.
rules.rationale: The HTTP method already states the action. A trailing create, add or new segment turns a resource API into ad hoc RPC names, so clients cannot predict paths and PUT, PATCH and DELETE lose their pairing.
rules.remediation: POST to the collection path, use PUT on the item path for an upsert and PATCH for a partial update.
rules.summary: POST routes name their collection instead of ending in a create, add or new segment.

examples.title: A local marker hides a domain outcome outside the return contract
The return contract represents the expected unsupported outcome

limitations: This review warning checks stable module-level local Exception/ValueError subclasses whose bodies contain only pass, ellipsis or docstring expressions, including empty local subclasses of those markers. A source-visible direct raise of the class or its constructor is required; imported errors, payload-bearing classes, methods, decorators, generic/ambiguous bases and unused definitions abstain.

Raising a ValueError-derived marker from an import-proven Pydantic field/model validator or legacy validator preserves that rejection protocol. Unknown external bases and visible escapes of the class to registrations, callbacks or other value consumers abstain; HTTPException and other framework-required exception types remain valid.

Expectedness is not inferred from a name, message or prefix. Genuine exceptional markers may also match and require review rather than conversion. Cross-module callers and registrations, indirect raises, dynamically mutated namespaces and class aliases are not inferred.

Tests, generated and vendor code are excluded. No automatic rewrite is safe: a result return must preserve failure handling and transaction/resource unwinding. SARJ435 separately reviews joined-string reason identities.
rules.rationale: An empty custom exception creates another control-flow type without declaring failure data in the function's return contract. Expected domain outcomes can often use tagged result variants that callers handle explicitly, while exceptional failures and framework rejection still need exceptions.
rules.remediation: Review direct raises of this marker. If the condition is an expected domain outcome, return a typed tagged success/failure union and update every caller. Preserve true exceptional failures, validation rejection, transport/framework protocols, cancellation, unwinding and useful cause context. A class name or a raise does not prove the condition is expected.
rules.summary: Return typed outcomes for expected domain failures instead of name-only exceptions.

limitations: Every authored Python del statement is reported once, regardless of how many targets it contains.

Autofix only blanks one standalone, comment-free local deletion in a closed private nested ordinary helper with no parameters and exactly a None assignment to that same name, that deletion, and a literal return. Existing names, the assignment, line numbers and line endings remain unchanged; multiline deletion and unsupported source line separators are refused; all other deletion requires review.

Containing callables must have proven inert execution and no observable helper references, frame or metadata access, callbacks, reachable failures or unknown finalizers. Only proven local None deletion is modeled; deleted names retain an unbound tombstone so subsequent reads cannot resolve to a builtin or global.
Generated and vendored files are excluded.
rules.rationale: Deleting a name, attribute, or collection entry introduces lifetime or in-place mutation semantics that are harder to follow than explicit value construction.
rules.remediation: Remove unused-value deletion markers. Rebuild collections with comprehensions, copies, or immutable value helpers such as dataclasses.replace. When an external API or deliberate lifetime boundary requires deletion, add an exact SARJ442 suppression on the statement and explain why.
rules.summary: Avoid `del` statements; prefer constructing an immutable replacement value.

examples.title: A tagged outcome is discarded
The caller forwards the outcome

limitations: Review warning for standalone synchronous calls and directly awaited async calls to stable source-visible module functions. The return must resolve to at least two direct Pydantic, dataclass or required TypedDict variants sharing a string Literal discriminator with disjoint values. No name such as Result or Error establishes proof.

Module-local and prepared-project absolute imports, quoted bare aliases and PEP 604 returns, unquoted typing.Union and Annotated, and bounded non-generic type aliases are supported. Quoted typing-wrapper combinations, unknown receivers, decorated or generic functions, re-exports, optional/scalar branches, generic records, inheritance, dynamic namespaces, rebound identities and unsupported annotations abstain.

Named assignments, returned, passed or conditionally consumed results are preserved. A direct assignment to the single underscore target is an explicit discard and is reviewed. An unawaited async call belongs to coroutine checks. Direct class-body execution, generated sources and opaque providers are excluded. This rule identifies discarding; it does not prove that an assignment handles every variant or infer expected failure from a record name.

String Literal tags must be direct instance fields on every variant and retain their original class-scope binding. Quoted field tags remain outside the proof; quoted module return annotations retain their source declaration anchor. Dynamic fields, optional TypedDict fields, non-string tags, computed Literal values and multi-field discriminator hierarchies are not inferred. No automatic rewrite changes call behavior or error handling.
rules.rationale: A tagged return union makes possible outcomes visible in the type contract. Discarding the value bypasses the caller's opportunity to handle its alternatives, including a declared failure.
rules.remediation: Use or forward the returned outcome. Handle its variants with match and a typed exhaustive fallback such as assert_never; preserve payloads and side effects. Do not delete the operation or hide the result behind a dummy assignment.
rules.summary: Handle a returned tagged outcome instead of discarding it.

examples.title: Pass the validated replacement to the next operation
A checked replacement is constructed and discarded

limitations: Reports standalone calls to source-resolved, undecorated Python functions with a non-None return annotation, value returns, and an explicit raise.
Local and imported functions, import aliases, bounded re-exports, and directly awaited async functions are supported; unknown receivers, decorated callables, and dynamic namespaces are excluded.
Compiler scopes select runtime bindings; observed global/nonlocal reassignment and ambiguous scopes are excluded. Import identity is established without executing provider modules.
Observed first-party namespace writes and opaque module escapes invalidate affected providers across aliases, self imports and re-exports; package namespace hazards conservatively cover descendants.

Source-proven unittest.mock.patch APIs invalidate static contracts in the caller and provider/re-export modules, including string-target patches. Ordinary locally named patch functions do not disable checks.
Stable local callable aliases with prior direct assignments are followed through bounded chains. Conditional assignments and unresolved callable escapes are excluded.
Direct execution in class bodies is excluded because sequential lookup and metaclass-prepared namespaces can supply different callees. Method bodies remain checked.
Functions with explicit mutation, standalone command calls, generators, nested definitions, or context-manager/try/loop orchestration are excluded. This is not a general purity proof.

Calls inside returned values must resolve to supported builtin or source-resolved nominal value construction. Opaque command functions, receiver calls, and direct returned attribute/subscript reads are excluded; a conversion around an unknown command does not prove validation.

Import-resolved pytest.raises and source-proven unittest exception assertion blocks observe the exception contract and are excluded. Generated and vendored sources are excluded; maintained tests are checked.

Top-level return contracts follow stable lexical aliases, first-party type imports, unions, and Annotated type content through a bounded source-only analysis. Nullable collection elements and annotation metadata do not make the returned collection nullable.
Nullable, object, Any, Never, NoReturn, generic type-parameter, structural protocol, and unresolved return contracts are excluded. No automatic assignment, deletion, or validation rewrite is offered.
rules.rationale: Discarding a conversion's returned value makes validation an implicit exception side effect. The caller can continue with unvalidated or unnormalized inputs even after constructing a checked replacement.
rules.remediation: Use the checked result in the following operation, or expose a separate validation command returning None. Preserve exception behavior; do not delete the call or add a dummy assignment.
rules.summary: Consume a value-producing validator's result instead of relying on its exceptions.

examples.title: Argument section records behavior
Remove only the repeated type label

limitations: Safe fixes remove only native-proven redundant type labels in plain unescaped private nested synchronous nongenerator functions with no detected metadata consumer. Behavioral descriptions, other sections and quote style remain intact; public APIs, escaped/decorated helpers and escaped/raw literals remain review-only. Known frame and metadata capabilities, their import aliases and metadata field access prevent fixes.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.
Only fully typed functions and Google-like colon-headed argument, return, and yield sections are checked.
A documented label must parse as a Python type expression and match the corresponding annotation.
Generated files, runtime-consumed prompt, CLI, and route docstrings, properties, abstract methods, overloads, protocol methods, and partially typed signatures are excluded.
NumPy underlined sections and Sphinx type fields intentionally remain with their selected documentation convention.

A reasoned exact-code suppression on the function declaration or closing docstring line preserves required documentation tooling conventions; markers inside string content are not suppression comments.
rules.rationale: A repeated type spelling can drift from the annotation and obscures the behavioral contract that only prose can express.
rules.remediation: Remove only the redundant type label. Keep behavioral meaning, units, defaults, constraints, and raised-error conditions in the docstring.
rules.summary: A docstring type label repeats an annotation from the fully typed signature.

examples.title: A fixed model field is hidden behind a string-selected object return
Normalize the input and read the typed field

limitations: Checks stable private module functions with two parameters, an object/Any input and return, and a string field selector in either parameter order. The body must consist of a known local Pydantic model getattr branch, a builtin dict or import-proven standard Mapping get/subscript branch and a None fallback. Import-proven typing casts are transparent.

Every visible use must be a direct call with a declared model field selected by a literal or a bounded chain of dominating single-assignment constants. Dynamic selectors, escaped/public helpers, imported/inherited models, custom attribute hooks, shadowed builtins and ambiguous or rebound bindings abstain. No application modules are imported.

Opaque values, arbitrary dictionaries and generic reflection alone are valid. Raw Pydantic validators are not prohibited, but extracting this closed dual-shape reader does not make its erased field contract typed.
Authored tests are checked; generated/vendor code is excluded. This is a warning without an autofix because normalization can change rejection, coercion, default generation and error timing.
rules.rationale: A string-selected object return discards the model's field types and duplicates the raw and validated representations at every read. Literal field names at all local callers prove this is a fixed record API.
rules.remediation: Normalize raw input once with the named model's model_validate, then use typed attributes. Preserve missing-field, coercion, default and validation-error behavior; before validators still own raw input.
rules.summary: Normalize a known model instead of reading its fields through a model-or-dict accessor.

Use self-aliased imports to mark intentional facade re-exports to static tooling. limitations: Safe fixes remove duplicate elements only from comment-free literal sequences. Standalone literal append calls can also be removed. Any insert growth prevents autofixing the file because removing earlier entries would change positional insertion order; commented declarations remain review-only.
One fully static module-level list or tuple plus literal append, extend, and insert growth is analyzed.
Generated, dynamically reassigned, and non-Python declarations are excluded.
rules.rationale: Duplicate exports add noise to a module's public contract and commonly reveal copy-paste mistakes in generated or maintained facade lists.

examples.title: Two validators repeat one strip rule

limitations: Only methods decorated with an import-proven Pydantic `field_validator` in the same class body are compared.
Bodies must match structurally after renaming parameters by position and dropping a leading docstring.
Validators with different `mode` arguments, different decorator stacks, or near-identical bodies are not reported.
rules.rationale: Two field validators with the same mode and the same body are one validation rule written twice; a later fix to one copy silently leaves the other field validated by the old rule.
rules.remediation: List every field in one `@field_validator(...)` decorator and branch on `info.field_name` where the fields genuinely differ.
rules.summary: Pydantic field validators in one model repeat the same body.

examples.title: A 500 detail returns the exception message
A 500 detail is a fixed message

limitations: Checks `HTTPException` from FastAPI or Starlette with a status resolved to 500 (integer, Starlette `status.HTTP_500_*` or `HTTPStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`).
The detail must use the variable bound by an enclosing `except ... as name` handler directly (not one of its attributes), call a `traceback.format_*` function, or reference `__file__`.
Exception text copied first into another variable or model is not traced. Other statuses are not checked because 4xx details commonly map domain errors. Tests and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: An unexpected exception's text can contain SQL, file paths, hostnames, provider responses or personal data. Copying it into a 500 response discloses internals to any caller and gives attackers a probe.
rules.remediation: Log the exception with its traceback, then raise the 500 with a fixed detail or error code.
rules.summary: HTTP 500 exception details must not carry exception text or tracebacks.

examples.title: Remove statically redundant nesting
The authored return needs no constant guards
Guard clauses reduce nesting
Synthetic library eligibility after: score 7
Synthetic library eligibility before: score 28
Six nested decisions require a review

limitations: Autofix only flattens a whole-function chain of at most 32 literal True guards with no else to its existing standalone single-line literal return, inside a closed private nested ordinary zero-parameter helper. Other complexity requires review.

All containing callables must have proven inert execution without Global/Nonlocal declarations, escaped helper references, observable frames or metadata, callbacks, reachable failures or unknown finalizers. Comments and unsupported source line separators prevent edits. The exact return spelling, physical line number, surrounding source and LF/CRLF endings are preserved.
Sarj metric, not exact Sonar compatibility: functions and lambdas are independent; calls, recursion, function annotations, parameter defaults, and decorators are not scored.

Conditions, loops, exception handlers, match statements, and conditional expressions add one plus nesting. Elif and else add one; their bodies add nesting. Each run of like boolean operators adds one.
Comprehension loops and filters add one plus nesting. Match cases are free; case guards count as nested conditions. Try, finally, with, return, break, continue, and await add no points themselves.
Generated code is excluded; authored tests and all function lengths are checked. The threshold is a shared policy constant, not a correctness boundary.
rules.rationale: Nested control flow increases the context a reader must retain while following a function.
rules.remediation: Examples are fictional and written for this documentation; domain types are omitted. The library example replaces nested eligibility checks with early returns while preserving evaluation order. Refactor one function at a time, starting with its largest contributors. First simplify control flow and reduce nesting within the function. Extract a helper only when it clarifies a cohesive responsibility or enables meaningful reuse; do not split code solely to lower the score. Use lookup tables only for equivalent pure dispatch. Preserve APIs, side effects, evaluation order, and exception behavior. Run relevant tests before and after; remeasure the original and extracted functions. Do not hide branches in dense expressions or add indirection just to lower a score.
rules.summary: Error on cognitive complexity above 20; scores up to 20 pass.

limitations: Only pytest-collected test functions in test_*.py and *_test.py modules are inspected; fixtures, helpers, nested functions, and conftest.py are not.
A sleep is reported only when the next statement in the same block is an assert, so an assert placed after the enclosing with, if, or try block is not reported.
A duration is fixed only when built from numeric literals and UPPER_CASE constants; durations read from other names or from calls are not reported.
Sleeps inside loops are treated as polling, and time.sleep in an async test is left to Ruff ASYNC251.
rules.rationale: A fixed sleep followed by an assertion guesses how long the code under test needs. On a loaded CI runner the guess is too short and the test flakes; on an idle one every run pays the whole interval.
rules.remediation: Await the signal the code exposes, such as an event, future, queue item, or fake callback, or poll the condition with a deadline. When the test deliberately proves that nothing happens during a quiet window, keep the sleep with an exact SARJ455 suppression that names the window.
rules.summary: Do not sleep for a fixed interval and then assert in a test.
