examples.title: A polling loop sleeps for a hardcoded interval

limitations: Only awaited asyncio.sleep, anyio.sleep, and trio.sleep, and time.sleep in synchronous functions, are inspected; import aliases are followed and shadowed names abstain. time.sleep in an async function is left to Ruff ASYNC251.

A duration is fixed when it folds with +, -, *, /, and // from numeric literals and UPPER_CASE constants bound once at module scope in the same file to such a literal; zero and negative results are yields, not waits.
Imported, reassigned, or shadowed constants, lowercase names, attributes including class constants, subscripts, and calls are treated as configurable and are not reported.

The sleep must sit in the body of a for, async for, or while loop inside the same function; loop else clauses, module-level and class-level loops, and loops in an enclosing function across a nested def, lambda, or class are not reported.
Test modules, test directories, conftest.py, test-support paths, and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: A polling or cleanup loop that sleeps for a literal interval gives tests no seam: every test that drives the loop pays the whole interval in real time, and replacing the module's sleep is a monkeypatch that SARJ445 forbids. Suites slow down one hardcoded interval at a time.
rules.remediation: Route the interval through a constructor or configuration parameter, or call an injected sleeper or clock, so tests can pass a zero interval or a recording fake. Keep a literal only behind an exact SARJ485 suppression that names why the interval must never change under test.
rules.summary: Do not sleep for a fixed literal interval inside a production loop.

examples.title: A 400 is treated as not found

limitations: Membership tests against a literal collection, `or` chains of equality on one subject, and match or-patterns are checked when they name both 400 and 404 as integers or recognized status constants.
Statuses held in variables or named constants other than the HTTPStatus and Starlette names are not resolved.
Test modules are excluded because parametrized cases list statuses together.
rules.rationale: A 400 means the request or its configuration is wrong; folding it into the not-found path makes a misconfiguration log success with an empty result, indistinguishable from a deleted record.
rules.remediation: Give 404 its own branch and raise the 400 as a non-retriable client error.
rules.summary: Do not handle HTTP 400 and 404 statuses in one branch.

examples.title: After-validator assigns a frozen model field

limitations: The rule checks direct public fields on direct Pydantic `BaseModel` subclasses configured with literal `ConfigDict(frozen=True)`, a literal model_config dictionary, or `frozen=True` as a class argument.
It detects direct assignment, annotated assignment, augmented assignment, and tuple or list destructuring through the validator's receiver.
Indirect mutation through method calls, `setattr`, or `object.__setattr__` is outside its scope.
Test and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: Direct field assignment contradicts the model's frozen contract and can fail only when the validator runs, making construction behavior surprising and brittle.
rules.remediation: Validate without mutation, compute the value before constructing the model, or return an explicitly updated model when replacement is part of the design.
rules.summary: Do not assign declared fields in after-validators on frozen Pydantic models.

rules.remediation: Require the constructor argument and resolve any default at the composition root or call site.
rules.summary: Constructor option silently falls back to application settings when omitted.

examples.title: No integer lies strictly between zero and one
Zero is admitted by the interval

limitations: Only plain direct module-level BaseModel subclasses and built-in int, float, str and list fields are inspected.
Bounds must be finite literals; int and length bounds must be integers, and float bounds must convert exactly.
Positive integer multiple_of constraints use exact integer arithmetic; floating-point steps remain outside the rule.
Literal strict, frozen, validate_default and extra model settings preserve coverage; other or dynamic configuration is excluded.
Unknown metadata, nullable types, repeated bound names, methods, dynamic namespaces and generated files are excluded.
Visible namespace APIs, dynamic module access, ambiguous imports and escaped or mutated imported objects exclude the file.
No autofix chooses a domain or changes validation behavior.
rules.rationale: Contradictory literal constraints reject every field value, including integer multiples and float intervals with no representable member.
rules.remediation: Correct the conflicting bounds so the declared field domain admits the intended values.
rules.summary: Pydantic field bounds must admit at least one value.

examples.title: Import machinery becomes a configurable parameter
Implementation owns its lazy import

limitations: Flags defaults resolving to importlib.import_module, importlib.__import__, or builtins.__import__, including stable module-level import and single-assignment aliases and unshadowed __import__.

Every body reference to the parameter must be a direct call with one identical literal module name. Dynamic names, multiple module names, forwarding, returned/captured hooks, rebinding, unpacking and unused defaults are excluded.

Tests, test support, and generated code are excluded. Required loader parameters, application loaders, wrapper lambdas, alias chains, comprehensions, and imports local to enclosing scopes are not inferred.

Conservatively skips shadowed or rebound names, wildcard-import files, reassigned loader attributes, conflicting conditional or relative imports, and exception or pattern captures of importer roots, symbols or assignment aliases. Identical repeated importer imports remain valid. A relevant-name capture in an unrelated local scope can cause a false negative because capture checks are file-wide.

Assignment aliases require one module binding and precede use by line and column. Defaults use their enclosing evaluation scope: earlier statements in the nearest executing class body can shadow loaders; methods and nested classes do not close over class attributes. Enclosing function body bindings remain conservative exclusions, but a function's parameters do not shadow its own defaults. Relevant global declarations and walrus writes exclude sensitive importer names. Compound class statements can cause conservative omissions. Dynamic namespace mutation is not inferred. No autofix: changing arguments or import placement can alter API and initialization behavior.
rules.rationale: When every direct use imports the same literal module, a generic importer can be unnecessary customization rather than a domain dependency. Dynamic plugin/import APIs legitimately need import hooks.
rules.remediation: Consider owning the fixed import inside the implementation when import-hook substitution is unnecessary. Preserve intentional import hooks and plugin APIs; do not add wrapper factories or Protocols just to silence this advisory.
rules.summary: Avoid a generic module-loader parameter used only to import one fixed module.

examples.title: Replace the nested value and its parent
A transformation changes its caller's model
Return a trusted replacement
A shallow model copy shares a nested model

limitations: Only source-proven Pydantic fields, typed model collections, stable local aliases, and recognized shallow copies are analyzed; application modules are never imported.
Mutation of ordinary instance receivers and fresh owned values is excluded. Before-validator raw inputs belong to SARJ482.

Ambiguous branch bindings, mixed-ownership literals, closures, opaque calls, custom copy hooks, dynamic update mappings, and deep-copy provenance are left unreported. Readonly collection interfaces do not imply immutable elements.
Recursive or deeply nested annotation traversal is bounded. Constructor argument aliases are not propagated through potentially custom validation.
Builtin list/dict/set mutators require a known container shape. Generated/vendor sources are excluded; maintained tests are checked. No automatic copying or validation rewrite is offered.
rules.rationale: Assignments through shared model inputs also change every caller alias. Copying only the outer list or model retains nested aliases and can make repeated transformations observe each other's changes.
rules.remediation: Return replacement models and explicitly capture the result. Copy each changed ancestor; permit fresh local builders and use exact suppressions for documented in-place APIs. model_copy updates must already satisfy the complete model contract.
rules.summary: Return replacement values instead of mutating caller-owned Pydantic models.

examples.title: Trusted construction still satisfies the declared vocabulary

limitations: Only plain, direct, module-level Pydantic BaseModel subclasses with supported built-in and typing field annotations are inspected; hooks, inheritance, class decorators and custom methods are excluded.

Checks explicit None conflicts, closed string Literal domains, and bounded side-effect-free literal values contradicting builtin primitive or container field contracts. Coercible input is not assumed to be validated stored output.

Container literals preserve their actual construction semantics, including last-wins dictionary keys. Unpacking, calls, unhashable literal containers, opaque values, numeric Literal domains, bounds, aliases and custom field types are not inferred. Bool remains an int subtype, and numeric int-to-float/complex assignability is preserved.
model_construct must use explicit keywords; omitted required fields are checked only when no unpacking or positional argument can supply them.

model_copy requires a fresh exact constructor or a stable unescaped local constructor binding, plus a plain literal update dictionary. Arbitrary annotated receivers and overridden methods are excluded.
Field aliases, non-passive model configuration, class or instance mutation and escape, ambiguous namespaces, tests and generated files are excluded.

Direct model field annotations exceeding a bounded depth or node budget exclude the file rather than risking recursive analysis failure. Literal analysis also bounds the value tree and combined string/bytes content to avoid excessive witness work.
Trusted valid construction and copy operations remain legal. No autofix chooses domain values or changes validation behavior.
rules.rationale: model_construct and model_copy(update=...) store supplied values without validation. A contradictory literal or an omitted required construction field can therefore invalidate a model's declared type while the permissive bypass signatures still pass static checking.
rules.remediation: Supply values satisfying the model contract and every required field, or validate a complete input mapping with the normal constructor or model_validate. A model_validate call on an existing model instance does not necessarily revalidate it; keep trusted bypasses only when their inputs preserve the contract.
rules.summary: Do not create a provably invalid model through Pydantic validation bypass APIs.

examples.title: Input conversion is followed by ordinary field validation
An after validator stores an incompatible primitive unchanged
A plain validator also bypasses subsequent field validation
The validator output satisfies the stored field contract

limitations: Checks stable direct module-level BaseModel classes containing one synchronous field-validator method, plain annotated fields, and optional literal defaults. Inheritance, configuration, custom methods, field metadata, class decorators and escaped or mutated model classes are excluded.

The validator must have the canonical field_validator/classmethod stack, explicit literal field targets, mode after or plain (including omitted default after), two required positional parameters, and a sole primitive literal return, optionally after a docstring. Before, wrap, serializer, unknown and composed validator contracts abstain.

Only contradictions with builtin scalar types, None, canonical Optional/Union and closed string Literal domains are proved. Numeric assignability preserves bool as int and int as float/complex. Opaque aliases, numeric Literal domains, containers and annotation graphs exceeding fixed budgets abstain.

Every targeted field must exist; unknown-field diagnostics belong to their existing owner. Multiple validators are excluded because a later validator can repair an intermediate value. One diagnostic identifies all contradictory fields for the returned literal.
Generated and vendor files are excluded; authored tests remain checked. No autofix changes validation phase, chooses domain values or narrows a public contract.
rules.rationale: Pydantic trusts the result of after and plain field validators without validating it against the field again. A correctly annotated validator can therefore store an integer in a string field while the model still promises a string to callers.
rules.remediation: Return a value satisfying every targeted field's stored contract. Split validators for different field domains, or perform input conversion in a before validator so the normal field validation follows it. Preserve intentional validation chains and wire serializers.
rules.summary: A terminal field validator must not return a literal contradicting its stored field type.

examples.title: Loguru captures the exception through opt
A standard logging argument does not capture the exception

limitations: Safe fixes handle only a direct proven Loguru logger call with literal arguments and keywords, replacing unused exc_info=True with opt(exception=True). Existing bind/opt chains, dynamic argument evaluation and commented calls remain review-only.
Only unambiguous Loguru imports and immediate bind/opt chains with literal exc_info=True are checked.
A literal message is required; templates using exc_info or the record, explicit exception capture, and exception() are excluded.
Unknown receivers, stored logger aliases, dynamic exc_info values, ambiguous imports, and generated files are excluded.
Runtime monkeypatches of Loguru objects or methods are not resolved.
An intentionally stored field can use a diagnostic-specific suppression. More complex logging context remains review-only.
rules.rationale: Loguru accepts logging keyword arguments as structured fields. The standard logging `exc_info=True` argument therefore does not attach an exception, leaving failure logs without their traceback.
rules.remediation: Use `logger.opt(exception=True)` or `logger.exception(...)` when reporting the active exception.
rules.summary: Loguru exc_info=True adds a field rather than retaining the exception traceback.

examples.title: Loguru leaves printf placeholders unchanged

limitations: Safe fixes handle direct proven logger calls with a brace-free literal message, matching argument count and exact native primitive values. Only simple %s/%r/%a and integer-literal %d/%i fields are converted; widths, numeric coercion, mappings, custom values and logger chains remain review-only.
Only unambiguous module-level Loguru imports and immediate bind/opt chains with a literal message and supplied positional formatting arguments are checked.

The decoded literal message must contain a valid percent conversion and no brace fields; Unicode and hex escapes preserve conversions. Escaped percent signs alone, malformed templates, dynamic messages and expanded arguments are excluded.
Standard logging, unknown receivers, stored aliases, shadowed or escaped imports, custom wrapper chains, keyword-only fields and generated files are excluded.
Visible namespace or logger mutations invalidate import proof. Interprocedural effects and runtime monkeypatches are not resolved.
Argument types and printf arity are not generally inferred. Only the explicitly proven primitive subset is fixed; other findings require formatting/structured-field review.
rules.rationale: Loguru formats messages with str.format rather than printf interpolation. A percent-style message with positional values keeps its placeholders and loses the values from the rendered diagnostic.
rules.remediation: Use Loguru brace fields with equivalent formatting, or retain diagnostic values as named structured fields. Review numeric, mapping and width specifications rather than mechanically replacing percent signs.
rules.summary: Use brace formatting for positional values passed to Loguru.

limitations: Only non-generated test paths and statically resolved unittest.mock constructors are analyzed.
The model's Pydantic ancestry and configured field data must be proven from source; application and SDK modules are never imported at runtime.
Model-method use, child callable invocation or behavior configuration, wrapped real instances, non-instance create_autospec calls, and doubles without configured model fields are excluded.
Unresolved model ancestry, ambiguous bindings, and indirect configuration beyond the supported provenance analysis are left unreported.
rules.rationale: Mocking a Pydantic value object bypasses validation, defaults, serialization, and field relationships. A specced mock still permits test data that the real model could never produce. Real model fixtures keep those contracts active while allowing services and external boundaries to remain mocked.
rules.remediation: Construct the real model, using a small typed factory for repeated valid defaults. Keep mock behavior at collaborator boundaries; a model method deliberately configured to raise remains a valid failure-injection test.
rules.summary: Build real Pydantic models when test doubles supply model field data.

examples.title: Build the replacement before changing it

limitations: Checks undecorated functions and methods with a direct builtin list/dict/set/tuple/frozenset return annotation, typed primitive mutable builtin container inputs, and assignments, returns, raises and structured if branches. Terminal paths must return a value or raise, with at least one value return. Returned container kinds and element types do not change borrowed input ownership.

Direct unshadowed builtin staticmethod/classmethod and canonical typing.final markers preserve the method body in plain class namespaces. Custom, patched, inherited or metaclass-prepared namespaces and multiple binding markers remain excluded.

Wildcard providers, type-parameter names that shadow builtin annotations, and method annotations in inherited, decorated or metaclass-prepared class namespaces do not prove builtin primitive ownership.

Tracks direct aliases and conditional-expression aliases with one proven borrowed owner, item writes/deletions, known builtin mutators and supported in-place operators. Rebinding to a fresh local builder ends the borrowed root's provenance.

Canonical source-resolved operator item writes/deletions and supported in-place functions are checked with positional arity and builtin kind contracts. Patched, escaped or ambiguous operator providers and unknown functional helpers are excluded.

Direct unshadowed builtin list/dict/set mutation descriptors and explicit mutating special methods use the same borrowed-target contract. Unknown classes, read methods and fresh local targets remain excluded.

Source-proven typing and typing_extensions cast/assert_type calls preserve borrowed identity. Two positional arguments are supported; cast also accepts its native typ/val keyword forms. Positional-only assert_type, duplicate/unknown arguments and opaque expansions are not guessed. Copying before the helper still ends borrowed provenance.

Branches retain only origins shared by every continuing path; uncertain joins lose provenance. Proven literal truth selects reachable statement/expression branches and respects boolean short-circuiting; return/raise paths stop flow. Eager comprehensions isolate target bindings; their outermost iterable uses the enclosing scope.
Boolean value selections preserve aliases only when every reachable result has one proven borrowed owner. Unknown conditions that can return unrelated values lose provenance.

Comprehension operands follow generator/filter order. Empty literal iterables and literal-false filters prevent later operands and bodies from being visited; effects in earlier operands remain checked.

Native collection literals supply truth facts for empty literals, explicit members and directly empty expansions. Contents are still evaluated; unknown spreads and application truth methods remain unresolved.

Literal primitive equality/order and singleton identity comparisons supply branch facts. Comparison chains stop before later operands after a proven false link; unknown application comparisons are never evaluated.

Synchronous generator expressions passed as the sole argument of a direct unshadowed native list/tuple/set/frozenset constructor are eagerly consumed and share comprehension flow. Other generator expressions evaluate only their outer iterable at creation; their bodies, filters and later iterables remain deferred, including asynchronous generators.
Local annotated assignments visit their value and evaluated target operands, not deferred annotation expressions; an annotation without a value does not perform an item write.

Chained assignment and deletion targets execute in order. Exact tuple/list literal destructuring captures right-side origins before binding targets in order; opaque, starred and mismatched destructuring remain excluded.
More than 32 nested branches, loops, try/context-manager orchestration, closures, assignment expressions, opaque type aliases, unknown receivers and dynamic namespaces are excluded.

Model-valued inputs and framework validators retain their existing rule owners. Mutation of nested descendants, receiver state, I/O and scalar command/result APIs are outside this rule's supported contract.
Generated and vendored sources are excluded; maintained tests are checked. No automatic copying, deletion, or command rewrite is offered.
rules.rationale: A container-valued transformation can change caller aliases before returning its result. Copying after the write leaves the original input changed.
rules.remediation: Copy each changed container before writing, return a fresh replacement, or expose a separate command returning None. Keep documented in-place contracts explicit; do not discard the operation or add a dummy assignment.
rules.summary: Return container replacements without mutating borrowed builtin inputs.

examples.title: Nested Config silently does not validate Settings.language

limitations: Only direct BaseModel or BaseSettings subclasses and validators directly owned by one nested class are inspected.
Nested classes with bases are excluded because inherited Pydantic fields cannot be resolved locally.
Intentional reusable validators with check_fields=False are excluded; Pydantic v1 validator syntax is supported.
Test and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: Pydantic collects validator metadata from the model class namespace. A decorator indented into a nested class is therefore invisible to the outer model, so its declared field silently loses validation.
rules.remediation: Move the field-validator method into the outer model class.
rules.summary: Outer-model Pydantic field validator is owned by a nested helper class.

examples.title: Omission silently selects an implementation

limitations: Warns for None-defaulted function parameters with a fallback used as a callable or a proven application-settings fallback; genuine absent state is allowed.

Constructor settings fallbacks remain owned by SARJ095; constructor nullability alone is not a defect. Decorated functions, tests, generated code, nested scope captures, non-callable object fallbacks, and interprocedural forwarding are excluded.

Callable use through a local assignment, annotation or None guard requires at most one body binding for that name and a call after the binding statement completes. Rebinding, deletion, imports, definitions, pattern or exception captures, global/nonlocal declarations and nested-scope bindings conservatively exclude that inference; direct inline calls remain independent. Settings provenance also excludes enclosing bindings and names written by a function declaring them global, while read-only global declarations remain valid.
No autofix: removing explicit None acceptance changes the callable contract, and moving a fallback can change initialization timing or error handling.
rules.rationale: A None dependency silently selects another implementation or ambient configuration, hiding wiring mistakes and adding unnecessary branches.
rules.remediation: Resolve the dependency at the call site and pass it explicitly; a concrete callable default is also valid when its lifetime is appropriate.
rules.summary: Require concrete function dependencies instead of resolving a None default inside the function.

examples.title: Page selected with an offset

limitations: Only SQL string literals, f-strings, and their static concatenations in recognized store modules are analyzed.
Only dynamic OFFSET values in credible SELECT queries are reported; fixed ordinal offsets are excluded.
Parenthesized arithmetic and common numeric wrappers such as GREATEST, LEAST, and COALESCE preserve the dynamic driver marker. Arbitrary SQL functions and procedural values remain opaque.
Generated files, migrations, docstrings, comments, quoted identifiers, and BigQuery `WITH OFFSET AS` array indexing are excluded.
ORM pagination APIs are outside this embedded-SQL rule.
rules.rationale: Dynamic offsets may require scanning discarded rows and may skip or repeat results during concurrent writes.
rules.remediation: Use a stable, immutable, unique ordering and a cursor predicate with the same direction; include a unique tie-breaker for non-unique sort columns. Keep OFFSET with a reasoned suppression for demonstrably bounded or static data, or an intentional random-access page contract.
rules.summary: Potentially unbounded `OFFSET` pagination in store SQL.

examples.title: Every declared literal belongs to the TypeIs target
TypeGuard permits an intentional partial predicate
Zero is still an integer in the false branch
Equality recognizes every member of a singleton target

examples.title: A value filter can return an ordinary bool
Truthiness can accept integers and reject the empty string

limitations: Checks undecorated, non-generic module functions with one parameter and one return, optionally after a docstring.
Requires an import-proven TypeIs target and a concrete builtin member demonstrably rejected by a direct predicate or by a builtin isinstance check followed by one predicate.
Targets are builtin int, str, bytes, bool and parameterized list, dict or set. Scalar comparisons use same-kind literals; length comparisons prove rejection of the valid empty member only.

Direct bool conversion rejects the valid falsey member. Unary not is checked only for scalar targets with an inhabited truthy member. Direct ordering or length comparisons require an exact matching builtin input annotation; equality comparisons use a concrete same-kind witness. Raw parameter returns are checked only when proven bool.

Also checks bounded, import-proven string Literal targets with exact builtin str or object input: a bool constant or equality/inequality comparison must reject an actual declared literal. Single-literal total equality predicates remain valid.

Input union analysis is iterative and bounded to 256 nodes. Constrained inputs, target unions, aliases, subclasses, custom refinements, helper calls, decorated functions and complex predicates are not inferred. TypeGuard may intentionally be partial and is excluded.
Visible shadowing, wildcard imports and namespace mutation abstain conservatively. There is no autofix because changing TypeIs affects both branches at callers.
Repeated top-level function definition names are excluded because overloads can expose a more constrained public input than the implementation annotation.
rules.rationale: TypeIs narrows both branches. A positive-int or non-empty-container filter can return false for a valid member of its target type, making callers incorrectly exclude that type in the false branch.
rules.remediation: Use an ordinary bool return for a value filter. Ensure every accepted value satisfies the declared target. Use TypeGuard for an intentional partial predicate only when its true branch is sound; TypeIs must recognize exactly the target values. Check false-branch callers when changing the narrowing contract.
rules.summary: TypeIs must not reject a value belonging to its declared target type.

examples.title: A returned record has a named row contract

limitations: Only import- or annotation-proven Psycopg cursors with a proven positional factory are inspected.
Direct fetch returns and unchanged local aliases are followed within one cursor context; iteration and helper-indirected flows are excluded.
Unknown, custom, inherited, or branch-dependent row factories are intentionally not inferred.
Test, generated, and migration files are excluded; exceptional record contracts require an exact suppression.
rules.rationale: Returning a tuple-shaped database record couples callers to selected-column order. A named row factory keeps the database boundary explicit; scalar and locally transformed results remain valid.
rules.remediation: For a returned record, use `row_factory=class_row(Model)` (prefer a validating model). Use `scalar_row` for scalar projections, or consume and transform a positional row inside the store.
rules.summary: A positional Psycopg record must not escape its function unchanged.

examples.title: Public function returns a positional record

limitations: Generated files and documentation examples are excluded.

Provenance-resolved builtin or typing fixed tuple return annotations with at least two slots are reported, including stable local aliases, quoted annotations, Annotated wrappers and optional unions in test helpers and fixtures; variadic tuples remain valid collections.

Existing direct tuple records remain errors; newly resolved typing_extensions providers, local aliases, application types named Unpack and optional-union records start as warnings for adoption review.

Classes with explicit bases, including object, are excluded without requiring an override decorator. Local base declarations do not prove runtime member ownership remains closed; class construction, native hooks and escaped handles can change inheritance. Independent module functions and plain classes remain eligible.
rules.rationale: A fixed tuple return makes callers remember positions and lets adjacent values be silently swapped. Named records preserve field meaning across public, private, decorated, method, and test boundaries.
rules.remediation: Return a frozen dataclass or validation model. Use `typing.NamedTuple` only when an exact tuple protocol is required.
rules.summary: Fixed tuple return records should use named fields instead of positional slots.

limitations: Safe fixes remove only proven inert standalone configuration assignments; proven inert constructor keywords are removed while preserving the constructor, binding and annotation. Commented and annotated configuration writes remain review-only.

Only non-generated test paths and stable local names unconditionally initialized from unittest.mock or an unshadowed pytest-mock fixture before configuration are analyzed. Dotted stores, auto-children, configured return-value chains, replacement or unpacked options, dynamic namespace access, and direct constructor-root or builtin namespace mutation are excluded. Unseen external mutations are not resolved.

Only same-block overwrites and exact-path terminal never-called assertions are checked; uncertain evaluation, native setter/iteration effects, custom hash/equality, control flow, reads, and terminal receiver escapes are excluded. Configuration values require literal/native primitive provenance.
rules.rationale: A mock behavior value is dead when a same-path write replaces it before observation, or when a terminal exact-path assertion proves the configured mock was never called.
rules.remediation: Delete the earlier inert configuration, retaining the mock constructor and binding when removing a keyword, or place the intended action before reconfiguration; delete behavior configuration contradicted by a terminal never-called assertion.
rules.summary: Remove mock behavior configuration proven unable to affect a test.

examples.title: Execute through an injected persistence owner

limitations: Only import-proven psycopg connection/cursor and psycopg_pool ConnectionPool or AsyncConnectionPool flows are classified. A free helper receiving an imported Cursor or AsyncCursor retains external execution ownership.

Straightforward constructor injection, connection and cursor context managers, aliases, rebindings, and conservative control-flow joins are followed. Mutated module namespaces and class-local annotation shadows abstain. Cursor parameters of class methods have unknown interprocedural ownership and do not establish an external execution origin.

Collected test modules, conftest.py, migrations, generated files, conventional operational-script roots, and literal SELECT 1 probes are excluded. Shared test-support helpers must use an injected owner.
rules.rationale: Free helpers and locally created clients can split query and transaction ownership across unrelated call sites, making persistence behavior harder to change consistently.
rules.remediation: Move the operation behind a store, repository, or narrow transaction owner that receives its Psycopg pool or connection through the constructor. Use an exact SARJ415 suppression when direct execution is the deliberate behavior under test.
rules.summary: Psycopg execution occurs outside a constructor-injected persistence owner.

limitations: A literal module-level __test__ = False disables pytest collection. Later bindings in eager module expressions or explicitly global class scopes clear that proof; class-local names, deferred bodies, and annotation-only names do not rebind it.
The rule recognizes source-like suffixes, shell templates ending in .sh.tftpl, and the exact Dockerfile basename; it follows local aliases, context-managed reads, and common normalization.

Direct generator/list-comprehension reads unpacked from stable module-level path tuples are followed; mutable collections, rebinding, filtered comprehensions, and interprocedural flows remain unreported.
Literal shebang startswith checks are representation contracts and remain unreported; other text compatibility sentinels require an exact suppression.
Files produced beneath recognized temporary-directory fixtures are generated artifacts, not repository source, and remain unreported.
Paths beneath fixture, golden, and snapshot directories are treated as deliberate representation contracts and remain unreported.
When raw representation is genuinely the contract (for example a golden or compatibility sentinel), use an exact line suppression with the reason.

Lambda bodies and unconsumed generators are separate scopes. Proven builtin all/any consumption follows generator and comprehension bindings; pattern captures clear prior source provenance. Empty literal iterations and literal false filters are not treated as source oracles.

Exact byte-copy checks against proven temporary outputs, and same-path byte preservation after a visible named write_bytes value, are representation contracts. Local value/path rebinding, intervening path writes, and conditional writes invalidate that proof; equality to fixed repository-source bytes still requires an exact suppression.
rules.rationale: Substring and regex checks can pass on comments or unreachable configuration and fail after behavior-preserving formatting changes.
rules.remediation: Parse the artifact, execute its validator, or assert on a runtime contract. If exact bytes or text are the deliberate compatibility contract, use an exact line suppression with the reason.
rules.summary: Test uses raw text from a source-like project path as its oracle.

Unknown free-function calls retain possible persistence effects and abstain. Source-proven Pydantic constructors, plain dataclass constructors, native NewType wrappers and unshadowed builtin value conversions are recognized as value construction for this advice; their validation hooks are not claimed to be runtime-pure.

Class names do not trigger the rule. Imported bases need the prepared project source graph. Unknown bases, SQL-backed stores, delegated spies, unrelated call recorders, dynamic collections and unsupported inheritance remain outside scope. One warning is emitted per recording implementation, with no automatic rewrite.
rules.rationale: An in-memory store double proves that a method was called but bypasses SQL, constraints, transactions and concurrency behavior. It can accept operations the real store rejects.
rules.remediation: Inject the real PostgreSQL store with an isolated database fixture and assert persisted state. Keep operational observability around real persistence rather than replacing persistence with an appended call list.
rules.summary: Use the PostgreSQL store in tests instead of a recording-only store implementation.

limitations: Only unannotated, single-target `alias = original` assignments with one binding and one read at `alias=alias` are checked.
The original must be a parameter or an earlier initialized local with one binding; reassignment, deletion, imports, alias chains and uncertain initialization are excluded.

Completed function-body if prefixes and their Boolean tests are supported only before a fresh, uniquely initialized local and alias in that same body. Parameters, earlier source bindings and aliases nested in with bodies after such prefixes are excluded.

Loops, try statements, asserts, other Boolean short-circuiting, nested scopes, global/nonlocal declarations and type aliases are excluded. Ordinary and async with bodies require ordered enclosing-suite binding evidence.
A conditional expression is admitted only when its test is a bare name bound once as a parameter, and neither local is read within the expression.
Typed aliases, files with type comments, same-scope quoted references and conditional reads of either local are excluded. Captured bindings and module/class aliases are preserved.
Aliases read inside template interpolations are preserved because templates expose expression text. This conservatively also excludes reads used only in format specifications.

Files with wildcard imports, Pydantic imports or references to known namespace readers, dynamic attribute getters or reference-count observers are excluded. Wildcard exports cannot establish builtin identity; computed type names can consume caller-local bindings without a Name read in the AST.
Dynamic class construction and class-valued references to type are excluded. Direct, unshadowed unary type(value) queries and standard-library dataclasses remain supported.
Generated source, stubs and malformed input are excluded; files must compile with normal module execution flags. Arbitrary external frame introspection is not modeled.

Native diagnostic fixes are limited to undecorated module functions with one required parameter, an optional existing docstring, a clean single-line alias and a tail return of unshadowed builtin dict with exactly the matching keyword. Recorded dict bindings, visible attribute/subscript writes, setter, mapping-mutator, ior, methodcaller or patch references, unittest imports, `|=` assignments, comments, non-UTF8 encodings, type parameters and visible function, frame or coroutine code-object inspection prevent fixes. Mutation guards also exclude unrelated ordinary mappings, nonmutating methodcaller uses, harmless unittest imports and integer `|=` assignments. Other calls remain diagnostic-only; arbitrary external tracing, reflection and monkeypatching are not modeled.

The central fixer also retains its separate closed nested private one-parameter helper profile: the whole body forwards one unannotated alias into a returned canonical builtin dict. Its closed-call, comment, annotation, escape, builtin and metadata-observation guards remain independent of native diagnostic fixes; a finding is edited through only one validated path.
Readability judgments, multiple reads, positional forwarding and more complex control flow remain outside the contract.
rules.rationale: An extra local binding makes readers trace two names for one value when the keyword already communicates its role.
rules.remediation: Apply the safe fix where offered; otherwise pass the original local to the matching keyword and remove the unannotated alias after review.
rules.summary: Remove a local alias used only for its matching keyword argument.

limitations: Public-to-private name aliases are checked only as direct module-body assignments; assignments through an unconditional, unshadowed stdlib `sys` import include module-level control flow.
Aliases inside module control flow, functions, classes, and `TYPE_CHECKING` branches are excluded.
Private targets, dunder sources, attribute values, destructuring, imports, and same-visibility aliases are excluded.
Literal-key registrations, child-module registrations, method calls, reads, and arbitrary registries are excluded.
Generated source, malformed source, and stub files (`.pyi`) are outside this rule's scope.
No autofix is offered because the intended compatibility surface and identity requirements need review.
rules.rationale: Binding a public name to a private implementation creates two names for one API and disguises the intended visibility boundary. Replacing the current module similarly mutates import identity at runtime in a way static tools cannot model. Both forms make navigation, introspection, and compatibility ownership surprising.
rules.remediation: Define maintained APIs under their public names and update local callers directly. Import the canonical path inside maintained code. If a compatibility module is still required, expose its supported names with explicit same-name imports grouped by source module. Preserve a required compatibility or module-identity contract with a reasoned exact suppression rather than renaming automatically.
rules.summary: Do not manufacture public APIs from private names or replace the current module.

limitations: Checks parsed PostgreSQL queries in proven psycopg SQL constructors and execution contexts. Generated sources, comments, malformed statements, opaque dynamic SQL and unrelated strings are excluded.

Only table self-aliases without alias column lists and bare-column output self-aliases are checked. Identifier folding follows PostgreSQL UTF-8 ASCII case rules. Casts, computed expressions, CTE aliases, different role names and quoted identifier case retain their contract. No automatic edit changes formatting, comments or query composition.
The finding is emitted once per SQL expression even when it contains several redundant aliases. It does not infer that different relation names belong to the same model.
rules.rationale: A self-alias adds syntax without naming a distinct role or result field. It obscures useful aliases among repeated names.
rules.remediation: Remove an alias whose PostgreSQL identifier equals the original table or bare column name. Keep role aliases for self joins, renamed outputs, quoted case distinctions and alias column lists.

limitations: Autofix only reuses one existing stable enclosing local literal binding for an entire repeated group of exact builtin len(literal) calls in closed private nested ordinary synchronous nongenerator helpers. An already-authored closed helper must read that binding through len; the correction introduces no names or module lookups and exposes no string identity.

Containing callables require proven inert execution and no frame/metadata/namespace escapes, comments or type parameters. Reassigned, shadowed, conditional, competing or module bindings, unknown callouts, reachable exceptions and groups with any other use remain manual.
Only exact same-file literals of at least 40 characters repeated across distinct callable scopes are compared; near-duplicates are not detected.
Cross-scope findings require credible SQL or an absolute route; identifier-like strings require an existing unique module constant.
Prose, documentation scaffolding, annotations, tests, migrations, examples, generated files, match patterns, and f-string fragments are excluded.
rules.rationale: When exact copies represent one SQL, route, or protocol contract, editing one copy can silently diverge the others. Identical text can also represent independent concepts, so this rule is advisory.
rules.remediation: If the occurrences are one maintained concept, reuse an existing constant or extract a descriptive module-level constant within that ownership boundary. If equality is intentional but ownership is independent, suppress with a rationale.
rules.summary: Exact SQL or route literals repeated across callable scopes should share one named binding.

examples.title: Do not repeat probabilistic trials without reproducibility

limitations: Only standard-library `random` calls in potentially repeated loop or comprehension regions in default-collected test modules and callables are checked.
Single draws, injected RNG objects, Hypothesis tests, and cryptographic randomness are excluded.
Only a statically deterministic, unconditional seed before the repeated sample suppresses the finding; fixture, plugin, and interprocedural seeding are not inferred.
rules.rationale: Repeated unseeded sampling creates unreproducible generated inputs, making failures harder to replay and debug when sampled values affect behavior.
rules.remediation: Use an isolated deterministic generator such as `rng = random.Random(17)`, inject one, or use a property framework that records failing seeds.
rules.summary: A collected test may repeatedly sample an unseeded standard-library PRNG.

examples.title: Description adds behavior not present in the schema

limitations: Safe fixes remove only the description keyword of a comment-free, error-level inert Field call whose entire literal description repeats the complete declared domain. Schema-ownership warnings remain review-only.
Only direct fields on classes with a direct BaseModel base are inspected.
Domains are resolved only from direct string Literals and static Literal aliases or string-valued Enums in the same module.
Descriptions are reported only when a narrow clause repeats the complete domain without mapping or rationale.
ERROR requires an inert direct model with no json_schema_extra options; custom construction, schema metadata, local aliases and Enum annotations retain WARNING with schema-ownership review guidance.
Test and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: Pydantic already publishes literal and enum domains in JSON Schema; duplicate must-be prose can contradict the generated contract after a value changes.
rules.remediation: Remove only the repeated value list. Preserve guidance about when to use each value, UX labels, examples, deprecation, or rationale not encoded by the field type.
rules.summary: Do not restate a string Literal or local string Enum domain in its Pydantic description.

examples.title: Comment adds operational context

limitations: Safe fixes remove only a standalone comment whose complete plain-word sequence exactly matches the next single-line direct call identifier, ignoring case and a final period only. Stem matches, omitted words, labels, directives and other prose remain review-only; blank line count is preserved.
Detection uses conservative lexical heuristics for short standalone comments above simple actions.
Generated files, directives, protected comments, section labels, and comments adding novel context are excluded.
rules.rationale: When a comment adds no rationale, scope, ordering, or constraint, it duplicates code and can become stale. Preserve comments that add a constraint or rationale rather than restating identifiers.
rules.remediation: Delete it if it merely narrates one statement. Preserve or rewrite comments that explain a reason, constraint, consequence, ordering requirement, or meaningful region label.
rules.summary: Short standalone comment lexically restates the immediately following simple action.

limitations: Only statically recoverable SQL strings in credible query assignments or execution/composition calls in production source files are analyzed.
Dynamic SQL and SQLAlchemy expression trees are not analyzed; bounded CTE wildcards may require a documented suppression.

Autofix only expands a complete single-row integer VALUES query with authored quoted column names, directly consumed by a fresh default psycopg Connection in a closed source-owned function. Other projections remain manual.

examples.title: Native syntax preserves the existing ownership contract
Existing semantic ownership exclusions remain valid
A settings type remains a passive record
A settings-named class calls injected persistence

limitations: Only direct module classes named *Settings, *Config, *Configuration, or *Options are checked.

A finding requires a typed collaborator field and an ordinary public method that calls that field; pure computations, properties, validators, serializers, factories, generated files, and tests are excluded. Nested scopes, containers of collaborators, class objects, and methods that rebind self are not inferred.
The rule does not require every data object to use a particular record library and does not infer behavior from a filename alone.
rules.rationale: A class named as settings or configuration promises passive data. Calling injected stores, clients, or services from that object hides orchestration behind a data boundary and couples configuration construction to runtime behavior.
rules.remediation: Move collaborator calls into a service, coordinator, or compiler with an honest behavioral name; keep the settings/configuration object as a TypedDict, Pydantic model, attrs class, or dataclass.

examples.title: Unchecked keys retain their object type
A container check does not prove string keys

limitations: Checks top-level, undecorated, non-generic synchronous functions with one positional parameter proven to be builtin object and a single return isinstance(parameter, builtin_container), optionally after a docstring.
Repeated module-level function names abstain: an overload's public input contract can be narrower than the implementation annotation.
The TypeGuard or TypeIs target must be a matching builtin dict, list, or set whose slots all resolve to object, str, int, bool, float, or bytes; at least one slot must be narrower than object.

Includes authored tests; generated and vendor source is excluded. String annotations, constrained input types, unions, Any, TypeVars, Protocols, assignment aliases, nested definitions, and content validators are not inferred.

Annotation imports include TYPE_CHECKING imports. Runtime imports use conservative file-wide shadow facts, so unrelated local rebinding can cause false negatives. Wildcard imports, explicit writes to relevant builtin or typing attributes, and exception, pattern or walrus bindings that shadow relevant names or imported aliases exclude the file; dynamic namespace mutation is not inferred.
Relative or conditional imports that replace relevant builtin or typing names exclude the file unless the import proves the same canonical symbol. Unrelated relative imports remain in scope.
No autofix: widening the return contract can require caller changes, while adding content validation changes behavior and cost.

Visible __builtins__ access, canonical namespace-capability imports, module-class changes, and escaping typing/builtins module aliases abstain because namespace mutation can change the meaning of the check.

Canonical native builtin function objects outside direct calls also abstain: captured, passed, or introspected function values can expose the mutable builtin namespace. The explicit native-function inventory covers CPython 3.14 and 3.15; unrelated application methods remain in scope, and arbitrary external effects are not inferred.

Known native function names and canonical imported aliases remain possible namespace capabilities when shadowing or later rebinding obscures their identity. This conservatively excludes some benign first-class application variables with builtin function names.
Direct __lazy_import__ calls and canonical aliases also abstain: CPython 3.15 introduces lazy imports that can return mutable module namespaces.
rules.rationale: TypeGuard and TypeIs let callers trust their declared narrowing. Checking only dict, list, or set does not validate keys, values, or elements, so callers can perform operations that fail at runtime.
rules.remediation: Use object for unchecked container slots, or validate their contents when the narrower contract is required. Keep constrained input types that already prove the contents.
rules.summary: Do not claim typed container contents from a container-only type guard.

examples.title: Unchecked contents retain a container contract
Check the actual named tuple class for nominal membership
Tuple membership does not establish a named record
A dictionary check does not prove a required key

limitations: Checks unique, undecorated, non-generic module functions with one object parameter and a sole direct builtin isinstance check of that same parameter, optionally after a docstring.

Targets must be stable, unescaped local class declarations directly inheriting import-proven typing or typing_extensions TypedDict or NamedTuple. TypedDict targets need a required key; every NamedTuple target promises its nominal record API. Inheritance, class decorators, methods, aliases, imported targets and opaque field annotations abstain.

TypedDict total=False and NotRequired-only declarations are preserved. Canonical Required and ReadOnly wrappers are recognized; unknown class options and computed requiredness abstain. NamedTuple constructor defaults do not make named attributes optional, and even zero-field records promise methods absent from plain tuple.

Only bounded builtin and canonical typing field annotations with literal metadata are analyzed. Class-scope shadows, record rebinding, namespace mutation or escape, and repeated function names abstain conservatively.

Constrained input types, public overload contracts, content validators and helpers are not inferred. This rule proves missing shape; it does not claim that key presence alone validates field contents.
Authored tests remain checked; generated and vendor files are excluded. No autofix invents validation or changes narrowing at callers.
rules.rationale: An empty dict or tuple passes a container-only check while lacking a TypedDict's required key or a NamedTuple's named attributes and record API. A guard annotation makes callers trust that missing contract.
rules.remediation: Validate the required record shape and field contracts, or keep an honest container return type. For a NamedTuple, checking its actual class can establish nominal membership; tuple membership alone cannot.
rules.summary: Do not promise a local record's contract from a container-only check.

limitations: Detection covers truthy scalar constants, definitely non-empty list/set/dict displays, and directly asserted or locally bound generator expressions and lambdas.
Generator consumption, lambda invocation, comprehensions, and runtime iterator/callable values are not inferred; empty universal-quantification contracts remain valid.
Test-local immutable scalar bindings and their aliases are tracked only through straight-line assignments; calls, control flow, mutable values, and global/nonlocal writes invalidate tracking.

Locally created generator/lambda objects and aliases are tracked for truthiness only; their creation clears earlier setup facts, and comparisons, consumption, invocation, and runtime-created iterators/callables are not inferred.

Pure Boolean conditions, compatible numeric/string/bytes ordering and chained comparisons over known scalar setup are evaluated; proven-true pure assertions retain bindings because their messages do not execute.
Ruff owns asserted strings and tuples, literal comparisons and identity, and unittest-style assertion methods.
Generated files, always-failing assertions, deliberate match-arm success markers, and runtime-value comparisons are excluded.
rules.rationale: A condition that stays truthy whenever evaluation succeeds cannot reject an incorrect result and often means the intended condition was wrapped in a container, deferred without execution, or placed in the message slot.
rules.remediation: Assert an explicit runtime-derived condition. If the test only requires an operation not to raise, evaluate it directly and retain any meaningful follow-up assertion. String accumulator grown on every iteration

limitations: Autofix only handles a private nested ordinary synchronous nongenerator helper with closed direct callers, no known frame/metadata capabilities or comments, and exactly empty-string initialization, one literal loop, and return. The loop must append its exact-string item to that accumulator and contain at least two nonempty string literals; existing names, loop order, and fresh final-string identity are preserved with list append and join.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.
The rule requires syntax that establishes string-like growth and excludes generated files.
Subscript targets, per-iteration reinitialization, and intermediate values consumed by the loop are excluded.
rules.rationale: Repeated immutable-string growth can copy the accumulated value on each iteration and become quadratic.
rules.remediation: Collect fragments and join once, or use `io.StringIO` when incremental writes are required.
rules.summary: Avoid repeatedly growing a proven string accumulator across a loop backedge.

examples.title: Cleanup preserves cancellation
Cancellation becomes a successful return

limitations: Only explicit, import-proven asyncio.CancelledError handlers in async functions are inspected; broad handlers, contextlib.suppress, tests, support fixtures, and generated files are excluded.

Only straight-line handlers with a return or normal fallthrough are reported. Compound handlers, re-raising, and translated exceptions are excluded. Any attribute call named uncancel is conservatively excluded without proving its receiver, so unrelated methods can hide a finding.

A single-name task created by asyncio.create_task, immediately cancelled before a try that only awaits it, is intentionally excluded as child cleanup; this does not prove concurrent caller cancellation cannot occur.
Try statements with control-transferring or compound finalizers are excluded, including handlers nested beneath them. Runtime helper effects and interprocedural task ownership are not inferred.
Only a try body consisting of one awaited, unmodified canonical asyncio.sleep call with literal arguments is blocking. Unresolved operations and child cancellation remain advisory.
rules.rationale: Returning or falling through after catching CancelledError can make cancelled work look successful and interfere with task groups and timeout shutdown. Child cancellation must be distinguished from cancellation of the caller.
rules.remediation: Re-raise after cleanup. If child cancellation is an expected result, first propagate cancellation when asyncio.current_task().cancelling() is nonzero. Use an exact suppression for a documented boundary that deliberately consumes cancellation.
rules.summary: Preserve cancellation when an async operation is cancelled.

examples.title: A test replaces a mock's resolved collaborator method
Configure behavior through an existing mock method

limitations: Only non-generated test paths are analyzed; a destination method and replacement callable must have statically resolved provenance.
Inference uses source declarations and conservative constructor, annotation, fixture, and helper relationships; it never imports application or SDK code at runtime.
Data fields, callable-valued fields, mock configuration attributes, whole-object fake injection, and scoped patch calls are excluded.
Wrappers visibly forwarding a captured original of the same receiver and member, and matching saved-original restorations in finally, are excluded.
Unknown types, ambiguous bindings, unresolved decorators or inheritance, and dynamically chosen members are left unreported; canonical typing.final class decorators are transparent.
rules.rationale: Grafting a function onto a collaborator or mock hides the boundary's callable contract and bypasses the mock's call and await records. An injected fake makes behavior explicit; configuring an existing contract-aware mock preserves its observation API. Scoped patches also restore real objects reliably.
rules.remediation: Inject a concrete fake or configure the existing autospecced mock method's return_value or side_effect. Preserve the real method's synchronous or asynchronous contract, including synchronous awaitable returns. Explain other intentional runtime interception with an exact-code local suppression.
rules.summary: Avoid assigning replacement implementations directly onto resolved methods in tests.

STALE_TIME = timedelta(minutes=5)

examples.title: Typed value carries the unit

limitations: Safe fixes remove only an exact number-and-unit comment on a direct nonnegative numeric literal assignment when the existing name has exactly that same unit suffix and the numeric values agree. Arithmetic, conversion, conflicting or missing units, aliases and explanatory prose remain review-only; executable code and line endings are retained.
Detection targets one-line numeric assignments with one simple name or attribute target and a trailing comment that repeats one number and unit.

Calls, returns, loops, assertions, chained or destructured assignments, multi-number comments, approximate conversions, reasons, references, directives, bracketed values, invalid syntax, and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: A unit encoded only in a comment can drift; a unit-bearing name makes it machine- and reviewer-visible, while a duration type can enforce it.
rules.remediation: Encode or reconcile the unit in the assigned name or typed value, such as timeout_ms or timedelta(minutes=5), then delete the duplicate comment.
rules.summary: A trailing comment redundantly labels a numeric assignment with its value and unit.

examples.title: Unique constraint selected from error text
Unique constraint selected from structured diagnostics

limitations: The rule recognizes import-proven psycopg/psycopg2 UniqueViolation and asyncpg UniqueViolationError handlers whose translating branch matches direct or single-assignment rendered-message data.
Generic IntegrityError handlers, driver wrappers, branch-ambiguous aliases, and interprocedural message helpers remain outside its scope.
Tests and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: Database error text is localized and can change with driver or server versions; supported PostgreSQL drivers expose the violated constraint as structured diagnostic data.
rules.remediation: Compare the driver's structured constraint field: `exc.diag.constraint_name` for psycopg or `exc.constraint_name` for asyncpg. SQLSTATE 23505 identifies the violation category, not the constraint.
rules.summary: Do not make unique-violation control flow depend on rendered exception text.

examples.title: Decorator names the declared field
Decorator targets a field the model does not declare

limitations: Only direct module-level BaseModel subclasses with a static namespace and resolved field decorators are inspected.
Unknown inheritance, computed fields, custom decorators, overwritten methods, wildcard fields and uncertain check_fields are excluded.
Visible namespace APIs, dynamic module access, ambiguous imports and escaped or mutated imported objects exclude the file.
One diagnostic is emitted per decorator even if several field targets are missing.
rules.rationale: A field validator or serializer naming a missing field prevents the model from being constructed.
rules.remediation: Use the declared field name, or explicitly set check_fields=False for a validator intended for subclass fields.
rules.summary: Pydantic field decorators must target declared fields.

examples.title: A module description consumed at runtime is retained
A wrapper excluding __doc__ does not consume input prose

limitations: Safe fixes delete standalone module docstrings with no detected consumer, dynamic namespace access or frame/metadata observation. Legal notices, adjacent string expressions, trailing comments and same-line code prevent deletion. A docstring-only module may become empty.

Function fixes require a second native error-level exact-name-restatement finding on an unescaped private nested synchronous nongenerator function. All references must be direct calls; public callable APIs, classes, behavioral function prose, escapes and metadata consumers remain review-only. Known frame and metadata capabilities, their import aliases and metadata field access prevent fixes.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.

Generated files, doctests, syntax-required function stub bodies, schema classes, framework decorators, explicit __doc__/help/getdoc consumers, canonical metadata-copy decorators, and local sarj-noqa suppressions are excluded.

Ordinary class prose is checked even when it is the entire body or dataclass retains it as incidental metadata. Replace an otherwise empty class body with pass; explicit documentation consumers and schema descriptions remain protected.
The rule is intentionally default-deny: public API documentation without mechanically visible consumption needs an auditable SARJ420 suppression.
Dynamic Click or Typer decorator options are conservatively treated as possible help consumers; explicit non-None help leaves the docstring eligible.

Source-proven direct decorators returning a wraps-decorated wrapper consume only their input doc; factory and wrapper implementation prose remain eligible. Unknown assigned/updated options, shadowed bindings, lazy outer factories, opaque wrapper headers, and unresolved imports do not prove metadata consumption.
rules.rationale: A docstring with no detected consumer makes code depend on prose for ordinary meaning and creates a second maintenance surface that agents expand and maintainers must review.
rules.remediation: Delete the docstring. If author-controlled code is unclear without it, clarify names, types, and structure or extract a small named helper. Keep a genuinely hidden invariant as one concise local comment. When external tooling consumes __doc__, use an exact SARJ420 suppression that names the consumer.
rules.summary: No docstring consumer detected — delete it; make author-controlled names, types, and structure explain the code.

limitations: Import-resolved pytest.raises blocks consume copy operations as exception assertions and are excluded.

Arbitrary copy/replace methods, shadowed imports, Pydantic method or copy-hook overrides, and unknown receivers are excluded.
Assignments, returns, and passing the result to another call consume the result and are not reported. Copy hooks can run user code, so no deletion or assignment autofix is offered.
Generated/vendor sources are excluded; maintained tests are checked.
rules.rationale: Copy-on-write replacement APIs return another value rather than updating the original. Discarding their result can silently leave subsequent operations using unchanged data.
rules.remediation: Assign, return, or otherwise consume the replacement. A copy hook intentionally exercised for its effects or exceptions can use a narrow suppression; do not automatically delete the call.
rules.summary: Use the replacement returned by a resolved copy API.

examples.title: The callable exposes only inputs it uses

limitations: Safe fixes remove unannotated bool/None-default keyword-only inputs only from private unescaped nested synchronous nongenerator helpers with proven direct callers, updating only bool/None literal caller keywords. Module/public/callback contracts, type parameters, comments, reflection, annotations, expanded calls and effectful values remain review-only; native severities are unchanged. Known frame and metadata capabilities, their import aliases and metadata field access prevent fixes.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.

ERROR is limited to private synchronous module functions with proven direct callers, no dynamic namespace or variadic/decorated contract, inert builtin bool/None annotations or no annotation, and bool/None defaults and supplied values. Public, method, callback, required-slot and effectful signature/argument cases retain WARNING.
Only underscore-prefixed keyword-only declarations are checked; positional and variadic callback slots are excluded.
Decorated functions other than unshadowed builtin staticmethod/classmethod, inherited methods, and intentional stubs are excluded.
Any reference within the body counts as use, including nested scopes; shadowing and reassignment can produce false negatives.
Functions accessing locals, vars, eval, or exec through recognized builtin bindings are excluded.
Callables referenced as values are excluded because their external keyword contract is unknown. Lambda parameters, unknown dynamic reflection, and cross-module callback contracts are not resolved.
Generated and vendored files are excluded; test source is checked.
rules.rationale: A keyword-only parameter requires callers to use its declared name. Prefixing an unused input with an underscore silences unused-argument lint while retaining an input whose value has no effect. Removing the dead input and its callers keeps the callable's interface honest.
rules.remediation: Remove the unused keyword-only parameter and update callers together. If an external contract requires the input, preserve its required spelling and use a narrow, reasoned unused-argument suppression. Do not erase a precise callback signature with **kwargs or add dummy reads to silence this warning.
rules.summary: Remove unused underscore-prefixed keyword-only parameters instead of hiding them from lint.

examples.title: Keep a conventional placeholder inside unpacking

limitations: Safe fixes remove only primitive literal markers directly in function bodies, inserting pass when necessary. Calls, parameters, resource retention, chained assignments and annotations remain review-only.
Plain and annotated assignments whose standalone target is `_` are reported, including chained assignments.
Formal-parameter references are reported too, including positional, keyword-only, and variadic parameters.
Unpacking placeholders, loop targets, wildcard imports, and underscore-prefixed names are excluded.
A binding read in the same enclosing scope is not a discard. Reads in nested scopes conservatively preserve it, even when shadowing cannot be resolved.
Generated and vendored files are excluded.
rules.rationale: A standalone `_ = value` assignment adds a binding without clarifying intent. A side-effecting call can be invoked directly. Reading unused parameters only to satisfy a linter hides whether a callback is intentionally inert or implements an incomplete contract.
rules.remediation: Invoke calls directly when their result needs no retention. When a result owns a lease or resource lifetime, retain it under an informative name such as `_retained_lease`; do not drop it. Remove or rename locally owned unused values; when an external interface requires the exact unused parameter, put a narrow reasoned linter suppression on its declaration. Use an explicit empty body for an intentional stub, `@override` for a real override, or `NotImplementedError` for an unsupported operation; preserve required keyword names.
rules.summary: Do not use standalone assignments to `_` to discard values.

Ordinary scoped directives must be attached to code; recognized Ruff and Flake8 file directives may stand alone.
Generated-source markers do not waive this check. Generated/vendor boundaries belong in explicit whole-path exclusions.
rules.rationale: Generic reasons satisfy review conventions without making the suppressed risk auditable or removable.
rules.remediation: Name the concrete tool mismatch or safety invariant and the condition that would allow removal. Cite an upstream issue or affected version when that is the durable boundary.
rules.summary: Suppressions need a concrete description of the exception.

rules.rationale: Request and response bodies often contain personal, financial, or echoed authentication data, while log sinks commonly have broader readership and longer retention.
rules.remediation: Log explicit non-sensitive metadata such as request IDs, response status, counts, or a deliberately sanitized summary. Suppress with a rationale when the payload type is proven public and bounded.

examples.title: The retry is a POST

limitations: Only literal route paths on a FastAPI or APIRouter receiver created in the same file are checked.
The final path segment is read; its first word (split on '-', '_' or '.') must be run, trigger, send, dispatch, execute, launch, enqueue or retry. Plural nouns such as runs are accepted.
A GET that dispatches work under any other name is not detected. Tests and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: GET must be safe. A GET that dispatches work can be fired cross-site by an image tag or link prefetch, bypasses CSRF protection, and is retried freely by proxies and clients.
rules.remediation: Change the operation to POST and keep GET for reads.
rules.summary: GET routes must not end in a work verb such as run, send, trigger or retry.

examples.title: Dictionary cases have stable names

limitations: Only import-proven pytest parametrization over static list or tuple tables in maintained test files is analyzed.
Cases with a pytest-readable scalar column or a statically non-None explicit ID are allowed.
Dynamic and callable IDs and repository-level pytest_make_parametrize_id hooks are not evaluated.
rules.rationale: Without a semantic naming owner, fallback IDs such as `payload0` are hard to diagnose and silently change when the table is reordered.
rules.remediation: Check the owning pytest_make_parametrize_id hook before adding IDs; reuse an existing semantic naming owner. Otherwise give each opaque row a semantic `pytest.param(..., id=...)`, or use a semantic callable `ids=` when one mapping applies to the entire table.
rules.summary: Opaque static pytest parameter cases lack table-local semantic IDs.

examples.title: Component test keeps one external boundary
Test patches six collaborators

limitations: Only maintained, collected tests are analyzed; generated files and nested lexical scopes are excluded.
The warning counts independently rooted doubles and inferred collaborator owners, including mock-named fixtures.
Class-level patches, configuration and process-state knobs, and identified composition-root or documentation harnesses are excluded.
rules.rationale: Broad double setup obscures the behavior under test and often couples tests to implementation wiring.
rules.remediation: Prefer real in-process dependencies, a component harness, or purpose-built fakes; keep mocks at true external boundaries.
rules.summary: Tests should not use more than five independently rooted test doubles or collaborator substitutions.
