examples.title: A self join does not prove distinct model ownership

limitations: An architecture review warning, not a claim that SQL joins are inherently incorrect or slow. Distinct literal PostgreSQL relations are a source-visible proxy for ownership; syntax cannot establish whether two relations represent the same domain model.

Checks native Psycopg execution and direct same-class query-forwarding wrappers in non-test Python. Each SELECT block needs at least two different direct table relations joined in that block. Self joins, CTE references, derived relations, table-valued functions, dynamic relation names, schema-ambiguous qualification and unsupported SQL abstain.

Ordinary explicit JOINs, comma joins and lateral modifiers over direct relations remain reviewable. A join to a CTE does not borrow its underlying relation as a direct model boundary. One warning is emitted per authored SQL expression; no automatic rewrite moves transaction or locking boundaries.
rules.rationale: A SQL join across separate persistence relations couples their read representations and can bypass the owning store's access and conversion policy. This architecture prefers bounded store reads and typed application composition when their consistency contract permits it.
rules.remediation: Review the relation owners, then load the related records through their typed stores, batch by IDs and compose them in application code. Preserve tenant filters, null-extension, cardinality, snapshot consistency, authorization and FOR UPDATE locks. Keep an explained exception for an atomic database operation; replacing a join with unrelated reads can change behavior or introduce N+1 queries.
rules.summary: Compose distinct model records in application code instead of a cross-model SQL join.

examples.title: Autospec checks the function call shape
A function spec leaves invocation permissive

limitations: Only authored test files, proven unittest.mock constructors, earlier undecorated non-generic module-local function specs without **kwargs, and unconditional simple mock assignments are analyzed.

Requires a stable binding and at least one direct call with explicit keywords in the same scope. Escapes, aliases, rebinding, dynamic argument unpacking, wildcard imports and reflective namespace mutation are excluded.

Imported functions, class or descriptor specs, wrapping, side effects and uncertain configuration are excluded. AsyncMock requires an async function spec so autospec preserves awaiting. Import and function shadow checks, including exception/pattern captures and importer-root walrus/global writes, are conservative across the file. Proven builtins reflection aliases are excluded.
Exact call-shape assertions such as assert_called_once_with can already validate a spec's signature; this policy requires validation during invocation. Autospec does not enforce argument value types.
Passing autospec=True to a Mock constructor merely configures an attribute; it does not activate autospeccing. Use create_autospec instead.
Specs whose function objects escape to aliases, helpers, or attribute access are excluded so altered signatures and descriptor metadata remain explicit contracts. No autofix is offered.
rules.rationale: Mock, MagicMock and AsyncMock with spec or spec_set allow incompatible arguments during invocation. Tests that assert only results or call counts can therefore accept a misspelled keyword or stale call shape.
rules.remediation: Use create_autospec(function, spec_set=True), preserving configured results. An async function produces an awaitable mock whose signature is checked when awaited. Retain a reasoned local exception for a deliberately permissive double.
rules.summary: Prefer autospec for specced function mocks called with explicit keywords.

examples.title: Collect writes for an available bulk command

limitations: Only a synchronous for loop containing one discarded upsert call is considered. Its receiver must resolve to a typed parameter or a constructor-injected attribute with source-declared compatible upsert/upsert_many methods.

Signatures must have one required command argument and matching scalar/collection input and output types, including equivalent quoted annotations. Annotated first-party imports use the existing project index; unresolved, inherited, overloaded, decorated, rebound, reassigned and dynamic contracts are excluded, as are explicit metaclasses and class keywords.

Result-dependent loops, comprehensions, async streams, loop else clauses, extra statements and per-row exception or transaction blocks are excluded. A batch can change duplicate-key and failure semantics, so this remains an advisory without an autofix.
Maintained tests are checked; generated/vendor sources are excluded. A bulk method is not invented when none is declared.
rules.rationale: A loop of independent singleton writes repeats database calls while an existing bulk command centralizes conflict handling and batch execution.
rules.remediation: Collect commands and call upsert_many in bounded batches after reviewing duplicate keys, failure atomicity, ordering, and tenant scope. Preserve deliberately per-row transactions or effects with an exact suppression.
rules.summary: Use a declared compatible upsert_many instead of discarded serial upserts.

examples.title: Keep the collection projection declarative

limitations: Safe fixes apply only error-level candidates in undecorated module functions with no parameters and exactly initialization, one loop over literal primitive elements or correctly unpacked literal pairs, and return. List/set elements and dictionary keys/values must be primitive literals, bound loop names, or tuples composed of them. Unknown iterators, callbacks, properties, overloads, reachable errors, extra statements and advisory candidates remain review-only; the initialized binding and annotation are retained.

Supported list/set builders and dictionary builders with stable loop-local-name or literal keys block as errors. Dictionary attribute/descriptor keys remain advisory because assignment evaluates value before key while a comprehension evaluates key before value.
Only function-local, adjacent empty initializers and one synchronous single-purpose loop are checked.

The rule fills gaps left by Ruff PERF401, PERF403, and FURB142: derived dict projections, constructor-valued and filtered dict projections, destructured list projections, narrowly filtered computed list candidates, and filtered set builders.

Comments, loop-target leakage, try blocks, aliases, complex projections, and replacements that do not fit a 120-column line or a simple formatter-style multiline comprehension are excluded. Namespace observers, explicit inspect/sys frame access, and collections referenced by nested functions are excluded. Dynamic function aliases and helper-hidden frame reads are not resolved. Only the literal-domain subset is autofixed; other dictionary key/value evaluation order remains review-only.
Attribute projections can invoke properties or descriptors, so reviewers should keep the loop when the relative order of those reads is observable.

Computed list candidates are limited to one local assignment, a truthiness or None filter, and one bounded projection. Validation, logging, exceptions, multiple guards, and secondary mutation remain imperative.
rules.rationale: An empty collection followed by a loop whose only behavior is one projection or filtered insertion spreads a declarative map/filter across mutable scaffolding.
rules.remediation: Build the fresh collection with one dict, list, or set comprehension. When a list candidate must be computed once and reused in the element, bind it in the filter with :=. Keep the loop when mutation is incremental, evaluation order is observable, or the imperative form carries additional behavior.
rules.summary: Single-purpose fresh collection builder loop — prefer a direct comprehension.

examples.title: Request API key uses ordinary equality

limitations: The diagnostic requires evidence of an externally supplied credential and configured or stored secret state.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.
Adjacent equality pairs, literal encode normalization, and unambiguous same-scope aliases from headers, cookies, settings, or environment are traced.
Generated files, tests, test-support modules, equality methods, public sentinels, and type-like values are excluded.
`compare_digest` requires compatible ASCII string or bytes-like operands and may still reveal type or length.

Automatic fixes require a closed private nested synchronous helper whose two required local operands are forwarded directly from its containing function parameters. Three existing defaults must already capture canonical compare_digest, type and bytes; every closed call omits those defaults. Only captured exact-type guards, the equality return and False fallback are allowed; unknown calls, attribute/subscript reads, imports, mutations, frame escapes, comments and type-parameter shadows abstain. No bindings, captures or imports are added; the intended timing behavior changes.
rules.rationale: Ordinary equality may short-circuit based on matching content when attacker-controlled credentials are checked against configured secret state.
rules.remediation: For opaque tokens and MACs, normalize both operands to the same supported type and use `hmac.compare_digest`; for passwords, use the password-hashing library's verification API.
rules.summary: Externally supplied authenticators are compared with timing-sensitive equality.

examples.title: Declare collection validation once
A named collection schema owns the batch

limitations: Only locally proven, undecorated Pydantic BaseModel classes, local inheritance and unique aliases are recognized; imported application models and dynamic ancestry remain unreported.

Inputs must be a literal collection, an unambiguous list/tuple/Sequence declaration, or materialized rows from a locally bound Psycopg dict_row/class_row cursor. Unknown and streaming iterables are excluded.

Comprehensions must have one synchronous generator and no filter. Loops require an adjacent fresh list and one validation-only try block with a proven ValidationError handler that only logs and drops a record.
Changing models or context, preprocessing, rejection reports, secondary effects, observable loop locals, and validation options other than literal from_attributes=True are excluded.
Simple append loops remain owned by Ruff PERF401; its resulting model-validation comprehension is checked here. Proven SARJ013 cursor conversions take precedence over this warning.

There is no autofix: collection validation can change error aggregation, record omission, logging, evaluation after the first invalid record, and failure timing. Tests, generated files and vendor sources are excluded.
rules.rationale: Per-record validation comprehensions and catch/log/drop builders spread a collection contract across repeated model calls and mutable error-handling scaffolding. A named collection schema makes the batch's error policy explicit.
rules.remediation: Use class_row(Model) for unchanged Psycopg model rows, or a named RootModel[list[Model]] for collection validation. Declare whether invalid records reject the batch or are intentionally omitted (for example with OnErrorOmit). Preserve required logging and rejection reports.
rules.summary: Validate a homogeneous Pydantic batch with a declared collection contract.

Explicit tags preserve positional constructor calls with init=False
Data variants lack a common explicit tag

from typing import Annotated, Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
class EmailDelivery(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal['email']
    address: str
class PickupDelivery(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal['pickup']
    address: str | None = None
type Delivery = Annotated[EmailDelivery | PickupDelivery, Field(discriminator='kind')]

examples.title: Only the email variant requires an address; pickup preserves its optional address

limitations: Declared module-level unions of at least two source-visible direct dataclasses, Pydantic BaseModels or TypedDicts require a shared disjoint Literal field. PEP 604, typing Union, Optional, Annotated, forward references and bounded local aliases are supported; a None branch is allowed.

The explicit-tag policy is a modeling preference: nominal variants already support isinstance narrowing. Scalar/container unions, inline annotations, generic or inherited variants, behavior classes, unresolved variants and dynamic or ambiguous namespaces are excluded. Imported tag aliases are not resolved; an explicit literal field paired with an unresolved imported or local class domain abstains, as do opaque explicit Literal domains. Qualified imported domains and unsupported computed aliases remain uncertain rather than proving a missing tag.

String, bytes, integer, Boolean and None tag values are supported. Boolean and integer Literal values retain their distinct static types; use identity checks when equality would conflate their runtime values. A bounded hierarchy of shared literal fields may distinguish nested groups; overlapping tags without a further discriminator still fail. Nested Literal domains and transparent Final, ReadOnly, Annotated and local alias wrappers are supported. TypedDict tags must be required; dataclass ClassVar tags must have a value. Direct import-proven InitVar annotations without defaults are constructor inputs rather than instance tags; quoted, wrapped, locally aliased or defaulted InitVar forms remain uncertain. Import-proven typing final decorators preserve record recognition. Explicit Pydantic callable Discriminators, bounded stable reusable metadata, single-value plain local class namespaces, literal immutable tuple projections and imported pydantic.types constructors are respected; source-proven string field names, including local bindings and concatenation, still need Literal fields. Source-proven string discriminator writes through stable aliases invalidate callable coverage; opaque mutation, helper escapes and excessive alias graphs abstain. Module bindings are independent of unrelated local parameters and their attribute writes; class annotation shadows and global rebinding remain excluded. Other runtime configuration and default correctness remain separate contracts. No automatic field addition is safe for every constructor or serializer.
For nullable-field dependencies, only stable direct module-level import-proven Pydantic BaseModel subclasses with pure direct after model validators are inspected.

Bounded paths may contain finite tag comparisons or literal-container membership, None identity tests, Boolean combinations, nested guards and returns of the same instance. Every rejection region must prove one tag-dependent nullable-field requirement; joint missing-field or independent-tag-axis conditions abstain.

Tags must use imported Literal domains, optionally composed through direct unions, with at least two distinct homogeneous string, integer or Boolean values, optionally including an explicit None state. Mixed primitive families, bool/int equality collisions, open or computed tags abstain. Payloads must explicitly include None in a union, imported Union or Optional.
Every non-null payload member must have a source-proven inhabited built-in scalar or container type; opaque aliases, custom types and None-only or bottom-type unions are excluded.
A field required by every admitted tag value is a common field constraint rather than evidence for a discriminated union and is excluded.

Unsupported Field validation constraints cannot prove non-null payload inhabitance; defaults, aliases and passive metadata remain eligible. Literal exception messages or local assignments of those messages are supported with import-proven builtin rejection types.

Opaque helpers, effectful validators, inherited models, model mutation or escape, ambiguous namespaces, tests and generated files are excluded. The analyzer bounds validator nodes, Boolean depth, paths and rejection regions; complex forms abstain.
This error requires explicit data modeling; it does not require absent payloads in other variants or change external compatibility automatically.
rules.rationale: An explicit shared tag identifies data variants and supports field-based narrowing. A nullable field remains statically nullable even when an after validator requires it for a literal tag. A union of models with distinct Literal tags carries that dependency in the type and supports safe narrowing without repeating runtime guards.
rules.remediation: Give every data variant a common field with disjoint Literal values. For dataclasses, field(default=..., init=False) can preserve existing constructor calls; review serialized contracts. Consider a discriminated union of model variants. Make the payload non-nullable only in variants proven to reject None, and preserve every other accepted field combination, defaults, aliases and wire shape. Independent optional fields can remain optional within each variant.
rules.summary: Give data unions explicit Literal discriminators and express tag-dependent payloads as variants.

The policy is stylistic and intentionally leaves URL, path, protocol and declarative fragments alone. Stable aliases of join-built strings retain the fragment-composition exclusion; unresolved or rebound values are not inferred.

Preserve an explicit `str(value)` conversion as `{value!s}` and `repr(value)` as `{value!r}` when those conversion semantics matter. limitations: Only source-proven Pydantic BaseSettings classes and directly owned public fields are checked. Two distinct fields must share the first complete snake-case namespace token; character prefixes, environment aliases, inherited fields and unrelated data classes do not establish a group.

Boolean, expectation and quantitative modifiers such as is, has, use, expected, min, max, num, total and default do not establish component namespaces. A prefix already present as a field is left for explicit API review.

ClassVar, Final, private attributes, model_config, computed fields, tests, generated code, unknown decorators and unresolved bases are excluded. Each namespace produces one error, anchored at its first field; an exact class or first-field suppression is honored.

Source-proven nested BaseSettings fields do not count as flat candidates. A source-proven nested child already groups a namespace when its parent field has the same first complete Python namespace token, or when its public directly owned fields share that prefix apart from bare fields that are not other source-proven nested settings objects. A competing namespace or nested settings component under a different parent namespace retains subgroup findings. Class names alone, unknown annotations and unknown parent types do not establish ownership.
There is no automatic rewrite: nesting may change environment-variable decoding, aliases, source precedence and consumer access paths.
rules.rationale: Repeated namespace prefixes flatten one component's configuration across the parent settings API. A focused settings object gives that component an explicit boundary.
rules.remediation: Move the related fields into a focused nested settings object, normally constructed with Field(default_factory=...). Preserve existing environment aliases, prefixes, validation, defaults and source precedence, and verify real environment loading before changing the settings API.
rules.summary: Group settings fields that share a Python namespace prefix into a nested settings object.

examples.title: Avoid replacing the SDK constructor lookup

limitations: Only maintained test paths are analyzed; generated files and production helpers are excluded.
The rule recognizes pytest monkeypatch fixtures, unambiguous local MonkeyPatch constructors and context handles, and statically resolved unittest.mock or pytest-mock patch APIs.
Environment, mapping, import-path, and working-directory mutations are intentionally allowed.
Untyped handles are recognized only on pytest tests or fixtures; directly parametrized values are excluded.
A nested function that captures a monkeypatch handle from an outer scope is not inferred.
Instance ownership, collaborator contracts, and active consumer lookups are not inferred; justified scoped patches need a local suppression.
rules.rationale: Attribute patching hides collaborators and configuration behind ambient module or object state, coupling tests to lookup locations instead of an explicit boundary. Replacing a scoped patch with bare assignment does not fix that coupling and loses automatic restoration. Pytest monkeypatch remains appropriate for reversible process state such as environment variables and the working directory.
rules.remediation: Pass the collaborator, settings, clock, sleeper, random source, client, or factory explicitly; prefer a real in-process dependency, framework override, or purpose-built ABC/Protocol fake. A scoped patch may replace an existing constructor-injected collaborator on a test-owned instance with an interface-conforming fake when rebuilding the fixture would add wiring without improving the boundary. Keep attribute-existence checks enabled and the tested implementation intact. Suppress SARJ445 only at that call, naming the owned instance and injection seam. For inherently global boundaries or lookup interception, explain why injection would invalidate the test. Establish the binding the exercised consumer actually reads, including already-bound import aliases, and show that the oracle rejects a wrong consumer. Do not switch to bare assignment merely to avoid this rule.
rules.summary: Prefer explicit test dependencies; justify scoped attribute patches at the boundary.

limitations: Safe fixes remove only an exact single argument-type ignore from an existing terminal assert_never call after every member of a canonical local StrEnum is already handled by terminating identity branches. Missing members, other suppressions, reasons, aliases, guarded branches and dynamic domains remain manual.
Only subjects explicitly annotated as a locally declared Enum, StrEnum, IntEnum, or ReprEnum are checked.
Flags, imported or untyped domains, class-pattern unions, guarded arms, generated files, and dynamic dispatch are excluded.
Independently warns on import-proven assert_never calls with a trailing blanket or argument-type ignore; module-wide disables are not analyzed.
rules.rationale: A no-op wildcard or else branch hides missing enum members and lets newly added members pass unnoticed. Suppressing the argument-type error at assert_never also disables its static exhaustiveness guarantee.
rules.remediation: Handle every enum member, bind the catch-all value, and pass it to `typing.assert_never`; raise an explicit exception when static exhaustiveness is unavailable. Narrow the accepted type or handle missing variants instead of suppressing assert_never's argument check.
rules.summary: Typed enum dispatch must not silently ignore unhandled members.

limitations: Only functions whose dispatch subject is a simple parameter annotated Exception or BaseException are checked.
The classifier must contain at least three adjacent isinstance branches and an immediate return or raise fallback; one or more branches must contain two or more terminating refinement checks.

Type operands must be unshadowed builtin or imported names ending in Error or Exception, including literal tuples and PEP 604 unions. Imported runtime groups with plural or unrelated names are excluded.
This is an advisory, not a safe automatic rewrite: imported bindings and custom instance checks cannot be proven from syntax, and guarded cases must preserve overlap and fallthrough.
Generated files and projects proven to support Python before 3.10 are excluded.
rules.rationale: A long exception classifier that repeats isinstance checks and then refines one exception type hides the ordered set of provider outcomes. Guarded class cases make the type and refinement order explicit.
rules.remediation: Consider repeated guarded class cases while preserving subclass order, guard evaluation, and fallthrough. Keep constant comparisons in guards; a bare name in a class-pattern field captures instead of comparing.
rules.summary: Prefer guarded match/case for refined exception type dispatch.

limitations: Safe fixes require a closed private nested synchronous helper with proven inert containing scopes and exact primitive literal callers. Only comment-free builtin class-check ladders on one parameter qualify; unknown subjects, callbacks, frame/closure escapes, sibling checks, grouped conditions, guards and custom classes remain review-only.

General dispatch requires two or more adjacent, unguarded `isinstance` branches over the same simple name. Repeated isinstance calls joined only by or on that same name are also checked; use an OR class pattern for shared behavior. A single isinstance call with a type union remains allowed.

Additional review warnings require at least one source-proven Pydantic/Enum branch. Native-only sequences retain the established proof and exclusions. Mixed model/builtin dispatch is supported; review warnings have no automatic fixes.
A terminating sibling prefix may precede a two-arm if/elif tail whose bodies can fall through. Preserve nested checks inside case bodies rather than moving them into case guards.

The checked types must be unshadowed builtins, undecorated module-local classes without an explicit or known locally inherited custom metaclass, or proven stdlib ast classes; unresolved imports, runtime type groups, repeated type references, generated files, and non-terminating sibling checks are excluded.

Local ancestry must resolve to stable undeclared-metaclass classes or proven builtin/stdlib ast bases. External bases, runtime base aliases, and parameterized base expressions remain excluded because their metaclass or __class_getitem__ effects are unproven.

Nested attribute-validation guards are excluded: converting them to keyword class patterns can turn attribute errors into match fallthrough, and an imported isinstance operand may be a runtime tuple rather than a class.
A terminal-looking context-manager body does not prove a sibling branch terminates: exceptions can be suppressed. An unconditional return or raise after the context manager remains eligible.

Declared support for Python before 3.10 suppresses this recommendation when proven by the nearest project metadata or exact installed-distribution ownership. Missing or ambiguous target metadata retains advisory behavior; it does not prove a modern target.
rules.rationale: A repeated mutually exclusive `isinstance` dispatch repeats its subject and hides the closed list of runtime shapes. Class patterns make the alternatives explicit without repeating the dispatch subject.
rules.remediation: Replace the branches with `match subject` and one class-pattern arm per distinct type; combine types that share behavior with an OR-pattern.
rules.summary: Prefer `match` for structural runtime type dispatch.

examples.title: Keep error variants and their fallback under one dispatch subject

limitations: Safe fixes require a closed private nested synchronous helper with proven inert containing scopes and exact primitive literal callers. Only comment-free literal-equality ladders on one parameter qualify; unknown subjects, callbacks, frame/closure escapes, sibling checks, grouped conditions and guards remain review-only.

ERROR covers direct literal equality ladders on an unrebound local parameter and terminal equality dispatch on a stable local name against distinct dotted values from one import-proven namespace or local enum. A proven minimum Python version of 3.10 and no visible namespace access are required. Other supported dispatch remains WARNING.
Equality-only ladders require two or more tests on the same left-hand name or attribute chain, followed by else.
Cases must be distinct string, bytes, or numeric literals, or singly bound module constants containing them; shadowed constants and singleton values are excluded.
This is a readability suggestion, not proof of exhaustiveness or a safe automatic rewrite: attributes can have side effects and match evaluates its subject once.
Grouped or guarded ladders and terminal sibling branches require three distinct arms on a bare name; only the last arm may have a selector-first guard.

Two or more terminal sibling equality branches with a terminal fallback, or an if/elif ladder with else, also qualify when comparing one bare name with distinct values from the same qualified namespace. Imported values are not assumed to be exhaustive enum members. This subset remains review-only because import attributes and equality may have custom behavior.
Groups contain two to six distinct string literals in a tuple, list, or set. Set hashing and custom equality can differ from pattern matching; no runtime string type is inferred.

Declared support for Python before 3.10 suppresses this recommendation when proven by the nearest project metadata or exact installed-distribution ownership. Missing or ambiguous target metadata retains advisory behavior; it does not prove a modern target.
rules.rationale: A single dispatch subject makes distinct value cases and their fallback easier to review.
rules.remediation: Consider match/case while preserving fallback and constant semantics; use literal or dotted value patterns, never bare constant names that capture instead of compare. Review membership versus equality, subject evaluation, and guard order before rewriting.

limitations: Test, test-support, and generated files are excluded.
Collections require at least eight deeply immutable elements, or three when allocated inside a loop; only representation-insensitive reads are accepted.
Final dictionaries retain mutable contents at runtime; unknown calls, mutation, and escaping references are excluded from hoisting candidates.
Visible frame or dynamic-namespace observation retains WARNING because moving a local binding can change observed caller state.

Regex findings require a proven stdlib `re.compile` binding and exclude `re.DEBUG`; regex cache lookup findings remain warnings because invocation frequency and initialization timing are unproved. Immutable literal collection tables enforce the explicit static-lifetime policy at error severity; preserve any intentional per-call ownership with an exact-code exception.
rules.rationale: Rebuilding a substantial static collection repeats allocation, while calling `re.compile` with a constant pattern repeats a regex-cache lookup. Native immutable collections or Final dictionary bindings make the static lifetime explicit for proven read-only use.
rules.remediation: Define the value once at module scope as a tuple, frozenset, Final[dict[K, V]], or compiled pattern, then reference it from the function. Final prevents reassignment in type-checked code but does not freeze dictionary contents; use MappingProxyType when runtime write protection is required. Preserve ordering and concrete-type behavior used by callers.

examples.title: Test installs a module without guaranteed restoration
Pytest restores the module registry after the test

limitations: Teardown ownership and original-state restoration across yield are not inferred. Valid cleanup or restoration may still warn and require a reasoned local suppression.
Only maintained test paths are analyzed; generated files, production code, and module/class bootstrap mutations are excluded.
The rule covers os.chdir, sys.path.insert(0, ...), and direct sys.modules set, delete, or unused pop operations with an equivalent pytest restoring helper.
Environment variables remain owned by Ruff TID251/B003; argv, locale, timezone, warning filters, and process APIs without an equivalent helper are outside this rule.
Imports and import aliases are resolved conservatively. Indirect container aliases and dynamically selected modules are not inferred.
rules.rationale: The working directory and Python import registries are shared by every test in the process. A direct mutation can survive an assertion or setup failure, making later tests depend on execution order.
rules.remediation: Establish restoration in setup with pytest's monkeypatch.chdir, monkeypatch.syspath_prepend, monkeypatch.setitem, or monkeypatch.delitem so the original state is recorded before the mutation. Alternatively, explicitly restore the original state with a matching try/finally. Adding monkeypatch operations only during teardown can undo intended cleanup: undoing a teardown deletion can reinstall a temporary sys.modules entry. Intentional cleanup with established ownership may use a local, reasoned SARJ446 suppression.
rules.summary: Test mutates process-wide state without a restoring test scope.

examples.title: A monotonic clock measures duration

limitations: A start used exclusively in direct while-loop duration comparisons against finite nonnegative literal thresholds blocks as an error. Returned, logged, and other elapsed-time measurements retain advisory findings because wall-clock telemetry can be intentional.
Only an unconditional, single-assignment function-local start reading whose every read is the right operand of time.time() - start is reported.
Only unshadowed module-level clock imports are resolved. Reassignment, additional timestamp uses, escapes, nested-scope reads, comprehensions, reflection, and mixed-clock expressions are excluded.
Instance fields, process or persisted deadlines, indirect end-clock readings, and generated files are not inferred. No automatic rewrite is provided.
rules.rationale: System-clock corrections can make wall-clock differences negative or unexpectedly large. A monotonic clock measures elapsed intervals without these jumps.
rules.remediation: Use time.monotonic() or time.perf_counter() for both the start reading and its elapsed-time readings. Keep time.time() when measuring absolute timestamps or deliberate wall-clock adjustments.
rules.summary: Use a monotonic clock for a local wall-clock value used only to measure elapsed time.

The response owns encoded content without annotation-only validation

limitations: Plain built-in str adapters are checked only inside assertions. The JSON branch checks exactly dict[str, pydantic.JsonValue] immediately wrapping FastAPI jsonable_encoder of a dictionary literal with string literal keys; dynamic values and keyword encoder options are allowed. Custom encoders must be a literal mapping with only proven built-in bytes keys, so they cannot replace the root mapping or its string keys. Unknown input shapes, opaque or shape-changing encoders, schema aliases, other containers, constrained types, unions, models, configured adapters and validation options are excluded.

Scoped import aliases and unescaped unconditional module or local adapter bindings are recognized, including independent functions reusing a name. Conditional, reassigned, indirect or class/comprehension/parameter/global/nonlocal cached bindings are excluded, as are shadowed symbols, wildcard imports and imports with visible mutation or escape.

String assertion messages and deferred expressions are excluded. The JSON branch excludes lambdas, comprehensions, function/class headers and cached encoded values; proven pytest.raises(ValidationError) contexts and try bodies catching ValidationError are preserved. Broader catches and contextlib.suppress are not inferred. This advisory does not prove equivalent behavior: intentional validation or byte-decoding contracts need a local reasoned suppression; there is no autofix.
rules.rationale: A plain string adapter obscures an assertion and can decode bytes. Generic JSON-dictionary validation after encoding adds a separate runtime contract, often only to satisfy an annotation; it can reject nested integer keys that a response serializer accepts and does not prove response serializability.
rules.remediation: Use isinstance(value, str) for string assertions. For annotation-only JSON adaptation, return a typed Response/JSONResponse at the serialization boundary. Keep structured input and specific schema validation. Preserve intentional coercion, recursive string-key validation or ValidationError contracts explicitly.
rules.summary: Avoid unconstrained adapters for string assertions or already encoded JSON mappings.

examples.title: Two domain ID roles share the same primitive carrier

limitations: The rule checks functions, methods, constructors, and classes for at least two ID-shaped roles with the same proven carrier. Existing coverage remains an error.

Imported first-party carriers and non-ID roles backed by a unique matching NewType in the owning distribution or a declared local dependency are errors. A single raw ID role also qualifies when that distribution already declares an unambiguous matching nominal type, including optional and collection forms. Ambiguous exports, conditional or relative imports, cycles, and unresolved ownership are skipped.

Non-ID role discovery uses exact snake-case names and proven matching carriers; it does not infer brands from names alone. Dependency discovery respects declared workspace members and exclusions, and excludes optional and transitive dependencies.
Rebound aliases, generic aliases, carrier names shadowed by type parameters, and mutated or escaped canonical provider namespaces are skipped conservatively across the file.
Generated code, migrations, external adapters, operational context, raw schemas, SQLAlchemy Mapped fields, ambiguous imports, and unlike carrier shapes are excluded.

Classes with explicit bases, including object, are excluded without requiring an override decorator. Local base declarations do not prove runtime member ownership remains closed; class construction, native hooks and escaped handles can change inheritance. Independent module functions and plain classes remain eligible.
rules.rationale: Two identifiers with the same primitive or container carrier can be exchanged without a type-checking error. Erasing an established domain ID has the same problem even when a boundary accepts one identifier. Nominal types make those role mistakes visible while leaving unlike carriers alone.
rules.remediation: Use `typing.NewType` as the low-runtime-cost default and propagate it from the raw edge through the domain boundary. A nominal value object is also valid when runtime validation or behavior is required.
rules.summary: Python boundaries should distinguish swappable identifier roles with nominal types.

rules.rationale: When an implementation immediately replaces both `None` and an empty list with the same fresh empty list, the callable contract exposes an extra input state that its body does not retain.
rules.remediation: After reviewing callers and list identity or mutation behavior, either require the list or accept `Sequence[T] = ()` and materialize a list internally. Removing explicit `None` acceptance is an API migration.

examples.title: Review a usage value split across nullable fields

limitations: This is a broad modeling review warning, not proof of an all-or-nothing invariant or an invalid runtime state. A shared underscore-delimited prefix and at least two explicitly nullable fields are the deterministic trigger; independent same-prefix settings can also match and should remain independent when that is their contract.

Checks stable direct module-level source-declared Pydantic BaseModels, plain direct dataclasses and TypedDicts. This advisory relationship follows unshadowed imports and explicit namespace writes, without proving the runtime effects of unrelated callbacks. PEP 604, Optional, Union, Annotated, quoted annotations and bounded module type aliases are recognized; container-element nullability alone is not field nullability. ClassVar and InitVar metadata are excluded. A required or unresolved same-prefix sibling prevents grouping that broader prefix.

Larger overlapping groups take precedence, with the longest common prefix for the same field set. Each field belongs to at most one finding. Inherited/generic models, unknown decorators or namespaces, rebound owners, tests, generated and vendor code are excluded.
The rule does not infer relationships from shared suffixes, enforce non-null child fields or automatically nest public models. SARJ510 owns proven tag-dependent variant payloads.
rules.rationale: Several nullable fields with a common record prefix can scatter one optional value across a larger model, requiring repeated presence checks and obscuring which partial states are intentional. A nested value can give that concept one boundary while retaining independently nullable children.
rules.remediation: Review whether the fields represent one value and, if so, introduce a typed composite with one optional outer field. Preserve valid partial states, omitted-key behavior, defaults, aliases, validation and wire/storage compatibility. Keep independent optional children nullable. A shared prefix does not prove that all fields must be present together.
rules.summary: Review related optional fields as one optional composite value.

examples.title: One or-pattern owns the shared body

limitations: Safe fixes merge only comment-free proven runs and preserve the first body verbatim; runs containing comments remain review-only.
Only adjacent, unguarded, refutable arms with structurally identical non-empty bodies are compared.
Arms with different bound names or comments, intervening or leading comments, and combined patterns rejected by Python are excluded.

Bodies that read pattern captures or names used by the match subject are excluded: merging can lose correlated narrowing required by typed calls. This syntax-only check also abstains from safe forwarding of those values.
rules.rationale: An or-pattern expresses shared handling once and prevents identical arms from drifting apart.
rules.remediation: Join the equivalent patterns with `|` and keep their shared body under the merged arm.
rules.summary: Merge adjacent `case` arms with identical bodies into one or-pattern.

examples.title: The importer erases its module result
The proven private literal return already has its precise type
Existing source proof permits a narrow convergent fix

limitations: Safe fixes narrow only a bare builtin object return annotation to builtin str for a closed private nested synchronous helper returning one exact string literal, with every call used directly as an if test and all containing return contracts explicit. Existing inert/metadata/binding proofs must hold; public/domain/container/parameter/model contracts and other result uses remain review-only.

Checks builtin object in function signatures and class field annotations, including supported containers, callables, optional unions and quoted annotations. Local opaque values, object() sentinels, Literal/Annotated metadata, framework hooks, proven override signatures, and registered raw Pydantic callbacks are excluded. Functions that directly validate an object parameter through a source-visible BaseModel, BaseSettings or RootModel model_validate call, positionally or with obj=, retain that raw boundary. JSON text inputs still require a text or byte contract. Aliases must resolve to their source declaration and their bodies use definition scope. Alias graphs are bounded and shared branches reuse their facts. Imported or shadowed application types named object are preserved. Genuine opaque public contracts can use an explained exact-code exception; narrowing outside the exact private truthiness-only subset remains manual.

An import-proven TypeGuard or TypeIs retains bare object on its guarded positional parameter and unchecked object slots in its declared refinement result; other object parameters remain checked. Guard correctness belongs to the type-guard rules. Universal type[object] class contracts and the return of a canonical module-level PEP 562 __getattr__ hook retain their opaque runtime contracts.

Ordinary raw validators retain object inputs tied to builtin isinstance, exact builtin type comparisons or an actual source-resolved TypeGuard/TypeIs through rejecting branches, actual type/refinement assertions, accepting terminal branches with a rejecting fallback, or conditional expressions. Stable projections from containers with unchecked value slots retain their raw root contract when those values are validated. Source-visible local and imported validators may delegate those inputs and raw results; precise result narrowing does not justify a bare object output. Related unchecked mapping projections and transforms retain unknown values; import-proven native parsers and JSONDecoder preserve raw outputs. Universal builtin and stdlib interoperation may retain raw inputs. Independent object parameters, domain constructors and unproven parser names remain checked. Source resolution and dataflow are bounded with cycle guards; rebinding, decorators and namespace mutation invalidate delegated proof.

Native opaque contracts include canonical ast.Constant.value reads and captures, FunctionType invocations, identity-only inputs and sys.getrefcount. Actual exec/eval globals and locals retain unknown values only through bounded native dict construction and alias flow; unrelated dictionaries and source domain factories do not borrow that ownership. Stub property returns on an import-proven runtime_checkable Protocol retain unchecked incoming attributes. Generic callable results, ordinary Protocol methods, application properties and unused parameters remain checked.

Raw input unions may include scalar or None branches; only genuine unchecked container branches seed raw projections. Mapping consumers that inspect only keys retain uninspected value slots. Projected aliases require simple statement dominance, and precise active guards permit typed consumption after validation. Native namespace output reads require a preceding direct function-scope execution and abstain after authored mutations. Benign builtins imports do not hide builtin object contracts; explicit object shadowing and source-visible object mutations remain outside scope.

An import-proven Iterable of unchecked values retains its raw element contract when every input use is a direct synchronous iteration and every reachable element read directly enters source-proven Pydantic model_validate. Deferred closures, rebinding, other iterator/element uses, unknown model providers and JSON-text parsers do not establish that boundary.

Rejecting branches may end in a stable source-visible synchronous helper whose body ends with an unconditional raise and contains no return or yield path. Names and NoReturn annotations alone do not establish termination; decorated, mutated, asynchronous, generator and returning helpers remain unknown.
rules.rationale: An object annotation hides the operations and data the caller actually supplies. It often spreads casts and handwritten shape checks into consumers.
rules.remediation: Use a concrete domain type, Protocol, TypeVar, Pydantic model or JsonValue as appropriate. Importer callables return types.ModuleType. Keep object for genuinely opaque Python values and raw validation boundaries with an explained local exception when necessary; never replace it with Any or a cast.
rules.summary: Use a precise type for declared application contracts instead of object.

async def save(cursor: AsyncCursor, rows):
    for row in rows:
        await cursor.execute('INSERT INTO users (id) VALUES (%s)', (row.id,))

examples.title: Batch the same parameterized statement

limitations: Only a synchronous for loop with one discarded execute call on an import-proven typed Psycopg Cursor or AsyncCursor parameter is inspected. The query must be one literal INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE with placeholders and loop-dependent bound parameters.

RETURNING, queries, dynamic SQL, extra execute options, async streams, loop else clauses, additional statements and per-row exception or transaction contexts are excluded. Connection.execute is excluded because connections do not expose the same executemany API.
No automatic batching or performance claim is made for a particular workload. Advisory severity preserves deliberately sequential database effects; exact suppressions document those contracts.
Generated/vendor sources are excluded; maintained tests are checked. Stable aliases and cursors acquired through context managers are intentionally outside the initial proof boundary.
Cursor state reads, iteration and opaque cursor escapes are excluded: executemany accumulates rowcount and can change observable execution interleaving.
rules.rationale: A bare execute loop repeats the same statement through separate client calls. Psycopg executemany centralizes batch execution and can pipeline those operations.
rules.remediation: Prefer an existing bulk store method; otherwise send bounded parameter batches through cursor.executemany. Preserve transaction ownership, per-row failure behavior, ordering and backpressure.
rules.summary: Use Psycopg executemany for a serial loop of invariant parameterized writes without row results.

examples.title: Two assertions describe one expected model

limitations: Only consecutive plain equality or bool/None identity assertions on two distinct declared fields of a source-proven Pydantic model are considered. Models are resolved through declared parameter/local/return annotations and simple construction/validation calls. Fields inherited through a single source-visible base chain are included; ambiguous multiple inheritance is not expanded. Plain properties, private attributes, model_config and ClassVar type wrappers are excluded; Annotated metadata does not turn a data field into a class variable; Final annotations are conservatively excluded as well. Unknown receivers, non-model objects, calls in expected values, assertion messages, repeated fields, nested attributes and custom comparison operators are excluded. This is a review advisory, never an automatic rewrite or assertion deletion.
rules.rationale: Consecutive assertions on the same model scatter one expected record across statements and obscure which fields form the test's contract.
rules.remediation: Prefer 'assert result == ExpectedModel(...)' for the complete contract, or 'assert result.model_dump(include={...}) == {...}' for an intentional subset. Keep any needed None guard. Preserve identity, approximate comparisons, custom serialization and private-attribute semantics; do not fill irrelevant fields or use model_construct/model_copy to bypass validation.
rules.summary: Compare a Pydantic model or an explicit field projection instead of consecutive property assertions.

examples.title: A test constructs its service's store
The store arrives through pytest

limitations: Source-visible module-level collaborator instances must also enter tests through fixtures. Argument binding must be explicit: starred positional arguments, keyword unpacking and duplicate bindings abstain rather than guessing collaborator ownership.

Safe fixes only reuse an already-requested typed factory inside an authored runtime identity guard over a closed source-owned collaborator graph. They change only its immediate constructor callee; no fixture, signature, guard, setup event or lifecycle is introduced. All other findings require review.

Checks collected pytest functions and plain test classes. A local or inline class construction must feed a proven stored-and-invoked ABC/Protocol collaborator, or a proven BaseSettings instance must be passed to a call. Names alone never identify a service. Constructor failure tests, fixtures, helpers, dynamic/unresolved sources, generated and test-support paths are excluded. No automatic fixture extraction or lifecycle change.
rules.rationale: Constructing collaborators in a test bypasses pytest's dependency graph, caching and overrides even when only one test currently needs the setup.
rules.remediation: Request function-scoped store, service and settings fixtures by parameter. Use a typed factory fixture for variants or multiple instances. Keep construction under test explicit and preserve setup ordering and the actual owner's cleanup; do not create global singletons or autouse fixtures.
rules.summary: Pass test collaborators through fixtures instead of constructing dependency graphs inside tests.

def test_app():

examples.title: A test calls shared generic pool setup

limitations: Only directly collected module-level test functions in conventional pytest module names are checked.
Only unshadowed runtime imports from a uniquely resolved conftest in the test's ancestor directories are followed under conventional pytest discovery.
Helpers must be undecorated synchronous functions with no formal inputs and one direct return of an imported psycopg_pool pool constructor.

Async pools require an explicit literal open=False, no unpacked arguments, and no calls inside constructor arguments; opened or dynamically configured async pools need lifecycle-specific fixture design.
Setup must be the first executable statement and immediately feed a plain call, or appear inline as a direct argument of that first call.
Class tests, decorated helpers, unknown test decorators, dynamic imports, re-exports, and ambiguous or out-of-bound source paths are excluded.
Tests with statically visible callable references in any scope are excluded; scope-ambiguous references are handled conservatively.
Command-line conftest discovery overrides and external pytest plugin registrations are not inferred.
rules.rationale: Calling a shared conftest pool helper during initial test setup bypasses an explicit pytest fixture dependency, per-test caching, and fixture overrides, even when the helper already centralizes allocation. This preference does not establish a resource leak.
rules.remediation: Request one function-scoped fixture visible to the test. Declare required setup ordering as fixture dependencies and preserve initial pool state and cleanup ownership. An unopened allocation fixture should return the pool without opening or closing it when application lifespan owns that lifecycle. Use yield teardown only when the fixture owns cleanup; keep factories for variants or fresh instances.
rules.summary: Request shared database-pool setup through a pytest fixture.

examples.title: An end anchor permits a final newline
Normalized match still permits a final newline
A strict end anchor rejects the final newline
Validate the entire value

limitations: Autofix only replaces the final `$` with strict `\Z` in one simple anchored ASCII character-class pattern passed to an existing canonical module-qualified re.match call with an exact string-literal subject containing no newline and no flags. It preserves the existing callee, argument order, literal quoting, and boolean-validation context; explicit mocks, namespace reflection, mutations, escapes, dynamic inputs, and other patterns remain for review.
Checks direct negative match/is-None rejection guards and returns of bool(match), not match, or match is/is-not None. Match-object returns, extraction, search, and compound conditions are excluded.

Patterns must be valid string or bytes literals bounded by `^` or `\A` and an unescaped outer `$`; top-level alternation, inline extension groups other than noncapturing groups, and flags other than literal zero are excluded.

Only imported standard-library re functions and unique, unconditional module or same-function compile bindings are resolved. Rebinding, import shadowing, escaped regex objects or modules, explicit match positions, tests, and generated files are excluded.
Binding checks are deliberately file-wide, so unrelated same-named locals can suppress findings. Dynamic monkeypatching and interprocedural changes are not inferred.
rules.rationale: The regex `$` anchor can match before a final newline, so an anchored match can accept a value that was not fully validated.
rules.remediation: Use `re.fullmatch` or the compiled pattern's `fullmatch` method for strict whole-value validation. Preserve deliberate terminal-newline acceptance or an existing match contract with a reasoned exact SARJ460 exception; do not rewrite that behavior automatically.
rules.summary: An anchored regex validation predicate does not require a full-string match.

examples.title: Constructor silently selects an empty configuration
Caller explicitly chooses an absent configuration

limitations: This architectural preference is advisory: a default is not necessarily a correctness defect.
Only directly defined __init__ signatures are checked, including class-suite branches and static/class methods; assigned or generated constructors and dataclass fields are not inferred.
Tests, generated files, stubs, and proven overload declarations are excluded. Ambiguous imports, namespace mutation, or escaped overload handles retain the advisory conservatively.
Dynamic decorator replacement and cross-function mutation timing are not inferred.
Removing defaults can break callers, so the rule does not autofix signatures.
rules.rationale: Defaulted constructor parameters hide choices at the composition boundary. Replacing None with an empty string, a constant, or a factory still permits an implicit choice. A required nullable parameter makes a meaningful absent value explicit without inventing a sentinel.
rules.remediation: Require the parameter and update callers to pass their choice explicitly; preserve meaningful None values. Suppress intentional framework or public-library defaults with a compatibility reason.
rules.summary: Prefer required constructor parameters so callers choose dependencies and configuration explicitly.

examples.title: A claimed narrowing is not a schema validator
Return a validated domain value

limitations: Warns on import-proven typing/typing_extensions TypeGuard return annotations, including quoted annotations and stable module type aliases. This is an architecture preference even when a particular guard correctly validates its result.

Shadowed or mutated imports, dynamic namespaces, wildcard imports, generated/vendor files and unresolved imported application aliases abstain. Boolean predicates and TypeIs are outside this policy; existing guard correctness rules still check unsafe narrowing.
No automatic rewrite: validated values, boolean predicates and rejecting parsers have different APIs and error behavior. Runtime validation must actually inspect or construct the accepted value.
rules.rationale: TypeGuard tells the type checker to trust a predicate's claimed result; its annotation performs no runtime validation. Returning a validated domain value keeps the accepted schema and downstream contract together.
rules.remediation: At data boundaries, validate into a named Pydantic model or TypeAdapter and return the validated value. For type dispatch, use actual isinstance checks or match class patterns. Do not replace TypeGuard with a cast or merely change its annotation to TypeIs. Explain indispensable low-level refinements with a local exact-code exception.
rules.summary: Prefer runtime validation to TypeGuard assertions.

Generated code, directives, ambiguous comments, policy sentinels, non-HTTP protocols, vendor status codes, and values already carrying the fact are excluded; tests remain in scope.

examples.title: Fluent method names its enclosing class

limitations: Safe fixes replace only error-level return annotations when Self is already imported unambiguously. Advisory contracts, added imports, shadowed aliases and commented annotations remain review-only.

Only final instance methods on stable undecorated module classes without bases, with a closed canonical final provider and every return equal to the unrebound receiver, block as errors. Other fluent methods and class constructors remain advisory to preserve valid override and construction contracts.
Owned class and method mutation, namespace access, and escaped class references retain warning severity.
Class creation must have inert literal members and supported method signatures/decorators; special methods and unknown descriptor values remain advisory.
Standalone files with unknown module identity and non-typing imports retain warnings because self-imported class aliases cannot be resolved safely.
Only undecorated or provenance-safe methods whose every return directly preserves the receiver type are analyzed.
Static methods, generators, final classes, metaclasses, inherited-base annotations, and behavior-changing decorators are excluded.
rules.rationale: `Self` preserves the concrete subclass type when an inherited method returns its receiver or constructs through its class receiver.
rules.remediation: Import `Self` from `typing` (or `typing_extensions` on Python before 3.11) and use it as the return annotation.
rules.summary: Prefer `Self` for self-returning methods and alternate constructors.

Declared fields rely on the annotated contract. Unknown or union field types, properties, explicit owner/field reassignment, branch-merged bindings, stored intersections, and generated files are excluded. Captured bindings in deferred lambda/generator bodies and starred intersection arguments are excluded. The other operand must be a known iterable.
Nonliteral intersections remain suggestions because short-circuiting may make custom element equality or hashing side effects observable.
rules.rationale: `isdisjoint` names the overlap predicate directly and avoids allocating an intersection that is immediately discarded.
rules.remediation: Use `left.isdisjoint(right)` and negate it when the condition requires overlap.
rules.summary: Prefer `set.isdisjoint` when a built-in set intersection is used only as a boolean predicate.

limitations: Automatic fixes reuse one existing canonical module Literal alias only when its finite string domain strictly contains a closed private nested helper's handled literal match cases and every direct caller supplies a handled-case literal. Reachable fallback exceptions retain manual ownership because their tracebacks can expose private helper frames. An unhandled alias member must keep the existing rejecting fallback reachable; exact handled-domain aliases remain manual because narrowing would introduce an unreachable-pattern type error. Only the str parameter annotation changes; defaults, comments, generics, aliases/escapes, reflection/frame access, shared bodies and runtime enum creation remain manual.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.
The rule requires a sibling choice collection or dispatch that explicitly rejects unlisted strings.
Generated code, external vocabularies, open-ended name domains, and test-only comparison clusters are excluded.
rules.rationale: A named closed domain lets type checking and review catch invalid values and incomplete handling.
rules.remediation: Define a `StrEnum`, or a named `Literal` alias when enum runtime behavior is unnecessary.
rules.summary: Prefer `StrEnum` for application-owned string domains with explicit closed-set evidence.

Checks parameters of source-visible functions passed directly to typer.run or registered with a stable local Typer application's command/callback decorator. Missing annotations and bare Any/object, including Annotated wrappers, are reported. Ordinary functions and unrelated command decorators are excluded.

Stable local import and application aliases are followed. Shadowed or mutated imports, wildcard imports, dynamic namespaces and generated/vendor files abstain. Imported command functions, dynamic registrations and composite erased types require separate type checking.
No automatic rewrite: positional/option compatibility and conversion behavior require review. This policy does not claim every argparse or Click program is incorrectly validated.
rules.rationale: A list of argv strings does not declare positional meaning, conversions or option validation. Typer derives those contracts from the command signature and rejects invalid arguments before calling application code.
rules.remediation: Use typer.run on a command with explicit parameter types, or register typed functions with Typer.command/callback. Preserve option names, defaults, validation and exit behavior during migration.

Existing mapping-shape and external-boundary diagnostics take precedence at the same read when selected together; selecting this rule alone still reports it.

examples.title: The field retains its domain type

limitations: Only source-proven BaseSettings classes and raw str/int/float fields are checked. Evidence comes from an enum or stable NewType default, an absolute HTTP/HTTPS/WS/WSS URL default or exact Field(gt=0)/Field(ge=0) metadata. Field names alone never imply credentials, IDs, ports, paths or allowed choices. Existing constrained/optional domain types remain valid. Field types and Field providers use their lexical scope, including generic parameter shadowing. Private attributes, model_config and ClassVar type wrappers are excluded; Final annotations are conservatively excluded as well. URL and numeric changes require review; SDK conversion, required None defaults, NaN/infinity and environment source parsing need explicit tests. No automatic rewrite.
rules.rationale: A primitive annotation can accept values outside an enum, nominal identifier or URL contract already demonstrated by its default. Repeated lower-bound metadata can also hide a standard validated type.
rules.remediation: Reuse the default's enum or NewType, use a Pydantic URL type with the accepted schemes, and prefer PositiveInt/NonNegativeInt or PositiveFloat/NonNegativeFloat for exact zero bounds. Keep units, aliases and source precedence explicit. Use SecretStr for secrets, existing domain identifiers, nested settings with default_factory, declarative bounds and pure computed properties where their contracts justify them. Validate textual environment values; do not enable blanket strict mode or change coercion, optionality or startup behavior without checking real environment inputs.
rules.summary: Declare settings fields with the domain types already demonstrated by their defaults.

examples.title: The awaited lookup is bound in its absence guard

limitations: Safe fixes reuse the proven assignment/guard candidate and preserve the original condition, awaited expression, body and sentinel.
Only one-line awaited calls followed immediately by an exact `is None` or `is not None` guard ending in return or raise are checked.
Statements before the terminal operation must be simple assignments; expressions and compound control flow are excluded.

An `is None` guard requires a later use on the surviving path and must not use or rebind the name inside the guard; an `is not None` guard must consume the binding inside the terminal branch and leave no later use before rebinding.
The combined condition must fit 120 columns; comments, else branches, ambiguous name flow, generated files, and broader assignment-expression preferences are excluded.
rules.rationale: When an awaited lookup and its terminal None guard are adjacent, binding in the condition keeps the operation, branch decision, and temporary name in one compact expression.
rules.remediation: Rewrite `value = await lookup(); if value is None: return` as `if (value := await lookup()) is None: return`. Preserve `is not None` when the terminal branch returns or raises with the bound value. A short message assignment may remain inside the guard before the terminal statement. Keep two statements when the awaited assignment is an intentional debugging or tracing boundary.
rules.summary: Bind a compact awaited lookup in its immediately following terminal None guard.

examples.title: Comprehension evaluates one call twice

limitations: Autofix only handles a private nested ordinary synchronous nongenerator helper whose entire body returns one list comprehension over literal exact strings, with one identical call as its filter and result: proven builtin len, or zero-argument strip/lower/upper/lstrip/rstrip/casefold/capitalize/title/swapcase/expandtabs. Exact direct callers, fresh file-wide binding names, and absence of known frame or metadata capabilities are required; public, escaped, generic, variadic, and effectful shapes remain for review.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.
Only single-generator comprehensions inside non-test callable bodies are analyzed; generated code and nested or deferred expression scopes are excluded.
Nested calls, differing sibling calls, unsafe short-circuit branches, and recognized type-inspection, consuming, or nondeterministic calls are excluded.

General findings cannot prove referential transparency. Outside the exact literal-string autofix subset, a named expression binds in the containing callable, so the chosen name must be fresh and reviewed.
rules.rationale: When both evaluations are intended to produce one stable value, repeating the call wastes work and obscures that relationship.
rules.remediation: If reevaluation is unintended, bind the result once in the filter with a fresh containing-scope name and reuse it. Keep separate calls or use an explicit loop when each evaluation is meaningful.
rules.summary: The same call runs in a comprehension filter and its result.

limitations: Safe fixes preserve the original regex expression, identifier spelling, condition and body.
Only a short, single-line assignment physically followed by a truthy or `is not None` check is analyzed.
The receiver must resolve to an imported `re` or `regex` module, a unique compile binding, or a parameter annotated as its Pattern type.
Tests, generated files, comments or blank lines between statements, rewrites over 100 columns, rebindings, and later result uses are excluded.
rules.rationale: A named expression can keep a short regex operation with its only condition while preserving access to the result.
rules.remediation: For a truthy check, use `if (match := pattern.search(text)):`. For an explicit None check, preserve it as `if (match := pattern.search(text)) is not None:`.
rules.summary: A proven regex Match-or-None result is assigned only for the following condition.

examples.title: Stream loop binds in its condition
Producer loop preserves a None sentinel
Stream loop assigns and then breaks

limitations: Safe fixes preserve the original producer expression, sentinel comparison and remaining loop body; comments on the loop header abstain.
Only `while True` loops beginning with a single-line call assignment and a physically adjacent falsy or `None` break are analyzed.

Tests, generated files, comments attached to or separating the matched statements, blank lines, type comments, rewrites over 100 columns, loop or guard `else` clauses, and empty rewritten bodies are excluded.
The producer receiver is not resolved; calls and awaited calls are accepted when the surrounding loop shape is otherwise exact.
rules.rationale: A named-expression loop can state a repeated producer call and its termination condition together.
rules.remediation: For `if not value: break`, use `while (value := read()):`. For `if value is None: break`, preserve the sentinel with `while (value := read()) is not None:`.
rules.summary: Collapse a compact producer assignment and immediate sentinel break into a named-expression loop.

examples.title: Drive behavior from an independent expected table
A fresh local expected table observes the actual production collection
Do not derive cases from production eligibility
A fixture equality does not observe the imported production collection

limitations: Only proven first-party, non-test imports with eligible, supported, allowed, or required in their names are checked in collected pytest parametrization.
Direct collections, simple unshadowed builtin wrappers, set expressions, and positional or keyword argvalues are recognized.
A direct module-level or collected-test equality against a distinct literal expected table proves an independent oracle; helper-indirected relationships remain unreported.

Collected-test oracles must read the imported production binding without parameter/local shadowing. Expected tuple bindings may be module-level or local and must be assigned once; fresh local literal lists/sets are accepted only when their sole read is the assertion.

Unchanged same-name default captures of production imports or immutable expected tuples, and single direct local reimports of the exact absolute module and symbol, retain provenance. Class-scope default shadowing, later writes, and imports after the assertion do not prove a production read.
rules.rationale: When exact eligibility or support membership is contractual, deriving cases from production lets a member change without an independent test oracle failing.
rules.remediation: For contractual membership, define a literal expected table, assert the production collection equals it, and drive behavior from the expected table. Suppress the warning with rationale for an intentional dynamic sweep.
rules.summary: Warn when pytest membership-contract cases are derived only from the first-party production collection.

examples.title: Fixture consumers use named fields
Fixture consumers must remember field positions

limitations: Only pytest and pytest-asyncio fixtures in test paths are analyzed.
Decorator identity follows direct absolute imports and preceding module/class bindings; dynamic provider aliases and plugin registration are not inferred.
Explicit writes to a proven provider's fixture attribute invalidate later module imports, including through executed class bodies; arbitrary call effects and assignment aliases are not inferred.
Factory closures, single-field tuples, starred tuple literals, and variadic tuple annotations are allowed.
Homogeneous variadic tuple annotations are treated as sequences and excluded; fixed domain tuple protocols require an exact suppression.
rules.rationale: Tuple-shaped fixture APIs encode each value's role in its position, so call sites are opaque and a reordered result can silently bind the wrong test dependency.
rules.remediation: Return a `NamedTuple`, frozen dataclass, or another result object and access its named fields; split independent values into separate fixtures when they do not form one record. Keep the tuple and use an exact SARJ044 suppression when tuple identity or ordering is itself the tested domain contract.
rules.summary: Pytest fixture exposes a fixed positional record as an unnamed tuple.

examples.title: Returning exits the stream context before the test runs
Yield keeps the stream open for the requesting test

limitations: Only proven pytest/pytest-asyncio fixtures in test paths with one decorator and a direct return inside the owning with/async with are analyzed.
Recognizes built-in/io streams, tempfile TemporaryFile/NamedTemporaryFile, HTTPX Client and async-with AsyncClient; arbitrary context managers and TestClient are excluded.
Aliases, escaped/rebound resources, provider mutation, nested helpers, generator fixtures, returned snapshots and returns after the context are not inferred.
Unreachable branches and intentional closed-resource contracts are not inferred; findings are warnings requiring review.
rules.rationale: Returning a context-managed stream or HTTPX client exits its context before pytest receives the value. The requesting test receives an already closed resource instead of a usable dependency.
rules.remediation: Yield the resource inside its context so teardown follows the requesting test, updating the generator annotation as needed. If the contract deliberately supplies a closed resource, use an exact SARJ525 suppression with that reason. Review exception and cleanup behavior; no automatic rewrite is provided.
rules.summary: Yield a managed fixture resource until its requesting test finishes.

examples.title: Docstring adds a concrete constraint
Docstring only repeats the class name

limitations: Decorated or inherited classes, recognized in-file runtime docstring reads, generated files, and docstring-only class bodies are excluded.
The rule compares conservative word stems from the class name; any non-grammatical novel term keeps the docstring.
rules.rationale: A name-only restatement adds maintenance cost without documenting the class contract.
rules.remediation: Remove the restatement after confirming `__doc__` is not an external contract. Keep schema descriptions, runtime-consumed prose, hidden invariants, lifetimes, and exclusions.
rules.summary: Undecorated base-free class docstring only repeats the class name.

examples.title: Function docstring adds an atomicity guarantee
Function docstring only repeats its declaration

limitations: Safe fixes remove exact error-level name restatements only from unescaped private nested synchronous nongenerator functions, with no decorators or namespace hazards and a matching native no-consumer finding. Public/escaped functions and meaningful or ambiguous prose remain review-only. Known frame and metadata capabilities, their import aliases and metadata field access prevent fixes.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.
Decorated functions, methods on decorated or inherited classes, recognized in-file runtime docstring reads, generated files, and docstring-only bodies are excluded.
Every non-grammatical Unicode word or number must already occur in the function name, parameters, or annotations; multi-parameter prose must include a distinguishing word from every parameter.

ERROR is limited to exact ordered function-name restatements with grammatical filler and an optional terminal period; directional punctuation, reordered words and broader stem-set matches retain WARNING.
rules.rationale: Restating a clear name and signature creates maintenance work without helping callers.
rules.remediation: Remove the restatement after confirming `__doc__` is not an external contract. Clarify author-controlled names or types, and keep prose that documents constraints, side effects, or failure modes.
rules.summary: Function or plain-method docstring only repeats its declaration.
