examples.title: Delete the module's implementation walkthrough

limitations: The historical rule ID is retained for compatibility, but every unconsumed module docstring is checked, including multiline prose, tests, special modules, stubs and executable scripts.

Generated files, doctests, explicit __doc__/help/getdoc consumers and exact SARJ099 suppressions are excluded. Module consumer analysis is shared with SARJ420; when both rules are selected, SARJ099 takes diagnostic precedence.

Safe fixes delete standalone module docstrings only when SARJ420 also confirms no detected consumer. Visible dynamic namespace or frame observation, module escapes, adjacent strings, comments within the expression, same-line code and trailing comments prevent fixes.

A fix must retain source encoding and shebang interpretation. Unknown external documentation consumers require an explained local exception; classes and callable documentation remain owned by SARJ420.

Imports of __main__ or pydoc conservatively withhold module fixes because they can publish the module or its help. They do not establish that an imported __main__ is the current module, so diagnostics still require an explicit consumer proof or exception.
Legal/license notices are never automatically deleted. Keep their text as comments when removing the surrounding module docstring manually.
rules.rationale: Module prose creates a second maintenance surface; names and code structure should explain the implementation, with hidden constraints kept next to their owner.
rules.remediation: Delete the module docstring. Preserve legal notices as comments, express ordinary meaning through names and types, and move a necessary hidden constraint next to the code it governs. Keep externally consumed documentation with an explained exact-code exception.
rules.summary: Delete top-of-file module docstrings without a detected runtime or documentation consumer.

limitations: Only undecorated private module-level helpers in authored test files are considered; conftest, generated and vendor sources are excluded.
The helper has only an optional docstring and one keyword construction, no defaults, and one required bare parameter per supplied field with equivalent resolved annotations.
Only non-generic first-party Pydantic records with statically known fields, plain ancestry, and no custom methods, decorators or field aliases are proven; application modules are never imported.
Unknown calls, unpacking, escapes, reflection, rebinding, patch strings, narrower parameter types, and unresolved constructor ownership are excluded. No autofix preserves intentional seams.
rules.rationale: A forwarding helper repeats the constructor's fields and types, creating a second signature to maintain without scenario defaults or setup.

examples.title: Tests repeat incidental order setup

limitations: Only calls to the same syntactic callee that share at least seven named arguments directly inside test functions are reported.
Mapping construction, data-record helpers, mock assertions, fixtures, nested closures, generated files, and dynamic callees are allowed.
rules.rationale: Large repeated argument lists duplicate incidental setup, bury scenario differences, and make signature changes noisy within a test file.
rules.remediation: Extract a scenario helper with sensible defaults, or use a parametrized case table, and override only values relevant to each case. Suppress the finding when every argument intentionally specifies the contract, an ordered state transition, or a retry.

Assertion messages, zero-argument calls, likely mutators, mocks, snapshots, spies, comments, and intervening setup are excluded.

Common mapping accessors are excluded because repeated field assertions usually describe one cohesive object contract, not independent input cases.
Tests participating in a no-repeated-test-body group are left to SARJ066, which has the broader finding.
Case names and parameter boundaries require judgment, so the rule has no autofix.
rules.rationale: When the calls are independent, named parameters isolate failures and identify the input that failed. Literal syntax alone cannot prove independence.
rules.remediation: Consider a named pytest parameter table only when call order, shared state, fixture lifecycle, and object identity are not part of the contract; otherwise keep the assertions together or suppress the warning.
rules.summary: Three same-shape literal call assertions may be independent parameter cases.

limitations: Only authored test classes directly inheriting one resolved first-party ABC are considered; decorated classes, metaclasses, generic classes and reflective modules are excluded.

Duplicate operations must implement the same abstract member with identical resolved typed signatures and immutable literal defaults. Only bare built-in raise NotImplementedError bodies, optionally with typing.override, qualify.

Methods with messages, side effects, generator bodies, other decorators, captured defaults or super dispatch remain leaf-owned. Signatures must match the abstract contract; unresolved names are not guessed.

Visible non-call observations of abstract operations, imported namespace writes and subclass/MRO hooks exclude a contract family. String annotation references are unresolved; external or dynamic observations still require review.

One diagnostic is emitted per duplicate class, retaining the first source occurrence as the comparison owner. No autofix or dynamic mock generation; intentional independent contracts require a reasoned exception.
rules.rationale: Copied unconfigured operations add test support code and drift independently when a contract changes.
rules.remediation: Use one explicit typed strict test base for the contract. Preserve each leaf fake's configured behavior and failure timing; verify that the complete base and wiring reduce maintained code.

examples.title: Replay-named store callable omits duplicate behavior

limitations: Only SQL literals passed directly, or through a stable local binding, to execute-like calls in explicitly replay-named callables in recognized store modules are analyzed.
Dynamic SQL policy composition and ordinary create, seed, migration, schedule, and upsert methods are excluded.
Target AS aliases and OVERRIDING clauses preserve INSERT detection. Conflict detection remains lexical within one SQL statement; per-CTE ownership is not established by this embedded-SQL rule.
rules.rationale: A store callable named ensure, enqueue, record_once, get_or_create, create_if_absent, or insert_if_absent promises that a retry will not create duplicate state.
rules.remediation: Add an explicit conflict action or same-target NOT EXISTS guard. If duplicate failure or append-only insertion is deliberate, add an exact SARJ018 suppression explaining it; rename only when the callable does not promise replay safety.
rules.summary: A literal INSERT in a replay-named store callable must declare duplicate behavior.

examples.title: A token without exp is accepted
The verifier requires exp

limitations: Safe fixes require an unmutated PyJWT import, no expanded/positional options, and absent options or a static mapping with a static string require sequence. They add only exp and preserve existing option flags and claims; maximum lifetime remains a separate policy decision.
Calls resolved to PyJWT module-level `jwt.decode` or `jwt.decode_complete` are checked; `PyJWT` instances are not.
A literal `options` mapping must contain a literal `require` collection with `exp`. Non-literal options, `**` unpacking, and literal options that disable signature verification are accepted.
A verifier that enforces its own lifetime from `iat` instead still needs an exact suppression with that reason.
Tests and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: PyJWT validates `exp` only when the claim is present. A token minted without `exp` (for example by a helper whose lifetime defaults to None) passes verification forever. RFC 8725 tells verifiers to enforce the claims they rely on rather than trust the minter.
rules.remediation: Pass `options={"require": ["exp"]}` to `jwt.decode` and bound the accepted lifetime.
rules.summary: PyJWT decode calls require the exp claim.

examples.title: A fake is supplied without inheriting its nominal ABC

limitations: Only direct constructor arguments and unreassigned local constructor results supplied to a resolvable typed parameter are checked. Opaque argument escapes and receiver calls invalidate cached origins, including aliases and TypeGuard adaptation.
Structural Protocols, dynamic factories, containers, casts, unresolved or multiple owned ABC ancestry, and third-party implementations are excluded.

Contracts with virtual registration, subclass/instance hooks, custom metaclasses or decorators, escaped class values, or dynamic namespaces are excluded. Consumer constructors must have one effective direct declaration; implementation constructors, __new__, class-creation hooks, custom descriptors and unknown ancestry are excluded throughout the hierarchy.
rules.rationale: An ABC is a nominal contract: inheriting it makes its abstract operations enforceable at instantiation. Protocols intentionally use structural typing and do not require inheritance.
rules.remediation: Make the owned implementation inherit the nominal ABC expected by the consumer.
rules.summary: Require owned substitutes to inherit an injected nominal abstract contract.

from psycopg_pool import AsyncConnectionPool
async def save(pool: AsyncConnectionPool):
    async with pool.connection() as conn, conn.transaction():
        await conn.execute("SELECT id FROM items FOR UPDATE")
        await conn.execute("UPDATE items SET n = 1")

examples.title: A pool checkout alone does not retain a lock

limitations: Reports import-proven Psycopg connections and cursors from typed parameters or constructor-injected pools. Dynamic factories, interprocedural SQL, and untyped ownership are not inferred.
Inspects literal SQL, simple local/module constants, and psycopg.sql.SQL wrappers. Dynamic SQL and unsupported SQL syntax are excluded.

A locking SELECT followed by a write on the same connection outside transaction() is reported; a single statement containing a mutation is treated as atomic. Multiple writes on a reachable local path are a warning because independent writes can be intentional.

Loops, exception handlers, match statements, comprehensions, and nested closures are not analyzed as execution paths. Manual BEGIN/commit protocols are not inferred. Tests, support fixtures, and generated files are excluded.

Non-autocommit connections can already provide implicit transaction protection. A manual commit is not itself evidence of a defect or of safety in autocommit mode; document the proven connection configuration when retaining that protocol. The rule cannot prove isolation level, database constraints, or application-level atomicity; fault-injection integration tests remain necessary.
rules.rationale: Pool checkout does not start a transaction in autocommit mode. Locks can expire before use and earlier writes can survive a later failure.
rules.remediation: Enclose the complete atomic operation in the same connection's transaction() context, or use one atomic SQL statement. Document intentionally independent writes with an exact suppression.
rules.summary: Make Psycopg locking reads and related writes explicitly transactional.

examples.title: Dispatching injected work establishes a service boundary

limitations: Module-level service, store, and provider roles qualify when a public operation invokes a directly retained constructor collaborator. Classes that dispatch retained callbacks through asyncio or issue requests through locally constructed httpx clients also qualify without a role name or directory.
Resolvable inherited ABC and Protocol operations, including private and generic contracts, satisfy this policy; unresolved ancestry is not treated as a missing contract.
Generated code, tests, data values, abstract declarations, descriptors, static/class helpers, and unknown rewriting decorators are excluded.

The bounded analysis follows directly retained constructor parameters and private instance helpers; dynamic field aliases and structurally implemented Protocols declared only by external consumers are not inferred.
An unannotated bare callback factory does not by itself establish a service collaborator. Called collaborator methods and proven native callback dispatch remain in scope.

Executor dispatch requires a directly acquired or uniquely assigned asyncio event loop, or asyncio.to_thread, and an explicit callback argument. Wrapper dispatchers and ambiguous starred arguments are not inferred.

HTTP client construction and request calls require stable native imports and an unescaped local client binding. An awaited typed callback invoked with a locally constructed first-party wrapper also qualifies when its active constructor or entered lifecycle reaches a source-proven native HTTP client factory. This establishes a resource dispatch boundary; the callback's network behavior is not inferred.

First-party wrapper source may be generated, but must belong to the owning distribution or a declared workspace dependency. Unknown third-party wrappers, conditional or decorated lifecycle/helper dispatch, mere construction or cleanup without callback dispatch, mutated or escaped clients, and non-HTTP values abstain.
Method signatures are checked by the type checker. This explicit-contract policy has no automatic rewrite; preserve required framework boundaries with a reasoned exact-code exception.
rules.rationale: A one-operation service can orchestrate other services without declaring the contract that callers consume and implementations and fakes satisfy.
rules.remediation: Declare a focused ABC or Protocol covering the service operations and make that contract explicit on the implementation; reuse an existing contract instead of adding a nominal duplicate.
rules.summary: Require an explicit contract for services that invoke collaborators or perform HTTP operations.

examples.title: A module-level retry decorator backs off on the wall clock

limitations: Only calls to tenacity.retry, tenacity.Retrying, and tenacity.AsyncRetrying resolved through imports are inspected; bare @retry, positional arguments, and **kwargs expansion abstain.

A wait is reported only when it is built inline from tenacity wait_* calls, optionally combined with +; wait_none(), literal-zero wait_fixed and wait_random calls, and known zero-only wait_combine or wait_chain calls do not wait. A wait read from a name, attribute, or other call is treated as injected.
Any sleep= argument other than a wall-clock sleep imported from asyncio, anyio, trio, time, tenacity, or tenacity.nap counts as a seam; the rule does not prove that tests replace it.
The backoff library has no sleep parameter, so its decorators are not inspected. Test modules, test directories, conftest.py, test-support paths, and generated files are excluded.
rules.rationale: A tenacity policy built with a backoff wait and no sleep argument sleeps on the wall clock. Every test that exercises a transient failure pays the backoff, and exhausting an exponential policy costs the sum of every interval. Replacing tenacity's sleep from a test is a monkeypatch that SARJ445 forbids.
rules.remediation: Build the policy in a factory or constructor that accepts a sleep callable and pass it as sleep=, or accept the wait strategy itself as a dependency. Tests then inject a no-op or recording sleeper, or wait_none().
rules.summary: Pass an injectable sleep to a tenacity retry policy that waits between attempts.

limitations: Autofix only migrates private nested ordinary synchronous nongenerator helpers with no escapes, known frame or metadata capabilities, type parameters, defaults, positional-only parameters, variadics, or existing keyword-only parameters. All exact direct callers must be valid and comment-free; existing parameter names and argument evaluation order are preserved.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.

Private module functions with closed, statically resolved direct callers block as errors; public and compatibility-sensitive signatures retain advisory findings. Use distinct nominal parameter types when positional ABI must remain unchanged.
Only high-risk groups of bare `str`, `int`, or `float` annotations are reported.
Tests, generated code, migrations, conventional ordered groups, explicit inheritance, local structural protocols, and recognized routes, CLI handlers, callbacks, and runtime protocols are excluded.
External and published calling contracts cannot be proven from one file, so public and module signatures remain advisory without autofix; only proven closed private owners block.
rules.rationale: A caller can exchange semantically distinct positional values without a type-checking failure.

Classes that statically disable settings decoding through a class keyword, model_config, or Config are excluded.
Custom settings sources and indirect splitter helpers are outside the rule's scope.

examples.title: A typed factory exposes the consumer's public Protocol

limitations: This advisory uses service-family names, constructor annotations, collaborator calls, and public-method counts as heuristics.
Only direct module classes are checked; tests, generated code, scripts, framework callbacks, Store/Repository persistence dependencies, and external or interface-like bases are excluded.

A suffixless class can also qualify when it retains a locally typed factory-created collaborator driving multiple public operations and production code constructs it directly to call at least two distinct operations. Constructor aliases and explicit module imports are resolved within the bounded project index; package-export indirection, wildcard imports, duplicate module identities, variable-held instances, factory indirection, and ambiguous control flow are not inferred. Top-level functions are analyzed in indexed modules; ordinary function-only modules may be excluded by the shared type index's lexical admission.

Otherwise, a one-method, suffixless, or store-backed class requires a concrete production type dependency and a test subclass or typed mock, or at least two production consumers for a multi-method class. A port owned in another module may require an exact suppression on the implementation.

The factory-created path requires stable local runtime classes. Unknown class decorators are not inferred; proven typing final and runtime_checkable decorators preserve class identity. Definition-time defaults and decorator expressions count as enclosing runtime bindings, while nested function bodies do not.

Factory-created collaborator storage and public operations also require original method bodies; unknown method decorators are excluded while canonical typing final and override aliases remain in scope. An unrelated decorated operation does not hide two proven consumed operations.
rules.rationale: A small port can decouple consumers when they genuinely need to substitute a concrete service boundary.
rules.remediation: When a real consumer needs substitution, define a focused consumer-owned `Protocol` and type that consumer against it; otherwise suppress the advisory instead of adding an unused abstraction.
rules.summary: Consider a consumer-owned port when visible service structure suggests a substitution boundary.

examples.title: Direct partial construction keeps native argument checking
Keyword arguments escape checking
An injected partial retains its result type but loses argument checking
Factory declares its keyword contract

limitations: Private module-level functions with closed, statically resolved direct callers block as errors. Public, async, or escaped callable contracts retain advisory findings so published dynamic APIs are preserved.

Only undecorated module-level functions with proven standard Callable[..., OwnedClass] or functools.partial[OwnedClass] parameters directly called with at least one named keyword are considered. Imported classes require scanned first-party declarations; direct partial construction and calls remain native type-checker ownership.

Tests, test support, generated code, unresolved/string/generic annotations, positional-only calls, unpacking, forwarding, nested captures, rebinding and ambiguous imports are excluded. Import capture checks are conservative across the file, so an unrelated local pattern, exception or walrus binding can prevent a warning.

A fixed call demonstrates signature erasure, not a current runtime defect. Genuine dynamic APIs can use a reasoned suppression. No autofix: the correct contract depends on whether classes or function factories are intended.
rules.rationale: Callable[..., T] and functools.partial[T] erase argument checking at injected boundaries, so misspelled keywords and incompatible factories pass strict typing and can fail at runtime.
rules.remediation: If factory substitution is unnecessary, call the existing constructor directly. Otherwise reuse an existing precise callable contract; use type[T] when the dependency requires a class, accounting for subclass constructor compatibility. Introduce a callable Protocol only when a substitutable keyword factory actually needs a new contract; preserve the accepted keyword names instead of replacing them with unchecked **kwargs.
rules.summary: Keep fixed keyword factory calls behind a precise callable signature.

limitations: Requires a resolved direct public ABC or Protocol base with multiple owned implementations explicitly covering its public operations.

Private consumer-owned Protocols, unresolved bases, indirect inheritance, single implementations, data-only dependencies, tests, and generated files are excluded.

ERROR requires identical resolved signatures for every used operation, including return type, accepted inputs, parameter kinds, names and literal defaults. Generic/decorated classes, descriptor methods and unresolved or variant signatures retain WARNING; preserve concrete postconditions and accepted-input variance before widening an annotation.
rules.rationale: A concrete dependency annotation obstructs substitution even when an existing public contract already has multiple implementations.
rules.remediation: Annotate the dependency with the existing public contract; do not create a new interface.

limitations: The rule follows import-proven JSON decoders, requests/httpx/aiohttp responses and clients, environment or subprocess results, and simple module-local helpers through single-assignment names.

Simple same-module wrappers preserve constructor arguments through direct stored-field accessor methods, including local identity-or-empty-dict narrowing helpers; inheritance, decorators, mutation, nested captures, unknown member escapes, and unknown helpers are excluded.

Synchronous module factories preserve direct wrapper returns, single-assignment local aliases, and required positional or keyword parameters substituted from proven call-site inputs. Defaults, variadics, branches, unknown effects or transforms, async/method/decorated factories, captures, and factory chains are excluded; annotations alone do not establish factory provenance.
It diagnoses literal-key subscription and get calls; iteration and other dynamic JSON use remain out of scope.
Unannotated parameters and unknown expressions are not assumed to be external; interprocedural and framework-specific boundaries can remain unreported.

Names bound by loops, comprehensions, context managers, exception handlers, pattern matching, imports, or destructuring are excluded when their provenance is ambiguous; unrelated binders do not suppress the rest of a function.
Repository-local JSON, json.load file handles, tests, generated files, and documentation examples are excluded.
rules.rationale: Annotations, casts, and partial key checks do not validate a wire protocol; a maintained runtime schema makes required fields, types, and protocol versions explicit at the boundary.
rules.remediation: Validate raw JSON with `Model.model_validate_json(...)`; use a named RootModel for scalar or collection roots. For an already-decoded response, use `model_validate` or another maintained runtime schema validator before reading fields.

examples.title: A match statement parses an opaque field by hand

limitations: Checks literal-string get/subscript reads on parameters or local names annotated as standard string mappings with object, Any or pydantic.JsonValue values. Stable module type aliases, quoted annotations, wrappers and local value aliases are recognized with bounded resolution.

A field must feed builtin isinstance/type checks, literal comparisons, truth tests or a constrained match pattern. Ordinary reads/forwarding, dynamic keys, homogeneous typed maps, imported application aliases, attributes and ambiguous/rebound assignments are excluded.

Import-resolved Pydantic before/wrap decorators with literal or stable local mode aliases, metadata validators and registered Discriminator callbacks own raw normalization. Stable function aliases, functools.partial binding only keyword-only configuration and simple bound/static/class methods are recognized. Prefer declarative fields before introducing callbacks.

Callback classes must be stable direct local declarations with no bases, class options, custom constructor or descriptor hooks. Import-proven typing.final and empty __slots__ preserve ownership. Other decorators, imported/inherited classes and directly mutated callback owners abstain. Nonescaping direct local helpers inherit raw ownership; escaped helpers remain checked. Generic type parameters shadow matching builtin/import annotation names.

Parsing helpers in authored tests are checked, but assert-contained test oracles are excluded. Generated/vendor sources and dynamic namespaces are excluded. This is a warning with no automatic rewrite because coercion, missing-field handling and error policy can differ.
rules.rationale: Fixed-key reads followed by runtime type, shape, or discriminator checks spread a record contract across control flow. An object/Any/JsonValue mapping does not declare those field contracts.
rules.remediation: Parse the raw object with a named Pydantic BaseModel or RootModel before using typed attributes. Prefer strict fields, Field bounds, aliases/AliasPath and discriminated unions to handwritten probes. For an already trusted internal record, declare a precise named record such as TypedDict instead of parsing it again. Preserve rejection, defaults and fail-closed behavior explicitly; bool is an int subclass.
rules.summary: Declare opaque mapping field shapes in Pydantic instead of probing them by hand.

A route reads a fixed key from a nested request mapping

limitations: Tests, generated sources, dynamic-key access, and non-FastAPI functions are excluded.

limitations: Only direct, import-proven Pydantic BaseModel fields with a literal default and an unqualified `N for the first ...` clause at the start of a description or parenthetical clause are inspected.
Descriptions that mention a smaller numeric value or explicit sentinel and exception language are skipped because the ordinal origin may not be the field minimum.
Import-proven field or model validators cause conservative abstention; their bodies are not interpreted.
Unknown named aliases, indirect model subclasses, nested container constraints, tests, and generated files are out of scope.

ERROR requires one direct BaseModel base, no class decorators or keywords, and an inert field/docstring/pass body. Descriptors, methods, configuration, mixed bases and computed field values retain WARNING because class-creation effects can change validation.
rules.rationale: An unqualified `N for the first ...` mapping defines the origin of an ordinal field; matching schema metadata keeps runtime validation and generated JSON Schema aligned with that public contract.
rules.remediation: Use `PositiveInt` for a 1-based ordinal, `NonNegativeInt` for a 0-based ordinal, or encode the origin with `Field(ge=N)` or equivalent top-level `Annotated` metadata.

limitations: Only module-level test* functions and methods of base-free, constructor-free Test* classes in recognized test files are checked; import-proven pytest marks are allowed, while other decorators abstain.
Structured, protected, value-bearing, generated, runtime-consumed, and lexically non-restating docstrings are preserved; semantic paraphrases are not inferred.
Literal or ambiguous __test__ opt-outs are excluded; repository-specific pytest collection-name overrides are not inferred.
rules.rationale: A docstring that narrates visible test code creates duplicate prose that can drift without explaining the regression or contract.
rules.remediation: Delete only the restatement and put the scenario and expected outcome in the test name. Keep concise non-obvious regression, constraint, or contract context in the docstring or a local comment.
rules.summary: Collected test docstring only repeats names and visible code.

limitations: Only direct module-level BaseModel subclasses without configuration or methods and public annotated Field declarations are inspected.
Factories must be zero-argument lambdas or undecorated module functions containing one return, optionally after a docstring.
Captured values require unique, acyclic module bindings to built-in mutable containers or direct unconfigured BaseModel instances.
Rebound names, shadowed imports, inherited or configured models, unknown services, nested scopes, and generated files are excluded.
Fields enabling default validation or supplying unknown keyword options are excluded because validation may copy or transform the factory result.
Factories producing new values, explicit copies, or values derived from validated data are excluded; intentional sharing needs a local suppression.

ERROR requires an inert body of plain field declarations, literal values, docstrings and pass statements. Descriptors, computed members and other class-creation effects retain WARNING because they can replace the source factory.

Generated files, tests, `__main__.py`, mutual recursion, and helpers with multiple callers are excluded.
Decorated definitions and dynamic references that cannot prove a sole caller are not reported.
Only lexically resolved builtin classmethod/staticmethod decorators are transparent; other decorators and executable statements are movement barriers.
Only direct calls and nonescaping local callable aliases establish callers; escaped values and ambiguous receivers are excluded.
rules.rationale: Caller-first ordering keeps the module's public flow visible before its implementation details.
rules.remediation: Move the private helper below its sole caller without changing either body.
rules.summary: A private helper used by one caller should be defined below that caller.

examples.title: Keep an update with a distinct concurrency contract

limitations: Only a single literal PostgreSQL UPDATE on the same table as a literal upsert is checked, with equality predicates exactly matching the conflict key and direct bound-value assignments already covered by EXCLUDED field assignments.

The command's fields must resolve from a source-declared class and flow directly into one INSERT VALUES row through literal positional or named parameters. Shadowed annotations, explicit descriptors and class keywords do not prove writable fields. The setter and upsert must declare the same result type, RETURNING projection and updated_at policy. SQL composition, inherited fields, dynamic commands, conditional or transformed upserts, unknown decorators, Python branching, arithmetic, joins, CTEs and multiple statements are excluded.

The finding is a consolidation review, not proof that INSERT ON CONFLICT preserves update-only behavior. A missing row must not be created accidentally; omitted fields must not be overwritten by defaults.

Context-manager behavior and other surrounding effects are not proven equivalent. Share ordinary write implementation behind existing authorization or transaction wrappers while preserving those contracts.
Generated and test sources are excluded. There is no automatic replacement and no requirement to expose immutable or privileged model fields.
rules.rationale: Independent per-field SQL methods duplicate write policy and can drift from the existing model command's validation, conflict handling and timestamps.
rules.remediation: Prefer one typed model command for ordinary writable fields. Reuse or extend its write implementation while preserving update-only, missing-row, omission/null, authorization and concurrency contracts; retain domain transitions as separate operations.
rules.summary: A plain field UPDATE duplicates fields already writable through the store's upsert command.

examples.title: Do not maintain a second singleton query path
Do not maintain a second singleton mutation path
Delegate the singleton read to the bulk implementation
Route singleton mutations through the bulk primitive

limitations: Concrete wrappers declared with a canonical bulk method in a production Store class are inspected; the canonical method may be abstract.
Reads retain the strict get/get_many contract. Writes require a typed collection key, compatible context and result types, and a recognizable many-method name.
The canonical write topology is the exact set_many_to_status(..., status) shape, with wrappers binding the matching status enum member.

A source-declared upsert/upsert_many pair with one matching typed model input and scalar/collection result also shares one canonical write implementation. Preserve conflict, tenant, null/omission and missing-row behavior; implement a real batch primitive before delegating to avoid recursion.
Wrappers with try/finally or other unsupported compound control flow are not diagnosed.
Singleton implementations with explicit cache or lock identifiers are excluded because their access path differs intentionally.
Signature compatibility is advisory: dynamic helpers and behavior not visible in the two method bodies require review.
Closed literal starred collection expansions preserve singleton delegation; unknown iterable expansion or additional keys do not prove the singleton contract.
Straight-line command and singleton-collection aliases preserve delegation; reassigned inputs and unsupported alias mutations do not prove that the original command reaches the bulk primitive.
rules.rationale: Independent singleton and bulk queries can drift in filtering, mutation semantics, row conversion, authorization, timestamps, and missing-row behavior while maintaining two database access paths.
rules.remediation: Delegate only when tenant, authorization, consistency, cache, lock, transaction, conversion, and missing-row semantics match. Otherwise add an exact SARJ421 suppression naming the concrete semantic difference.
rules.summary: A store singleton operation should reuse its equivalent bulk implementation.

examples.title: A fixture declares its duplicate behavior
Fixture inserts need an explicit duplicate decision

limitations: Checks recovered INSERT statements reaching import-proven Psycopg execution in recognized store modules or class-owned persistence helpers, including test fixtures and direct same-class forwarding wrappers. Generated Python and unknown or dynamically composed SQL abstain.

Any explicit PostgreSQL ON CONFLICT clause declares a policy. This rule does not prove its target, concurrency correctness, replay behavior or side effects. SELECT-side existence checks alone do not establish a concurrency-safe duplicate policy.
Plain INSERT remains a review finding when Python handles UniqueViolation or a fixture comment states invalid-row intent; preserve those contracts with an explained exact exception.
Replay-named store INSERT findings already owned by SARJ018 take precedence. This broader policy remains a warning and requires an explained exact exception for intentional database-error fixtures.
rules.rationale: A visible SQL conflict policy makes retry and fixture behavior reviewable at the write boundary. Plain INSERT can intentionally reject duplicates; record that contract with an exact rule exception.
rules.remediation: Declare the intended ON CONFLICT behavior, or add an exact SARJ547 exception explaining why duplicate rejection, append-only insertion, or deliberately invalid fixture data is required. Preserve uniqueness, errors, return shape and transaction behavior; DO NOTHING is not an automatic replacement.
rules.summary: Declare SQL conflict behavior for store INSERT statements, including fixture writes.

examples.title: Different relation ownership is preserved

limitations: This is API consolidation advice, not proof that writes are equivalent. Checks non-test store modules with an upsert-named command reaching an INSERT and a set_-named direct UPDATE of the same exactly qualified relation. A bounded direct same-class helper call can establish that INSERT target; the command name does not prove conflict handling. Dynamic SQL, inherited upserts, unknown owners and unrelated relations abstain.

Also reviews source-visible abstract set_ methods declared beside an abstract upsert in a store interface. The explicit setter API spelling triggers this interface policy; it does not prove the method is redundant or identify its implementation.

The precise ordinary-field duplication owner SARJ517 takes precedence at the same method. Guarded and multi-statement operations can still be reported for review, but their transaction and concurrency contracts must be retained. One diagnostic is emitted per method, with no automatic edit.
rules.rationale: Per-field mutation entry points beside a model upsert can scatter write validation and concurrency policy. A smaller typed command surface makes those contracts easier to review together.
rules.remediation: Review whether these methods can share a typed mutation command or internal write implementation. Preserve update-only and missing-row behavior, authorization, omission versus null, and guarded transitions. Do not replace a conditional UPDATE with an insert-capable upsert; model distinct transitions explicitly when they must stay separate.
rules.summary: Review per-field store mutations beside an existing model write command.

examples.title: Drain and wait after killing
Killing does not complete cleanup

limitations: Requires a unique, dominating local subprocess.Popen assignment and a resolved TimeoutExpired handler ending with a direct kill() after that process's wait or communicate.
Borrowed processes, custom factories, context-managed ownership, aliases, escaped handles or cleanup callbacks, and any later wait/communicate/poll are excluded conservatively.

Only direct timeout handlers are checked. Cross-function lifecycle, fields, dynamic mutation, arbitrary exit paths, and generated files are not analyzed. Choosing wait versus communicate requires reviewing output ownership.
Visible os child-reaper imports/calls and SIGCHLD ownership exclude the file. Later internal Popen cleanup helpers are recognized conservatively, without recommending private APIs.
Visible namespace APIs, frame/module introspection, code mutation and bound attribute setters invalidate the file's provenance proof.
rules.rationale: Sending a kill signal does not wait for process termination or collect the exit status; deterministic cleanup still requires waiting or communication.
rules.remediation: After kill(), call communicate() when owning captured pipes, or wait() when output is handled separately; an enclosing Popen context manager can also own cleanup.
rules.summary: Reap a locally owned subprocess after killing it on timeout.

examples.title: A store query orders only by a timestamp

limitations: Only fully reconstructable SQL string literals in recognized production store modules are analyzed.

The rule reports an exact, optionally qualified unquoted `*_at` column only when it is the final same-depth `ORDER BY` item before LIMIT, OFFSET, or FETCH, or when only a volatile/constant pseudo-key follows. Uniqueness is not schema-proven.
Dynamic string construction, formatted strings, quoted identifiers, expressions containing a timestamp column, and non-SELECT fragments are excluded.
The intended stable key cannot be inferred safely, so the rule does not offer an autofix.
Grouped, DISTINCT, WITH TIES, unbounded, window-only, aggregate-only, and docstring SQL are excluded.
A scalar query that projects only the exact timestamp ordering expression is excluded because equal-timestamp rows produce the same observable value.
rules.rationale: Timestamp columns are not necessarily unique, so bounded reads can choose different rows at a page or top-N boundary. Keyset pagination also needs the same secondary key in its cursor predicate.
rules.remediation: Add a deterministic unique key after the timestamp. For keyset pagination, include the key in both the ORDER BY tuple and cursor predicate, such as `(created_at, id) < (%s, %s)`.
rules.summary: Bounded store SQL whose final result-order key looks like a `*_at` timestamp should include a deterministic secondary key.

This warning requests manual review; joining strings does not prove a finite reason domain, so contextual string lists may also match and must not automatically become enums.

limitations: Safe fixes inline proven invariant bool/None values only in closed private nested synchronous nongenerator test factories without nested closure scopes, and remove the unannotated keyword-only option plus inert literal caller keywords. Module factories, annotations, type parameters, comments, reflection, dynamic calls, callable defaults and other values remain review-only. Known frame and metadata capabilities, their import aliases and metadata field access prevent fixes.

Containing callables must also be ordinary synchronous nongenerators with proven inert execution; unknown callouts, properties, overloads, reachable frame-exporting exceptions, and helper references crossing additional function, class, lambda, or comprehension scopes prevent fixes.

Invariant bool and None options are ERROR when the closed caller proof succeeds and the file has no visible namespace access. Other literals and callable defaults remain WARNING because identity and default binding timing may differ.

Literal findings consider private module-level helpers or _make_ and _build_ helpers nested directly inside test functions, with at least two known direct callers and straight-line construction bodies.

Callable findings consider module-level private helpers with the same construction shape and an earlier undecorated local function default, only when at least two known direct callers all omit that option.

Conftest module-level factories, explicit callable arguments, exports, decorators, escaping references, reflection, unpacking, rebinding, shadowing and ambiguous mutation or patch targets are excluded.
Same-name declarations elsewhere in the file conservatively exclude a helper. Advisory findings retain their customization contract for review.

Callable findings describe known callers in this file; cross-module and dynamic callers are not inferred. Retain intentional extension points with a reasoned exception, preserving definition-time default capture.
rules.rationale: Unused customization obscures the values that actually distinguish test scenarios.
rules.remediation: Consider keeping the invariant literal or stable local callable in the construction instead of exposing an unexercised option. Preserve intentional dependency contracts and callable default binding timing.
rules.summary: A private test factory exposes an invariant literal or unexercised local callable option.

limitations: Only authored PostgreSQL migrations are checked; dumps, generator-owned migrations, fixtures, and test sources are excluded.

Keep deployment checkpoints and operations whose ordering, expression evaluation, or lock contracts differ in separate statements.

examples.title: An excess index records its application query and plan evidence

limitations: Only authored production migrations are checked; tests, dumps, fixtures, and recognized generator-owned migrations are excluded.

Index declarations inside dollar-quoted stored or anonymous program bodies are not inferred.
The policy budgets distinct explicit index definitions in one file; it does not dereference query or EXPLAIN links, estimate workload selectivity, or reconstruct fleet-wide index state.
rules.rationale: Every explicit index adds write amplification, storage, vacuum work, and planner surface; bursts of indexes often encode unmeasured read paths in the transactional database.
rules.remediation: Keep at most three explicit indexes per table and eight per migration, or place an exact `index-justification: app-read: ...; query: path#symbol; explain: URL` or `index-justification: referential-action: ...` comment immediately above each excess index. For `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` only, `index-justification: uniqueness-constraint: ...; ticket: ABC-123` is also accepted. Do not add reporting-specific indexes without evaluating ClickHouse for reporting, historical analysis, and broad aggregations.
rules.summary: Require a structured local justification for excess explicit indexes in an authored migration.

examples.title: Constraint validated while it is added

limitations: Only PostgreSQL migration files and ALTER TABLE actions that directly add CHECK or foreign-key constraints are inspected.
Foreign keys may use the referenced table's implicit primary key; NOT VALID and NOT ENFORCED constraints do not require deferred validation advice.
A table is treated as fresh only after an unconditional empty CREATE TABLE in the same migration section; ambiguous or populating statements revoke that exemption.

Migration sections, executing table or materialized-view creation, extensions, and existing-table column rewrites revoke earlier empty-table proofs. Relation-resolution settings revoke unqualified proofs while preserving explicit schema identity; nonexecuting DDL retains them.
Validation transactions are not inferred; the diagnostic explains that VALIDATE CONSTRAINT belongs in a later committed migration or transaction.
rules.rationale: Validating a CHECK or foreign key while adding it scans existing rows while PostgreSQL holds locks that can block writes to the altered table and, for a foreign key, the referenced table.
rules.remediation: Add the constraint with NOT VALID and commit that migration or transaction. Validate it in a later committed migration or transaction so the lower-lock validation scan does not inherit the ADD lock.
rules.summary: CHECK and foreign-key constraints added to existing PostgreSQL tables should defer validation.

examples.title: A concurrent index build cannot execute in the runner's transaction

limitations: Only authored PostgreSQL migrations are checked; tests, fixtures, dumps and recognized generator-owned migrations are excluded.

Transaction proof comes from explicit BEGIN/START TRANSACTION or a valid dbmate up/down directive. COMMIT/END/ROLLBACK/ABORT, AND [NO] CHAIN and section boundaries are tracked; ROLLBACK TO a savepoint keeps the transaction active. Unknown caller transactions and other migration runners are not inferred.

Only parseable CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY statements and complete DROP INDEX or REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW command forms are inspected. Dollar-quoted procedural and scalar bodies are ignored; SQL-standard BEGIN ATOMIC routine bodies cause file-level abstention. Dynamic SQL, REINDEX and external catalog restrictions are not inferred.
One finding per command combines all demonstrated restrictions. No automatic transaction or DDL rewrite is safe.
rules.rationale: PostgreSQL rejects concurrent index creation and removal inside a transaction block. Concurrent index removal also rejects multiple targets and CASCADE, and a concurrent materialized-view refresh cannot request WITH NO DATA.
rules.remediation: Run concurrent index commands outside a transaction, using transaction:false for the relevant dbmate section. Drop one index per concurrent command without CASCADE. Choose either a concurrent populated refresh or a nonconcurrent WITH NO DATA refresh. Preserve deployment and atomicity requirements when changing transaction boundaries.
rules.summary: Keep concurrent PostgreSQL DDL in supported execution contexts.

The rule does not infer table contents, installed operator classes, function volatility, referenced constraints, partition keys, or deployment transaction boundaries. It does not rewrite DDL.
rules.rationale: Unsupported index options and constraint validation clauses fail when PostgreSQL executes a migration. These incompatibilities follow directly from the command and known built-in access-method capabilities.
rules.remediation: Use B-tree for a unique index; use a supported multicolumn method for multiple keys; list only column names in INCLUDE; qualify the indexed table instead of the new index name; and omit NOT VALID from UNIQUE or PRIMARY KEY additions. Preserve the intended uniqueness and query-access contract.

Dollar-quoted procedure and anonymous-block bodies and dynamically executed SQL are intentionally ignored.

A single header `sarj-migration-atomicity` comment may record complete lock, runtime, rollback, and postcondition evidence. This is an auditable human-reviewed declaration, not proof that the evidence is accurate.

rules.remediation: Split expand, backfill, enforcement, and contract work into independently deployable migrations, or document why atomic execution is required together with lock, runtime, rollback, and postcondition evidence.

rules.remediation: Move reporting queries to ClickHouse or another analytical database with an explicit freshness contract. Use EXISTS or indexed row lookups for operational reads. Preserve atomicity; a reviewed transactional invariant needs an exact, explained SARJ122 exception.

Semantically equivalent expressions with different normalized source spelling are intentionally not inferred.
Left-prefix review is limited to ordinary non-unique B-tree indexes with identical physical options and compatible INCLUDE coverage.
Only exact normalized active duplicates block; unique/nonunique access-path comparisons and strict left-prefix advice retain WARNING because query-plan value is unresolved.
rules.rationale: Duplicate definitions, non-unique copies of unique access paths, and strict B-tree prefixes can add write amplification, storage, vacuum work, and planner choices without a distinct measured read path.
rules.remediation: Remove the repeated definition or verify the exact query plan before retaining a potentially covered index. Preserve an index when uniqueness, key order, operator class, collation, predicate, included columns, partition scope, access method, tablespace, or storage parameters give it distinct behavior.
rules.summary: Report duplicate and conservatively covered indexes that remain active in one authored migration.

limitations: Safe fixes remove standalone line-comment banners and complete supported disabled SQL-only comment runs. Debt, references, directives, rollback guidance, mixed prose and block comments remain for review.
Only authored migration files are checked; dumps and generator-owned migrations are excluded.
The scanner distinguishes SQL comments from strings, identifiers, templates, and executable dollar-quoted bodies.
Commented-out SQL is reported only for a conservative complete-statement grammar; ambiguous prose and partial statements are preserved.
Migration-tool directives, explicit rollback instructions, and debt with a durable URL or issue identifier are preserved.
rules.rationale: Disabled statements drift while version control preserves their history, decorative dividers obscure migration structure, and debt without a durable owner silently persists.

examples.title: Use predicates with explicit null semantics

files.source: SELECT id FROM event WHERE archived_at = NULL;

examples.title: Ordinary equality does not test for missing values

limitations: Checks parsed authored PostgreSQL SQL, including queries and migrations. Dumps, generated files, tests, fixtures, explicit other dialects, unsupported statements and malformed SQL are excluded.
Only bare NULL and parenthesized NULL operands are checked. Casts, computed null values, subquery nullability and row-valued NOT IN lists are not inferred.

The rule recommends explicit predicates even when transform_null_equals is enabled. Catalog-defined non-strict comparison operators and intentional three-valued boolean results require an exact suppression; no automatic rewrite guesses their contract.
rules.rationale: Ordinary built-in comparisons with NULL produce unknown, so a WHERE or JOIN predicate does not match rows. A scalar NOT IN list containing NULL can never be true. These expressions often silently discard the rows the query intended to retain.
rules.remediation: Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL to test for missing values, and IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM for null-safe equality. Remove a literal NULL from a NOT IN list and express the intended null handling separately.
rules.summary: Use explicit NULL predicates instead of ordinary NULL comparisons.

examples.title: Pagination bounded by a stable cursor

files.source: SELECT created_at, id FROM event ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2;

examples.title: Pagination that scans skipped rows

limitations: Only dynamic driver markers in credible SELECT statements are reported; fixed ordinal offsets are preserved.
PostgreSQL, SQLite, and common Python driver markers are recognized, including a postfix cast inside a parenthesized dynamic offset and MySQL LIMIT offset,count syntax.

Parenthesized numeric arithmetic and common numeric wrappers preserve dynamic-offset detection. Casts on later arithmetic operands, quoted/multiword type names and arbitrary function bodies remain unresolved.
Dumps, migrations, generated paths or marked files, tests, fixtures, snapshots, ORM calls, bare procedural variables, and ambiguous templates are excluded.
rules.rationale: A parameterized offset grows with the requested page, forcing the database to scan and discard earlier rows. Concurrent inserts or deletes can also shift page boundaries, repeating or skipping rows.
rules.remediation: Use keyset pagination over a stable, immutable ordering. Match the cursor predicate to the ORDER BY direction and add a unique tie-breaker. Keep dynamic OFFSET only for an intentional random-access contract or demonstrably bounded/static data, with an exact SARJ107 suppression.
rules.summary: Dynamic OFFSET pagination in query SQL should use a stable cursor.

limitations: Automatic literal fixes require one literal-only SELECT or one simple CREATE TABLE with canonical typed literal defaults, with no other statements, reads, CTEs, operators, other constraints, custom casts or callouts. The external PostgreSQL built-in catalog must be canonical and unmodified; source-visible mutations are refused.

Autofix only corrects a canonical pg_catalog.json cast of the exact ordinary ASCII literal '{}' or '[]' inside an existing direct pg_catalog.jsonb cast and a canonical JSONB column DEFAULT. The outer JSONB boundary already owns normalization; schema types, other JSON documents, data expressions and missing boundaries remain manual.
PostgreSQL dump files are excluded.
JSON tokens inside comments, string literals, and longer identifiers are ignored.
Column declarations include optional COLUMN keywords, JSON arrays, and exact quoted or pg_catalog-qualified built-ins. Case-sensitive quoted custom types and other schemas remain excluded.
Query and data-migration casts are excluded because an external or legacy JSON column may require them.
rules.rationale: JSONB supports indexing and containment operators and avoids reparsing the stored document on every read.
rules.remediation: Declare JSONB columns and use jsonb casts for JSON document values.

limitations: Automatic literal fixes require one literal-only SELECT or one simple CREATE TABLE with canonical typed literal defaults, with no other statements, reads, CTEs, operators, other constraints, custom casts or callouts. The external PostgreSQL built-in catalog must be canonical and unmodified; source-visible mutations are refused.

Autofix only replaces an exact short ordinary ASCII literal's canonical pg_catalog.varchar(n) cast when an existing direct pg_catalog.text cast already owns its result. Positive valid bounds must preserve every input character; columns, overlength strings, custom types, escaped literals and absent outer text boundaries remain manual.
MySQL and SQLite sources are excluded because their VARCHAR behavior differs.

Complete parseable PostgreSQL statements distinguish bounded builtin types from function names and custom schema types, including exact lower-case quoted varchar and pg_catalog qualification. Fragments and unsupported procedural syntax retain unquoted lexical detection.
rules.rationale: PostgreSQL gives VARCHAR(n) no storage or performance advantage, while its length cap obscures a business constraint.
rules.remediation: Use TEXT and express a real maximum length with an explicit CHECK constraint when needed.
rules.summary: VARCHAR(n) — use TEXT (+ CHECK length if needed).

limitations: Only CASCADE, SET NULL, and SET DEFAULT actions are checked; ordinary NO ACTION/RESTRICT foreign keys stay silent.
Explicit schemas and quoted identifier case remain distinct; mixed qualification is unresolved and may refer to the same relation.
Literal FALSE partial indexes cannot cover foreign keys. Other partial predicates retain conservative legacy coverage; arbitrary implication and migration-time index drops are not evaluated.

A bounded scan includes indexes from sibling files in the same migration tree.

examples.title: Keep Cloud Run infrastructure in Terraform

limitations: Terraform coverage extracts literal strings and heredocs owned by resource local-exec.command with the default interpreter or a literal POSIX shell -c interpreter; HCL templates, computed commands, custom interpreters, remote-exec, and Terraform JSON are intentionally unreported.
A Terraform diagnostic can be suppressed locally with an exact-code # sarj-noqa: SARJ309 comment on the preceding physical line.
The bounded scanner reports explicitly recognized commands and deployment Actions; dynamic command construction and unlisted provider surfaces are intentionally unreported.
Multiline quoted shell data is excluded and command substitutions are not evaluated; function bodies are checked for possible mutations without proving invocation.

Literal argv execution fields in supported operational configurations, including Cloud Build entrypoint plus args, preserve the command boundary. Image-default entrypoints and non-executable configuration data are not inferred.
Wrapper-indirected commands are intentionally unreported; full-tree CI scans wrapper files directly only when they live in an operational root.
Wrangler deploy and versions deploy publish application artifacts and are intentionally not treated as infrastructure mutation; Wrangler resource-creation commands remain reportable.
Cloud Run image/source-only deploys and updates publish application artifacts; configuration, identity, scaling, networking, secret, and other infrastructure flags remain reportable.
kubectl set image publishes application artifacts; other set commands and infrastructure mutations remain reportable.
Read-only diagnostics such as terraform show, gcloud describe/list, and kubectl get are allowed.
Structured configuration keys are not mutation evidence; deployment authorization policies such as plan-address allowlists remain allowed.
rules.rationale: Imperative control-plane commands split deployment ownership between Terraform and repository-specific orchestration, so drift and safety depend on execution order. Publishing an application artifact is a release operation and remains outside this rule.
rules.remediation: Model the resource, identity, and lifecycle in Terraform; let CI select inputs and apply the saved plan without maintaining a second mutation path.
rules.summary: recognized control-plane commands bypass Terraform resource ownership

Shell comments and quoted-delimiter heredoc data are excluded. SQL keyword context is lexical, not proof of an execution sink; keywords embedded in path/name tokens are ignored.
rules.rationale: Slash-command arguments are user-controlled. Embedding them into a shell token or query string can change command structure or query semantics when the documented command is executed.
rules.remediation: Pass the argument as its own quoted shell token to a wrapper that validates or parameterizes it; never splice it into SQL, LogQL, or another query string.
rules.summary: raw Claude command argument interpolated into an executable shell or query fence

limitations: Requires a file immediately inside .github/workflows, an official Slack action consuming a same-job step output, and a direct pull-request title/head-ref environment binding.

Recognizes scalar, list or mapping trigger selectors using pull_request, pull_request_target, workflow_call, push and workflow_dispatch; at least one PR-capable trigger is required. Unknown, missing and review-event selectors abstain. A reusable workflow may inherit a PR caller; caller graphs are not modeled.

Literal false and whole github.event_name equality/inequality guards filter job, producer and consumer events. Other conditions are admitted only with PR-only remaining event possibilities; unresolved mixed-event guards abstain. General condition satisfiability is not modeled.

Prior inline shell references to GITHUB_ENV invalidate inherited workflow/job environment bindings; explicit producer-step bindings remain eligible. Dynamic aliases, external builders in prior steps, and action-managed environment mutations are not modeled.

Recognizes one jq constructor assignment and one unchanged printf to GITHUB_OUTPUT, optionally preceded by set -euo pipefail. Unknown shell commands, jq transformations, aliases, payload-file transport and custom Slack clients abstain.

Checks Block Kit section text and section fields. Header text only accepts plain_text and is not a mrkdwn sink. JSON serialization alone is not a Slack escape. This concerns reserved entity/link/mention controls; it does not claim to sanitize every formatting delimiter.
An external builder must be a literal argument-free bash/sh invocation, bounded to the same checkout. Only selected workflows are analyzed; selecting a builder alone does not discover its callers.
rules.rationale: JSON quoting does not neutralize Slack markup controls in pull-request titles or branch names.
rules.remediation: Use plain_text for event-controlled text, or deliberately encode reserved Slack controls before combining it with trusted markup.
rules.summary: Keep proven event-controlled text out of Slack markup controls.

examples.title: Invoke an external program with quoted arguments

limitations: Only semantic execution fields are analyzed: Actions/composite steps, Cloud Build steps, Skaffold hooks and containers, Kubernetes containers/probes/hooks, Compose commands, mise tasks, Docker instructions and Make recipe units.
Compose healthchecks disabled by a constant native boolean value are inert; unresolved disable interpolation fails analysis coverage.

Inline interpreter source, jq/awk filters, shell control flow, logical chains, pipelines and command substitutions are rejected regardless of program size. Sequential direct invocations, external files/modules and recursively verified shell wrappers are allowed; every invocation is checked.

Unknown external-image ENTRYPOINT defaults and dynamic executable identities are not inferred; runtime CMD is analyzed only when its entrypoint ownership is proven. Unsupported selected interpreter option grammars or unprovable shell payloads fail analysis coverage instead of passing silently.
Literal dumb-init child forwarding is verified against its upstream source; signal-rewrite and ambiguous option forms fail analysis coverage.
Make target/pattern variables and prerequisite inheritance require statically provable names; conflicting pattern values with version-dependent precedence fail analysis coverage.

Explicit stdin ownership is native-proven for Bash. Command-string selection after options is native-proven for Bash, sh, dash, zsh and ksh; zsh/ksh retain their existing option namespaces. Ambiguous command/value clusters and unproven uppercase-O forms fail coverage.
Each ordinary Make logical recipe is a separate execution block; .ONESHELL groups contiguous recipe lines. YAML aliases are reported at each executable use site.
rules.rationale: Programs embedded in deployment and build configuration bypass the normal language lint, type and local test boundaries. Simple sequences of existing commands are orchestration; executable logic belongs under the normal language tooling.
rules.remediation: Reuse existing native commands or workflow steps. Keep control flow and inline interpreter source in maintained, linted repository code; avoid wrapper scripts solely to rearrange commands.
rules.summary: DevOps execution block embeds program logic
